p: In “Saving a Nation,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the whole Bible, Old Testament included, was written for our learning, and uses Judges 17–18 (Micah, the tribe of Dan and the people of Laish) to picture a land where everyone does what is right in his own eyes. He says the church must stop living careless and self-confident, speak the Word of God in public, and unite over Bible morality. He also speaks about politics, entitlements, scientism and several controversial moral issues, and says the turning of a nation starts with the church.
Is the Old Testament still for us today?

He says everything written in the Bible was written for us to learn by, so the Old Testament Scriptures are very important to us. When God dealt with a nation, or a nation fell, we need to learn why and how to turn it around. He says the Old Testament events “occurred” and were not myths, and that “All Scripture” is profitable, with righteousness and good works as the focus of the Bible.
Is the Old Testament still for us today?

Everything written in the Bible was written for us to learn by. So Old Testament Scriptures are very important to us. All the Scriptures are important to us. And to remind you of this, Romans 15:4 says, “Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we, through patience and comfort of the Scriptures, might have hope.” So everything in the Bible is for us to go back and learn by. When God dealt with a nation, or a nation fell, or whatever, we need to learn why they did that and how to turn it around. 1 Corinthians 10:11 says, “All these things happened.” Now, not like Bill O’Reilly on Fox News, who says these were allegories, fictitious stories, myths, okay? That’s what Schuler [unclear] also taught, that the Bible was just a bunch of allegories and myths. But it says here, all these things, what? They occurred, okay? They weren’t myths, they weren’t dreams, they weren’t fantasies. They were actually things that occurred to them for examples, and written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the earth are come. And we know that the end of the world started when Jesus died on the cross and ascended back into heaven and started his church. We’re in the last days of God’s calendar. We don’t know how many years that’s going to be, but we’re in the ends, and this is for our learning. You got it? Now, there are people that say the Old Testament Scriptures are outdated, you know, it doesn’t work. They’re not reading their Bible. You learn tremendous things from the whole book, all the Scriptures, all right? And then 2 Timothy 3:16, “All Scripture” — how many? All of them — “is profitable for reproof, correction, instruction in” what? Righteousness. It’s righteousness that’s the focus, folks. I keep telling you that, all right? “That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all” what? Good works. So we’re supposed to do what? Good works. These people that say, “It’s not by works, no matter what you do, if you believe in Christ you’re going” — no. The focus of the Bible is to turn you from bad works to good works. And this is one of the important things that the baptism of the Holy Ghost does: the Holy Spirit turns you to good works. And we need that baptism of the Holy Spirit.
Is the Old Testament still for us today?

Romans 15:4: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that we through the patience and comfort of the Scriptures might have hope. 1 Corinthians 10:11: Now all these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. 2 Timothy 3:16-17: All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.
Why isn’t America the nation it was 60 years ago?

He says the struggle between conservatives and liberals is not new but goes back to the early 1800s. In 1927, he says, conservatives and fundamentalists dropped out of political involvement, which left politics to the liberal churches, the socialists and the liberal economic people, who “had no opposition” in making civil laws for decades. He says believers are the majority and could turn an election, but they have to get informed.
Why isn’t America the nation it was 60 years ago?

Now remember, everybody knows that America is not the nation it was sixty years ago. All you’ve got to do is read history. I happen to have lived through it. We showed you how we got to where we are at. Conservatives and fundamentalists versus liberal Christians has been since the early 1800s. Liberal and conservative economics has been since the early 1800s. And Republicans versus Democrats has been since the early 1800s. This is not a new thing, and you young people need to know that these terminologies are not a new thing for your generation. We have been struggling with these issues since our nation basically started. Amen? Now, we reminded you that in 1927 the conservatives and fundamentalists dropped out of political involvement until the ’60s and ’70s, when they were taking our religious liberties away. And then they bowed out again because of the media pressure of standing up for Bible morality. Our leaders at that time, including Jerry Falwell and Robinson [unclear] of the 700 Club and all that, and Buchanan — they all, when the pressure came on, they dropped out. I lived through it. Phyllis Schlafly is about the only one left, Eagle Forum, that hung in there, and she’s a Catholic. We showed you that that left politics to the liberal churches, the socialists, the liberal economic people, and they had no opposition to making civil laws for decades. And I want to remind you that a person can be liberal in social issues and conservative in economic issues. They can be conservative in Bible issues and liberal in economic and social issues. It can be a mixture. Are you there? And so, see, America needs to understand these things. The American church, as I showed you, has the pivoting power. The believers in America can turn an election any way we choose, because we are the majority. I showed you that. But to do that, we’ve got to inform these believers. You’ve got to get informed. You’ve got to learn more than, you know, salvation and going to heaven and the second coming. Can I hear an amen? We’ve got to learn the whole gospel of God.
Where did government entitlements come from?

He says entitlements started when Roosevelt began the New Deal during the Depression, when families could no longer take care of families. The problem, he says, was that it never got removed. It kept growing and came to be expected as a right, and it robbed families of being self-supporting. He adds that in the Bible the family is still a high priority and is held accountable to take care of its members.
Where did government entitlements come from?

Entitlements, we told you, started when Roosevelt started the New Deal. And Roosevelt himself said this: up to this time the family was a firm, like a law firm, a self-supporting group. The family took care of family. But see, when this Depression came along — I showed you pictures — people were out of work. Families couldn’t take care of families anymore. Many families could not take care of their families anymore. And Roosevelt came in with the New Deal, and he gave stimulus to people, gave aid to people, and so forth. And the poor people, of course, they turned Democratic and voted that way because they needed to survive. Amen. The problem was it never got removed. It kept growing, even when our economy was great. And these entitlements were expected. It was a right: “It’s my right as an American to get these things.” And then it robbed the families of being a self-supporting entity for each family member’s success. See, and folks, in the Bible the family is still a high priority, and they are held accountable to take care of family members in the Bible.
What does “every man did what was right in his own eyes” mean?

He says that in Judges 17 Micah had a house of gods, his own images and idols, and consecrated his son to be his priest, because there was no king in Israel and “every man did what was right in his own eyes.” He asks, “is that America?” and answers, “Absolutely.” He says God wanted to rule over them through his Scriptures, through the Levites.
What does “every man did what was right in his own eyes” mean?

But we’re going to look now in the Scriptures at how to turn a nation back to God. All right, it starts with the church. We’re going to go to Judges chapters 17 and 18 and find an illustration there of a condition that brought destruction. And here’s what we’re going to find: they’re going to reject Jesus and the Scriptures ruling over them. All right, this is what they did. We’re going to see they’re going to reject God ruling over them — Jesus Christ and his Word, the Scriptures. Judges 17:5-6. Micah was an Ephraimite, and he had a house of gods. He had his church in his home, all right? And he made an ephod like the real priest in the temple, with the shoulder stones with the tribe names on them, and the cloth and all that. And he had a teraphim — that is household gods. He made his own little images and idols, all right? And he consecrated one of his sons to be his priest. Isn’t that nice? He paid his son to preach what he wanted him to preach. Are you there? See, an Ephraimite could not be a priest, but it didn’t matter, you see, because there was no king in Israel; every man did what was right in his own eyes. That’s why. And is that America? Absolutely. Now, in the Bible, government — a king, a leader — was instituted to go to war, to unite the people, to protect from invaders and other nations that would come in and take what they had, and to see that justice was done in court. That’s what the leader was for. And they were given the authority to take taxes to support themselves to do this job. That’s the three areas: taxes, judicial, and war. But there was no king; there was no government. Actually, God wanted to rule over them through his Scriptures, through the Levites.
What does “every man did what was right in his own eyes” mean?

Judges 17:5-6: The man Micah had a shrine, and made an ephod and household idols; and he consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest. In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
Do we want God’s blessings but not His rule?

He says the people rejected God and the Scriptures, and that in 1 Samuel 8:7 God told Samuel, “they have rejected me that I should not rule over them.” He says people want to go to heaven and want God’s blessings and approval, but God wants to rule in their life, and they do not want it. He says it is not just an Old Testament thing, and points to Luke 19:14.
Do we want God’s blessings but not His rule?

But they rejected God. They rejected the Scriptures and did what they wanted to do in their own eyes. In 1 Samuel 8:7, just a few years after this scripture, Samuel was the last judge of ten judges, and God said to Samuel, “They have rejected me that I should not rule over them.” They haven’t rejected you, Samuel; they rejected me. See, the people didn’t want God telling them what to do. Is that America? Yeah. We want to go to heaven. We want his blessings. We want him to prosper us. But we don’t want to do what he tells us to do. Even in the New Testament, in Luke 19:14, the parable of the Lord going off and coming back, his citizens say, “We will not have this man to rule over us.” And that parable was about Jesus Christ. See, people want to go to heaven. People want God’s blessings and God’s approval, but God wants to rule in their life. He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life, and they don’t want it. So it’s not just an Old Testament thing. And this is where we’re at in Judges: the people doing what’s right — they didn’t want God telling them what to do. They’re coming up with their own way of worship, their own religion, and their own home and their own family. And this is the setting.
Do we want God’s blessings but not His rule?

1 Samuel 8:7: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Heed the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them. Luke 19:14: But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We will not have this man to reign over us.’
Why did the tribe of Dan go looking for more land?

Using a map, he says Dan decided their inheritance was too small and they needed more land, though they had not conquered all the land God gave them. He says the pockets of resistance remained because of their sin and because they did not obey God. They went up to Laish, met Micah, and took his gods and a wayward Levite who would preach whatever he was paid to preach.
Why did the tribe of Dan go looking for more land?

Now, here’s a map of Israel back in the days of the Bible. Here is a city up here. Israel had all this territory here, okay? Laish was right on the border of the kingdoms, the Canaanite kingdoms that God told them to conquer. They were somehow connected with Sidon, over here on the coast, the Phoenician Empire. The Phoenician Empire — God did not give God’s people authority to conquer them, all right? And the book of Judges covers a period of 1400 to 1100 BC. The Phoenicians were not conquered until 351 BC by any other nation, including Israel. All right, but Dan, down here in the southern part of the kingdom by Judah — they decided that their inheritance was too small and they needed more land. Now, the truth is, they hadn’t conquered all of this area. The Amorites had all the valley areas, and the Danites, God’s people, were forced up into the mountains. They were hillbillies like me, all right? The nice bottom land, where the farming and everything was great, the enemy had it. A lot of people think that God’s people conquered Canaan land, and they didn’t. They conquered it, but there were pockets of resistance they didn’t conquer because of their sin, because they didn’t obey God. They didn’t win the full war. That sounds like America. Yeah. And so, because they wouldn’t conquer the people that God gave them, then they went up here to Laish. They went looking for more property, more land. Ephraim is kind of in the middle here, and it’s kind of a big area. This is where Micah is; he’s an Ephraimite. And so they come to Micah’s house and they see his gods and his son as a priest. And by this time Micah has got a wayward Levite — because of money, Micah offered him money to come in and be his priest. This wayward Levite that was supposed to be ministering down here in the temple in Jerusalem said, “Sure, you’re going to pay me? I’ll be what? What do you want me to preach? Oh, you want household gods? Fine, that’s great, hallelujah. Oh, you want an ephod? Oh yeah, it’s great, whatever you want. Yeah, I’ll do it. Give me the bucks.” Are you there?
What does it mean to live “careless” and “secure” in your own feelings?

He says the people of Laish “dwelt careless,” which in the Hebrew means they felt secure, going by their feelings, not by Scripture or the Lord. He calls it the libertarian mentality: “don’t get involved, don’t stand up for anything.” He says the word “secure” means self-confidence, like football players pumping themselves up, and he asks, “Sound like the American church?”
What does it mean to live “careless” and “secure” in your own feelings?

So they picked up this guy’s gods and this guy’s Levite, and they went up to Laish, and they found some people that had this kind of attitude, this kind of lifestyle. The people of Laish dwelt careless. All right, “careless” there in the Hebrew is they felt secure — their feelings. See, when I feel this is okay, I feel I’m going to heaven — sounds like America. Yeah. Going by their feelings, not by Scripture, not by the Lord. They dwelt careless; they dwelt quietly. They were not involved. They’re really libertarians. You know what a libertarian is, don’t you? Yeah. As long as I’m not hurting anybody, I have the freedom to do what I want to do. That’s the libertarian mentality: don’t get involved, don’t stand up for anything. I am an individual, and whatever you want to believe, you believe. And so this is their attitude. All right, they were secure. Now, “secure” and “careless” are very close words, very close in the Hebrew. But this word “secure,” unlike “careless,” they felt secure; this word “secure” is they had self-confidence. Now, you ever seen these football players, before they go to play a game? They get in a huddle and they’re all pumped up. “Man, oh yeah, we’re going to win, we’re going to win, we’re going to win, we’re going to win! If we say it, we’ll get it. If we claim it, we’ll get it. Oh yeah, yeah!” And they hype themselves up psychologically, and they go in there feeling self-confident, and they lose. Somebody’s got to lose. Both teams are doing it, and one of them can’t come off a winner. Sound like the American church? Absolutely. They got personal self-confidence; they psych themselves up. Just like Sidon dwelt — lived this whole Phoenician thing — so they were connected to this Phoenician Empire, but they were on the border, and there was no magistrate, no judge, no government to shame them in anything. You see, this is the libertarian mentality: there’s no central government to deal with anything, everybody was independently, individually doing what they wanted to do.
What does it mean to live “careless” and “secure” in your own feelings?

Judges 18:7: So the five men departed and went to Laish. They saw the people who were there, how they dwelt safely, in the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and secure. There were no rulers in the land who might put them to shame for anything. They were far from the Sidonians, and they had no ties with anyone.
What happens to a nation when every group does what is right in its own eyes?

He says the people of Laish had no business with anyone, like American churches in their little corrals, and that the church’s downfall is that it does not speak Bible morality in public places but preaches to the choir. Then Dan struck Laish with the sword and burned the city: “one bad group destroying another bad group,” and he says “that’s what’s going to happen to America if we don’t turn things around.”
What happens to a nation when every group does what is right in its own eyes?

They had no business with anyone. See, our churches in America, in their little corrals, not having any business with the church down the street. Now this word “business” also means “speech.” They never talk to anybody. And that’s the downfall of the church right now: we don’t get out there in public places and speak Bible morality. If we do believe in it, we speak it to ourselves. We preach to the choir, people that already believe what we believe. We keep preaching to each other. This is the condition of the people of Laish. Now, where did it lead? Okay, Dan smote them with the edge of the sword and burnt the city with fire. He came in and destroyed them: one bad group destroying another bad group, doing what’s right in their own eyes. And that’s what’s going to happen to America if we don’t turn things around. Do you see it? Remember, these things were written for us to learn by. They weren’t there for history; they’re for us to learn by. They are history, but they’re recorded for us to learn by.
What happens to a nation when every group does what is right in its own eyes?

Judges 18:27-28: So they took the things Micah had made, and the priest who had belonged to him, and went to Laish, to a people quiet and secure; and they struck them with the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire. There was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon, and they had no ties with anyone. It was in the valley that belongs to Beth Rehob. So they rebuilt the city and dwelt there.
Do people pay ministers to tell them what they want to hear?

He says many churches and groups doing what is right in their own eyes hire ministers to flatter them, as in Isaiah 30:10, “Speak to us smooth things.” He says they do not want to hear about good works or what is right but that they are “okay,” and so they pay ministers to preach what they want to hear. He says he talks with people who feel sure they are going to heaven while they are sinning.
Do people pay ministers to tell them what they want to hear?

Now, just summarizing again, this illustrates the American church, okay? We have many churches, many groups doing what’s right in their own eyes, hiring and appointing ministers to flatter them, to please them, not God, as it says in Isaiah 30:10: “Speak to us smooth things. Speak to us deceits. Don’t speak to us right things.” And what’s the scripture we read? Profitable for what? Righteousness. Good works. We don’t want to hear about good works. We don’t want to hear about what’s right. We want to hear that we’re okay. And so they give them the money, they get the big fancy houses, they get the cars, they get the fame. They pay ministers to preach what they want to hear. We live careless. We feel it’s okay. I talk to them all the time: “I don’t see nothing wrong with this. I feel this is all right. I feel I’m going to heaven. I have confidence I’m going to heaven.” I witness the people every year, and they mean it. They actually believe they’re going to heaven. They have the emotional carelessness; they have the safety of their self-confidence. Carelessness — and they’re sinning, and doing sins that the Bible says you will go to the lake of fire, with no God-anointed leader to shame them to do right. The pope isn’t doing it. No united moral business with other churches. See, somewhere we’ve got to get fired up. We’ve got to unite with other churches over right issues. Can I hear an amen? Not the wrong issues — the right issues. Making our own gods: all roads lead to the same God. We covered that thoroughly. You know, Muslims are going to heaven, Hindus are going to heaven, everybody’s going to heaven — I don’t know why Jesus ever needed to die on the cross. The liberal churches believe that there is no hell.
Do people pay ministers to tell them what they want to hear?
Isaiah 30:10: Who say to the seers, “Do not see,” And to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us right things; Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits.
Will God destroy a nation that disobeys — or will He relent?

He reads Jeremiah 12:17, “I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation,” and Jeremiah 18:8, that if a nation turns from its evil, God will repent of the evil he thought to do. He says this is why we need to get the word out, and that if people embrace Bible morality “it is also an umbrella of protection when God judges.” If we do not, he says, “we get punished right along with the heathen.”
Will God destroy a nation that disobeys — or will He relent?

The result, here in Jeremiah 12:17: “If they will not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation.” You want to do what’s right in your own eyes? You believers want to worship God your own way and serve God your own way and do what you want to do? I’m going to destroy you right along with the rest. Are you there? But Jeremiah 18:8: “If that nation I have pronounced destruction turn from their evil ways, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” This is why we need to get the word out, because he said also, in Isaiah, that he would bring his people, the righteous ones, under his wings. You see? Hallelujah. And he said a thousand may fall at your right hand and ten thousand at your left, but nothing shall touch you. You see, if we get them to embrace Bible morality, it is also an umbrella of protection when God judges. Hallelujah. But if we don’t, we get punished right along with the heathen.
Will God destroy a nation that disobeys — or will He relent?

Jeremiah 12:17: But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation,” says the LORD. Jeremiah 18:8: if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. Psalm 91:4-7: He shall cover you with His feathers, And under His wings you shall take refuge; His truth shall be your shield and buckler. You shall not be afraid of the terror by night, Nor of the arrow that flies by day, Nor of the pestilence that walks in darkness, Nor of the destruction that lays waste at noonday. A thousand may fall at your side, And ten thousand at your right hand; But it shall not come near you.
What is scientism, and why does he read quotes from Hitler on socialism?

He reads quotes that he attributes to Hitler from 1930 and 1927, in which Hitler calls himself a socialist and an enemy of the capitalistic system. He then reads a definition of scientism, “the belief that science alone can explain phenomena,” and says “science has become a religion in America.”
What is scientism, and why does he read quotes from Hitler on socialism?

I want to give you a couple of quotes from Hitler. 1930: “Our adopted term ‘socialist’ has nothing to do with Marx and socialism. Marx and socialism is anti-property; true socialism is not.” That’s the University of California Press, 1982. 1927, Hitler said: “We are socialists, enemies of today’s capitalistic economic system for the exploitation of the economically weak, with its unfair salaries, with its unseemly evaluation of a human being according to wealth and property instead of responsibility and performance, and we are determined to destroy the capitalistic system under all conditions.” Doubleday, Hitler, Adolf Hitler, 1972. “Scientism is reliance on science for answers, the belief that science alone can explain phenomena” — that is, miracles and other occurrences, any kind of occurrence, as well as natural things. That’s the Bing dictionary. “The only source of genuine factual knowledge is scientism. They alone yield true knowledge about man and society.” The Dictionary of Modern Thought, 1999. See, science has become a religion in America.
Can Christians work together when they disagree on some things?

He tells of a Baptist pastor in Dallas whom the media called a “hate preacher” because he is against homosexual acts and same-sex marriage. He says they agree on the moral issues but disagree on the age of the earth, the pre-tribulation rapture and tongues, and that “I would unite with this guy any day on Bible morals.”
Can Christians work together when they disagree on some things?

Opponents, and some believers, attack any church’s moral standards. This is Jeffress [unclear], the pastor of the Baptist church in Dallas, Texas. He had Tim Tebow invited to his church, and Tim Tebow canceled out at the last minute because of homosexual groups — homosexual activist groups — putting the pressure on Tebow not to affiliate with this guy, because he’s against marriage between the same sex. He’s against homosexual acts and adultery and other Bible moral issues. Okay, and so the media really got on that, and they called him a hate preacher. You see, this guy, we agree on the moral issues. But when O’Reilly interviewed him, he said the earth was 12.5 billion years old. He said, us fundamentalists, there’s many fundamentalists that say the earth’s 6,000 years old, and the Bible doesn’t say that. Well, my friend, the Bible doesn’t say it’s 12.6 billion years old either. But you’ve got six twenty-four-hour days, and you add that up — any fourth grader can figure this out. The earth was created in six days, and it started from Adam and his generations down; it’s about 6,000 years old. Are you there? See, he’s caved in to the evolution pressure. So he and I would disagree on that, but that’s not a Bible moral issue, so I could still unite with him. He believes in the pre-tribulation rapture theory. These pre-tribulation rapture theory people can show me no proof in the Bible of a pre-tribulation rapture. They can give me — they have to twist, bend, stretch everything to get it done. There is no statement in the Bible, “I’m coming before the tribulation.” None. In fact, there’s a statement that says, “After the tribulation, I’m coming.” How many of you know that? Anyway, so we disagree on that. But disagreeing on that is not a Bible moral issue. See, it doesn’t hurt anybody. He doesn’t believe in us tongue talkers. I mean, I’m a tongue talker. I got filled with the Holy Ghost, and I spoke in tongues when I got filled with the Holy Ghost. So we disagree. In fact, he thinks tongue talkers are evil people, a cult. But I would unite with this guy any day on Bible morals, amen, because that’s what we unite around.
What should Christians not unite over, and who should they not fellowship with?

He says they do not unite over the second coming or how you are baptized. He lists fornication, sexual immorality, homosexuality, incest, greed, idolatry, a railer, a drunkard and an extortioner, and says that when a believer wants to say it is okay, “we are not to fellowship with them.” He then reads a verse about marking those who cause divisions and avoiding them.
What should Christians not unite over, and who should they not fellowship with?

Here are the list of things we do not unite over: fornication, sexual immorality, homosexuality, incest and all that. A believer who wants to say it’s okay — we are not to fellowship with them. Nothing to do with the second coming, nothing to do with a lot of these things that we divide over, how you’re baptized and all that stuff. Greed — not just wanting what somebody has, but doing everything you can to get it. Idolatry. A railer — that is a sharp-tongued person, a person that’s degrading, attacking with their voice. You probably looked at one when you washed this morning in the mirror, putting down everybody else and exalting yourself. I hear it all the time. I hear it every week. I hear a person telling me how bad this other person is, and they are bad themselves and have no intention of changing their badness. “But Pastor, you should really get on this person.” And a lot of times they’re doing exactly what that person is doing. Are you there? See, with our mouth we attack, we destroy. A drunkard — and yet Christians want to drink intoxication, and we know now one shot of whiskey is intoxication. An extortioner — that means you take things by force; you use your title or your position to make people do what you want them to do. With such a one, no, not even to eat. Mark 16:17 [unclear: the passage he reads is Romans 16:17], “Mark them which cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine which you’ve learned, and avoid them.”
What should Christians not unite over, and who should they not fellowship with?

1 Corinthians 5:11: But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone named a brother, who is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a person. Romans 16:17: Now I urge you, brethren, note those who cause divisions and offenses, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and avoid them.
What happens when a leader follows the crowd instead of good counsel?

He says that in 1 Kings 12:8 Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men and took the bad advice of the young men, and it split the nation and caused a civil war. He then plays a video of Obama saying his view on homosexuality changed because of friends, and asks if that shows he is a real Christian: “No. A Christian is one that follows Christ.” He says this kind of thing “is going to destroy our nation.”
What happens when a leader follows the crowd instead of good counsel?

There’s people that come in — 1 Kings 12:8 — Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men, who gave him right counsel, and consulted with the young men that grew up with him, which stood before him, and they gave him bad advice, and he did it. And it did split the nation. It caused a civil war. Are you with me? This video of Obama, I’ve showed it to you before. He’s saying, “My outlook on homosexuality has changed because of my friends and my acquaintances and people on my staff who are raising kids in a homosexual family and doing a good job. These are great people.” So now I am for homosexual marriages, same-sex marriages, and the homosexual lifestyle. Because he said he was against it when he ran for president, in 2007 or ’08, and right — but see, he listened to [unclear], and he says he’s a Christian, and he says he believes the Bible. Now, does this action tell you he believes the Bible? Does it tell you he’s a real Christian? No. A Christian is one that follows Christ. See, it’s just another example that we are like the tribe of Dan: we got God, but we do it any way we want. And this kind of stuff is going to destroy our nation. That’s the bottom line.
What happens when a leader follows the crowd instead of good counsel?
1 Kings 12:8: But he rejected the advice which the elders had given him, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
Can the Word of God still turn a nation?

He says that if we get the message out, the word will work, since the Bible says it will not return void. He says it is not the Catholics, the Protestants or the Jews but the word that has to get out, and that the church has been too long inside its four walls. “You speak the word, and the word convicts and convinces people,” and the turning of a nation starts with the church.
Can the Word of God still turn a nation?

But if we can get the message out, and the word will work — remember, the Bible says the word will not return what? Void. But it will be profitable and to the purpose that I have purposed it. But it’s the word. It’s not the Catholics, it’s not the Protestants, it’s not the Jews; it’s the word that’s got to get out. And we need to really get a hold of God and get organized and get a desire and a drive in our hearts to get the word out. For too long the church has been in its four walls, worshiping and praying, and not outside the walls telling the people that are believing wrong that they are wrong. Not in that way, but just by speaking what’s right, by speaking the word. Don’t go up and say, “You’re wrong.” You speak the word, and the word convicts and convinces people. The word does it. You don’t have to force them. The word will do the job. So we saw the start of the turning of a nation starts with who? The church. We’ve got to turn around, and we’ve got to help others turn around.
Can the Word of God still turn a nation?
Isaiah 55:11: So shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; It shall not return to Me void, But it shall accomplish what I please, And it shall prosper in the thing for which I sent it.
Did the events in the Old Testament really happen?

He says they did. He disagrees with those who say the Old Testament accounts are allegories, fictitious stories and myths, and says “They weren’t myths, they weren’t dreams, they weren’t fantasies.” He says they actually occurred to them as examples, written for our admonition.
Does he say the Old Testament is outdated?
No. He says people who say the Old Testament Scriptures are outdated are “not reading their Bible,” and that you learn tremendous things from the whole book, all the Scriptures.
What does he say is the focus of the Bible?

He says it is righteousness. He says the focus of the Bible is to turn you from bad works to good works, and that one of the important things the baptism of the Holy Ghost does is that the Holy Spirit turns you to good works.
Can believers in America turn an election?

He says the American church has the pivoting power: the believers in America can turn an election any way they choose, because they are the majority. To do that, he says, they have to be informed and learn the whole gospel of God, not only salvation, going to heaven and the second coming.
What does he say government is for in the Bible?

He says a king or leader was instituted to go to war, to unite the people and protect them from invaders, and to see that justice was done in court. He says the leader was given the authority to take taxes to do this job, which he calls “taxes, judicial, and war.”
Did Israel conquer all of the land of Canaan?

He says a lot of people think God’s people conquered Canaan, but they did not. They conquered it, he says, but there were pockets of resistance they did not conquer because of their sin and because they did not obey God. They “didn’t win the full war.”
What does he mean by the libertarian mentality?

He says a libertarian is someone who says, “as long as I’m not hurting anybody, I have the freedom to do what I want to do.” He calls it the mentality of “don’t get involved, don’t stand up for anything,” and says the people of Laish were like that.
Why does he say preaching to the choir is a problem?

He says the downfall of the church right now is that we do not get out in public places and speak Bible morality; if we believe in it, we speak it to ourselves. He says “We preach to the choir, people that already believe what we believe. We keep preaching to each other.”
Should churches unite, and over what?

He says that somewhere we have to get fired up and unite with other churches over right issues, “not the wrong issues, the right issues.” Later in the message he says Christians unite around Bible morals and do not unite over things like the second coming or how you are baptized.
Does he say all roads lead to the same God?

No. He lists “making our own gods” and the idea that “all roads lead to the same God” as part of the problem. He says the liberal churches say Muslims and Hindus are going to heaven, and asks why Jesus ever needed to die on the cross if that were so. He says the liberal churches believe there is no hell.
Is Bible morality an umbrella of protection?

He says that if we get people to embrace Bible morality, “it is also an umbrella of protection when God judges.” He says God would bring his people, the righteous ones, under his wings, and that if we do not, “we get punished right along with the heathen.”
What does he say the Bible says about the age of the earth?

He says the Bible does not say the earth is 12.5 billion years old, but it does not say 6,000 years in so many words either. He says there are six 24-hour days, and that if you add up the generations from Adam down it is about 6,000 years old. He adds that this is not a Bible moral issue, so he could still unite with someone who disagrees.
What does he say about the pre-tribulation rapture?

He says pre-tribulation rapture theory people can show him no proof in the Bible, and that there is no statement in the Bible saying “I’m coming before the tribulation.” He says there is a statement that says “after the tribulation, I’m coming,” but that disagreeing on it is not a Bible moral issue.
What does he mean by a “railer”?

He says a railer is a sharp-tongued person, a person who is degrading, attacking with their voice, putting down everybody else and exalting themselves. He says he hears it every week and that with our mouth we attack and we destroy.

items.d: In “Division Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer answers a new book that blames the church for young people leaving, saying the complaints are not new and the answer is to stop blaming and get in and make a…
p: In “Division Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer answers a new book that blames the church for young people leaving, saying the complaints are not new and the answer is to stop blaming and get in and make a difference. He then turns to 1 Corinthians 1:10, where Paul’s first correction of the Corinthians is division, and says our unity is in Jesus and the Scriptures, not in a minister, a denomination or whoever baptized us. Along the way he speaks about church boredom, science, intolerance, the home, and other religions.
Why do young people leave the church?

Pastor Kincer says the claim that 75% of young people are out of the church after high school is not new: it has been there since he became a Christian, and it used to be higher. When he stayed away as a young person, he says, it was his own decision, not the church’s fault. He wanted to go his own way and sin.
Why do young people leave the church?

There’s a new book out called You Lost Us. It’s going to sell millions of copies, like the other ones did that I’ve brought out before. And it’s all about attacking the church, blaming the church for the falling away of young people — Barna [unclear], and all these people, you know — and I debated with them this week, because I think they’re wrong. Number one, the statistic that 75% of young people are out of the church when they leave high school and go into college has always been there since I’ve been a Christian. In fact, it was a little higher. If it’s only 75%, we gained some ground. It used to be 80-some percent. Okay, that’s not a new statistic. Back when I was a young person, I didn’t go to church because I wanted to do my thing. It wasn’t the church’s fault. It was my decision. I wanted to sin. I wanted to go the way I wanted to go. I didn’t want any church or any God bridling me and telling me what to do. Don’t tell me what I can and can’t do.
Should we blame the church, or take responsibility?

He says God told him, “Son, don’t complain of the church. Get in and make a difference in the church.” It is easy to blame a church, he says, but another thing to take it on your own shoulders to find your God and make a difference. He adds that being baptized in the Holy Ghost brings power, the supernatural ability to make good, right, wise decisions.
Should we blame the church, or take responsibility?

When I got saved and I complained to God about these things, he told me, “Son, don’t complain of the church. Get in and make a difference in the church.” See, when you’re baptized in the Holy Ghost, you can actually get direction before you ever know the Scriptures, because the Holy Spirit will always give you the nature of God and the truth of the Scriptures until you know them. Do you understand that? And the baptism of the Holy Ghost is very important. Remember, he said you’d receive power. He didn’t say you’d receive tongues and prophecy. He said you would receive what? Power — supernatural ability to make good decisions, right decisions, wise decisions. Are you with me so far? And it’s easy to blame the Catholic church, the Baptist church, the Pentecostal church. It’s easy to blame. It’s another thing to take it on your shoulders to be responsible to find your God, and take it on your shoulders that I can make the difference in the church.
Should we blame the church, or take responsibility?
Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

He calls that claim a lie. He says that in this generation there are movies, DVDs, pamphlets and books on science and the Bible, so no young person has an excuse for not understanding, though he adds that the church cannot talk about science in the Bible every Sunday.

So they said young people — after they were interviewed in the statistics, and they went all through asking young people why they left the church — one of them was science. The church does not embrace science. I said, that’s a lie. We don’t go around talking about science all the time, but in this generation, like no generation before, there is such materials about science in the Bible that no young person has any excuse for not understanding. Could that be true? You can get movies, you can get DVDs, you can get pamphlets, you can get books on the issue and read them yourself. But the church can’t get up every Sunday and talk about science in the Bible.

He says church felt boring to him at 16 to 18 because he would not get involved. He was a clock-watcher who did not want to sing to the Lord or pray. David said he was glad to go to the house of the Lord (Psalm 122:1), and he says anyone who does not want to get involved in church, or in God, will be bored and will find every excuse not to be involved.

Anyway, the second thing is the young people said church was boring. Well, that’s exactly what I said when I was 17, 16, 18: church is boring — because I didn’t get involved. I wanted to do my thing. I didn’t want to sing unto the Lord. I didn’t want to get down and pray. I just couldn’t wait for the thing to get over. I was the clock watcher. When is this people going to quit? In fact, if I could, I’d get there late so I didn’t have to endure. The only thing is, my dad was never late to anything, and I picked up the habit. But a lot of us were late because we don’t want to spend any more minutes in that boring place than we have to, or we just lost our desire for Jesus. David said, “I was glad when they said unto me, Let us” — what? — “go to the house of the Lord.” Man, he was excited. It’s assembly time. Oh, glory, let’s go! And, see, we’ve lost all that. A lot of Christians have lost all that, and so they write these books blaming the church. But the church is made up of who? People. And it’s the people that are the determination of a church. Hallelujah. And so I go, that’s not nothing new. Anybody that doesn’t want to get involved in the church, involved in God, are going to be bored. Hallelujah. They’ll find every excuse not to be involved. Church, we can blame till we’re blue in the face, but the thing is, it’s our problem. It’s your problem. It’s your decision. Hallelujah.
Psalm 122:1: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.”

He says the church cannot change the Scriptures because public policy says certain things are okay. It has to preach what the Bible says, whether young people like it or not, and he names homosexuality and abortion as the examples the book raised.

They said the third thing, which should have been the first thing, is the church is intolerant. And then they describe that we are hard on the homosexuals, and hard on abortion. And I go, well, you can’t change the Scriptures because public policy says that these things are okay. And young people can’t change the Scriptures and blame the church when the Bible says that homosexuality is a sin, and you will go to hell for it. The church can’t change the Scriptures. We’ve got to preach it, whether the young people like it or not. Isn’t that true? And if they want to blame us for wanting to protect the life of innocent kids from abortion on demand, then that’s their problem. They’ve got to stand before God and give accountability for that.
Does the church have to change its message to keep young people?

He says the voices blaming the church are wrong, and asks, “Do we have to line up with the Scriptures, or do we get the Scriptures to line up with us?” His answer is that we have to line up with the Scriptures, since God is true and every man a liar. He also says the church does have its problems.
Does the church have to change its message to keep young people?

And I told the leader of this topic, you guys are wrong. This is nothing new at all. To me, you’re just wanting to sell another book. And they didn’t like that. Yeah, they’re going to make millions of bucks off this book. And people are going to be thinking, and see, that justifies the young people for leaving the church and going into sin and having sex before marriage and all the rest, because the book said the church is at fault. And the church does have its problems. And so this message, starting on January 1st, is in retaliation to all this stuff. You know why I got a suit on today? Because they said suits turn young people off. I said, a suit does not change me in any way or any shape. And just because you said suit, I’m going to wear a suit for two months. I hadn’t put on a suit for quite a while. A suit’s got nothing to do with it. People don’t come to church because you wear a suit. Where is the focus, church? We’ve lost it. And I wanted to introduce this message this way because I want you to understand there’s voices out there that are wrong. Let God be what? True. Let the Scriptures be what? True. And every man a what? Liar. Do we have to line up with the Scriptures, or do we get the Scriptures to line up with us? We’ve got to line up with the Scriptures. Hallelujah.
Does the church have to change its message to keep young people?
Romans 3:4: Certainly not! Indeed, let God be true but every man a liar. As it is written: “That You may be justified in Your words, And may overcome when You are judged.”
What does it mean to speak the same thing in church?

He says the first confrontation Paul brings to the Corinthian church is division: “I want you to all speak the same thing” (1 Corinthians 1:10). Like a Big Mac that is identical in every country, he says the Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same in every church.
What does it mean to speak the same thing in church?

And thusly, we are going to have our second session on starting, developing, and governing a New Testament church. This week we’re going to look at the development of the church, and the first confrontation that Paul is going to confront this tremendous church with is division — separating one from another. He says, “I want you to all speak the same thing.” First Corinthians 1:10. You see that McDonald’s sign up there? When I was in Salvador, when I was in Brazil, when I was in Korea, when I was in China, when I go to any state in America, I can go to McDonald’s, order a Big Mac, and it’s identical. They didn’t change the Big Mac. If I order fries, I get McDonald’s fries. If I order a Coke, I get the real Coke. I don’t get a China Coke, I don’t get a Korean Coke — I get Coke. And if you’ve never been to a third world country and ministering for two or three weeks, and your body can’t handle the food and you’re losing weight and all that, and you see a McDonald’s, it’s like seeing the tongues of fire on the day of Pentecost. Wow! Man, I said, stop the car! Stop the car, man! The driver pulled [over] — what’s wrong? What’s wrong? — There’s a McDonald’s! Go over there! The whole schedule changed. I ordered — must have been four Big Macs. I tell you, big fries, a Coke — and it was the same. See, the Holy Ghost shouldn’t be preached different in one church and preached another way in another church. It should be the what? Same. Salvation should be what? The same. Righteousness and holy living should be what? The same. Everything should be the same, like McDonald’s is. But in America, do we have that? No! And so we confuse everybody. He says, “I want you to speak the same thing.” Why? He says, “I don’t want there to be divisions, separations among you.” Why?
What does it mean to speak the same thing in church?

1 Corinthians 1:10: Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
Why is unity in the church so important?

He points to Jesus’ words in Matthew 12:25: every kingdom, city or house divided against itself will not stand. He compares standing to a military taking a stand to defend its country, and says a divided people will lose the war.
Why is unity in the church so important?

Why is this so important? Why did he take this subject as the first confrontation with this very good church? Didn’t he just describe it as a very good church? Yes, but they’ve got some changing to do, and division is the first one. Now this is why. This is why unity is so important. Are you ready? Matthew 12:25: every kingdom — are we in the kingdom of God? Yes. — every kingdom, every city, every house, every family, and even Satan. Jesus said these words: “If they’re divided against themselves, they will not stand.” See, the word stand means a military — you know, they’re taking a stand to defend their country. And if they’re not in unity, what’s going to happen? They’re going to lose the war. Are we losing the war in America? Yes, we are. We’ve got to admit that so that we can be a part of changing that.
Why is unity in the church so important?
Matthew 12:25: But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.

He says no: husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and the same moral standards, and show their children Jesus in their lives, or the home will not stand. When parents go two different ways, he says, conflict follows and kids cannot wait to get out of the home.

In the home, is it imperative that the husband and wife stand together with the same truth, the same moral standards? Is it important? And being an example to their children — not just telling their children about Jesus, but showing them in their life. Yes, it is. Why? Or the home isn’t going to stand. See, why do we get divorce in America, even in the Christian church? Because the husband and wife go two different ways. They start getting different beliefs, and then their actions come out of those beliefs, and then there’s conflict in the home. And kids can’t wait to get out of that conflict. They want to get out of home. You know, they’ll do anything. “Send me to college.” “Let me get married.” “I’ll join the military.” “Just get me out of this mess.” The unity is very important. And your kids’ parents need to see you in unity around Jesus, around truth — especially the morals of the Bible. Second Coming doesn’t mean a thing to kids. They need to see our moral standards. Amen? They need to see our tongue speaking rightly, our anger curbed. You shall receive what when the Holy Ghost comes upon you? Power. Hallelujah. So are we offered the sources, the solutions? Absolutely. You can’t violate these things.

Matthew 12:25: But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand. Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”
How should Christians handle disagreements in the church?

He says to be joined in the same mind and judgment, and to judge “right judgment” rather than by personal opinion, with decisions backed up by the Word of God, with two or three verses (John 7:24). He also says that when we disagree with something in the church, we should not go tell the whole world, because it weakens the church more.
How should Christians handle disagreements in the church?

And so the church should not be like it is today. “Perfectly joined in the same mind and judgment” — completely joined in the same thought, the same understanding. “Judge not according to appearance,” John 7:24, “but judge” what? Right judgment. Don’t judge for your personal opinion. Make decisions that are right and backed up by the Word of God, with two or three verses. “It’s been declared that there is quarreling, arguments, contentions among you.” And that’s what we do. If we disagree with it, we go out and blab to the world. Isn’t that right? We disagree with something going on in the church or some brother or something, we go out and tell everybody in the world. And it just weakens the church more.
How should Christians handle disagreements in the church?

1 Corinthians 1:10: Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment. John 7:24: Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment.” 1 Corinthians 1:11: For it has been declared to me concerning you, my brethren, by those of Chloe’s household, that there are contentions among you.
Who should we follow — a pastor, a denomination, or Christ?

Of the four groups in Corinth (“I’m of Paul,” “of Apollos,” “of Peter,” “of Christ”), he says only the Christ group is right. He says our unity comes from Christ, who is one with the Father and the Scriptures, not from a church name, a church group or a minister, and he asks whether the Pope, priests, Pentecostals or Baptists can save anyone. His answer is no.
Who should we follow — a pastor, a denomination, or Christ?

Okay, here’s the focus of the division. One says, “I’m of Paul.” One says, “I’m of Apollos.” One says, “I’m of Peter.” And one says, “I’m of Christ.” You’ve got four groups here and only one is right. Can you rationally, reasonably, logically tell me which group is right? Yeah, the Christ group. Hallelujah. And he explains it: is Christ divided? See, is Christ one with the Father? Is Christ one with the Scriptures? Is he united with the Father and the Scriptures? Yes. So where do I find my source of unity? In Christ, and me being like him, in unity with God and in unity with the Spirit. Not my church’s opinions, not my opinions, but Christ, in unity with his Father and in unity with the Scriptures. He says, “Was Paul bap— crucified for you?” See, was the Pope crucified for Catholics? Can the Pope save Catholics? No. Can their priests save Catholics? Can Pentecostals who speak in tongues save Pentecostals? No. Can the Baptists, who say tongues aren’t for today — and the baptism of the Holy Ghost, as we know it in Acts chapter 2 — can they save people? No. Is his argument good? Yes. So what he’s saying is, that last group is the right group. They’re focused on Christ, who can do something. Not their church name, not their church group, not some minister. It isn’t Schuller or Oral Roberts [unclear] or somebody. It is Christ and the Scriptures.
Who should we follow — a pastor, a denomination, or Christ?

1 Corinthians 1:12-13: Now I say this, that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” or “I am of Apollos,” or “I am of Cephas,” or “I am of Christ.” Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
Is Jesus the only way to God, or do all religions lead to the same God?

He says it is not all the same road to the same God. He points to Mormons re-baptizing converts and Muslims saying Christ did not die on the cross, says neither group believes Jesus is God, and says wanting everybody to be okay “makes Jesus a liar.” For him, “Jesus is God. If you know Jesus, you know God.”
Is Jesus the only way to God, or do all religions lead to the same God?

“Were you baptized in Paul’s name?” You see, I’m going to be making a statement later in this message about Mormons and Muslims. And the reason I know they’re not Christian is, Mormons, if you join their group, you have to get re-baptized. See, if they were Christians, they wouldn’t have to re-baptize us. I mean, if somebody’s baptized in the Baptist church or the Presbyterian church, I don’t get them re-baptized. Christ died how many times? Once. And besides, Satan definitely was not Jesus’s brother. And the Holy Ghost don’t make a mistake [unclear] polygamy and then have to change it. If an angel said something — angels don’t make mistakes. Muslims say that Christ did not die on the cross. Well, you just threw the whole Bible out. He said in the Old Testament he would die; in the New Testament it showed him dying. So it’s not all the same road to the same God, is it? And that’s what a lot of these young people that are blaming the church are wanting. They’re wanting everybody to be okay. That makes Jesus a liar. Hallelujah. And is Jesus God? See, the Mormons don’t believe that, and neither do the Muslims, and that’s a big problem. Jesus is God. If you know Jesus, you know God.
Is Jesus the only way to God, or do all religions lead to the same God?

1 Corinthians 1:12-13: Now I say this, that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” or “I am of Apollos,” or “I am of Cephas,” or “I am of Christ.” Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
Does it matter who baptized you?

He says no: Paul baptized only a few people so no one could say he baptized in his own name, so we should focus on Jesus rather than on the person or church group that baptized us. He sums up Paul’s three statements: follow and imitate Jesus, focus on Jesus, and preach Christ, his gospel and the cross, where the power of God is.
Does it matter who baptized you?

So, number one statement: follow and imitate Jesus, not a minister’s or a church group. Because Jesus is in unity with God. He is sinless. He died for us. He cleansed us from sin through water baptism. You see, Muslims don’t baptize in water. They have a purification ceremony. Jesus went down to the river and was what? Baptized. People were baptized — submerged in water. And Paul — uh, John the Baptist — said for the what? Remission of sin, the cleansing, the forgiveness of sin. And, church, that makes them wrong, and we can’t just overlook that, can we? We can’t change the Scriptures. Are you there? “All speak the same thing.” Paul baptized only three people to avoid that he baptized in his own name. So the second statement is, we’re not to focus on the person or the church group that baptized you. We’ve got to focus on who? Jesus. It’s almost identical to the second, first statement Paul made. Number three, Paul’s statement: preach Christ, preach his gospel, and preach the cross, for that’s where what is? Yeah — you want the power of God.
Does it matter who baptized you?

1 Corinthians 1:14-18: I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius, lest anyone should say that I had baptized in my own name. Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas. Besides, I do not know whether I baptized any other. For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel, not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of no effect. For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
Can new believers and long-time Christians worship in the same meeting?
He says yes. At a dinner table you can serve milk along with meat and mashed potatoes without a different supper for each age, and in the same way “we can have it all in one setting.”
Can new believers and long-time Christians worship in the same meeting?

And they say, well, you know, you can’t have new believers and old believers in the same meeting, in this new book. Folks, how many know, at a dinner table, you can serve milk along with meat and mashed potatoes? You don’t have to have, you know, a different supper for your four-year-old, and then a different supper for your adolescent, and then, you know, a real supper for the 30-year-old. I mean, we can have it all in one setting.
Is it true that 75% of young people leave church after high school?
He says that statistic is not new. It “has always been there since I’ve been a Christian,” he says, and it was a little higher, 80-some percent, so “we gained some ground.”
What does the baptism of the Holy Ghost give you?

He says you would receive power, not “tongues and prophecy”: the “supernatural ability to make good decisions, right decisions, wise decisions.” He also says the Holy Spirit will give you the nature of God and the truth of the Scriptures until you know them.
Where can young people learn about science and the Bible?
He says there are movies, DVDs, pamphlets and books on the issue that you can read yourself. He adds that the church cannot get up every Sunday and talk about science in the Bible.
Why do some Christians lose their excitement for church?

He says David was excited to go to the house of the Lord (Psalm 122:1), but a lot of Christians have lost that. He says some are late because they do not want to spend more minutes in church than they have to, “or we just lost our desire for Jesus.”
Can the church change the Bible to match public opinion?
He says no. “You can’t change the Scriptures because public policy says that these things are okay,” and the church has to preach the Bible whether young people like it or not.
Does wearing a suit matter in church?

He says no. He wore a suit for two months because the book said suits turn young people off, but “a suit does not change me in any way or any shape,” and “people don’t come to church because you wear a suit.”
What does a Big Mac have to do with church?

He says a Big Mac is identical in Salvador, Brazil, Korea, China and every state: “They didn’t change the Big Mac.” In the same way, he says, the Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same in every church, but in America “we confuse everybody.”
Why did Paul confront division first in the Corinthian church?

He notes that Paul had just described the Corinthians as a very good church, yet division was the first thing he corrected. The reason, he says, is Jesus’ words in Matthew 12:25: a divided kingdom, city or house will not stand, and a divided people loses the war.
Why do marriages fall apart, even in the church?

He says it happens when husband and wife go two different ways. They start getting different beliefs, their actions come out of those beliefs, and then there is conflict in the home. He says a husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards.
How can parents show their children Jesus?

He says children need to see it lived, not just hear it: “not just telling their children about Jesus, but showing them in their life.” They need to see their parents in unity around Jesus and truth, especially the morals of the Bible, with their tongue speaking rightly and their anger curbed.
Should I tell people when I disagree with something at church?

He says that when we disagree with something going on in the church or with some brother, we go out and tell everybody in the world, “and it just weakens the church more.” He points instead to making decisions that are right and backed up by the Word of God (John 7:24).
What does “I am of Paul, I am of Apollos, I am of Christ” mean?

He explains that in Corinth there were four groups, “I’m of Paul,” “of Apollos,” “of Peter,” and “of Christ,” and only one is right: the Christ group. Paul asks “Is Christ divided?” and he says our unity is in Christ, in unity with his Father and the Scriptures, not in our church’s opinions or our own.
Can a pope, a priest or a denomination save you?

He uses Paul’s question, was Paul crucified for you, to ask whether the Pope can save Catholics, whether Pentecostals who speak in tongues can save Pentecostals, and whether Baptists can save people. His answer is no. He says the focus is “Christ and the Scriptures,” not a church name, a church group or some minister.
He says yes: “Jesus is God. If you know Jesus, you know God.” He says the Mormons do not believe that, and neither do the Muslims, “and that’s a big problem.”
What does he say water baptism is for?

He says Jesus cleansed us from sin through water baptism. He points to Jesus going down to the river and being baptized, with people baptized, “submerged in water,” and says John baptized for the remission of sin, “the cleansing, the forgiveness of sin.”
