p: In “Division Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues through 1 Corinthians 1–2 and says unity is found in the power of God and the Spirit, not in excellent speaking, intellect or a favorite minister. He tells of his own changed life at the altar, why he recommends the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and why God has no grandchildren. He says we need God every day and not only in an emergency, and that love is spelled T-I-M-E.
Why do people call the gospel foolishness?

He says Jesus is a stumbling block to the Jews because they wanted a sign, and to the Gentiles it is “foolishness because they’re looking for total intellect,” just human reasoning rather than spiritual or scriptural reasoning. He says the preaching of Jesus Christ, the gospel and the cross is what saved him: “He died for me.”
Why do people call the gospel foolishness?

So, where’s the power of God and the preaching of Jesus Christ, the Gospel, and the cross? And folks, that’s what saved me. He convicted me. He died for me. If he died for me to forgive me, then I owe him something. I have a debt to show my appreciation by what? Living for him. And if I fall, I get back up, admit it, and keep going. The Jews require a sign, and the Gentiles [unclear] intellect, and the Jews see Jesus as a stumbling block because they want a sign, and he didn’t give them any sign but the death and burial and resurrection. So Jesus is a stumbling block to the Jews who have their own opinion on how this is going to work out. And the Gentiles, it’s foolishness because they’re looking for total intellect, just total human reasoning, not spiritual reasoning, not scriptural reasoning, human reasoning. And so they go, oh, this is nonsense. How can anybody be born of a virgin? How can anybody, you know, be raised from the dead?
Why do people call the gospel foolishness?

1 Corinthians 1:22-24: For Jews request a sign, and Greeks seek after wisdom; but we preach Christ crucified, to the Jews a stumbling block and to the Greeks foolishness, but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
Should we look to ministers or to Jesus?

He says Paul calls Jesus our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption, and the others were “nothing but messengers.” He says the American church looks to ministers and church groups instead of Christ, and people go to the church “where they’re comfortable, where their toes aren’t stepped on.” But you can go to a lousy church, look for Jesus, find him and be changed.
Should we look to ministers or to Jesus?

This is foolishness. So you’ve got to have scriptural reasoning, spiritual reasoning. And then Paul says, Jesus is our wisdom, our righteousness, sanctification, our power, our redemption, and our glory, our honor. Do we agree with that? Yeah. So what does Paul have to do with it? What does Apollos and Priscilla and Peter, what do they have to do with it? Nothing but messengers, get out of the way, give me Jesus. And what is the American church looking to? The people, they’re looking to ministers. They’re looking to a church group. Instead of Christ and the power of the gospel, we’re looking to somebody. Even people will say, we need a leader to be raised up. We need Jesus to arise in our lives. And people go to the church where they’re comfortable, where their toes aren’t stepped on, and, you know, they got the music and whatever. And, you know, they go and they leave the same way that they came. And that’s because that’s what Christians choose to do. You know, you can go to a lousy church and look for Jesus and find him and be changed because he will meet you no matter where you’re at. And you can wind up being a force in that church.
Should we look to ministers or to Jesus?
1 Corinthians 1:30: But of Him you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God—and righteousness and sanctification and redemption—
Does it take great speaking to change lives?

He says unity is in the power of God and the Spirit, “not the excellent intellectual speaking.” Even Apollos, who could speak, lacked the fullness of the message until Priscilla and Aquila came along. The only demonstration of the Spirit and power we have seen so far, he says, is “salvation and changed lives.”
Does it take great speaking to change lives?

Okay. I’m going to have to stop in the middle of this message because I don’t want to wear you out. We’re in a conference and we’ve got to have a break. Conferences have breaks. We can pick up this message next week. But unity, number four statement he makes, unity is in the power of God and the spirit, not the excellent intellectual speaking. It doesn’t matter if I went to college and learned how to speak intellectually and excellently. It doesn’t matter if I graduated from Toastmasters with the greatest honor and I can really speak. See, Apollos could speak. He had the Toastmasters ability to speak, but he lacked the fullness of the message till Priscilla and Aquila came along and enlarged his ability to speak the truth. He was limited in the truth he spoke. “I declared not God’s mystery with excellent speech, but in weakness, in fear and much trembling. In demonstration of the spirit and power.” So far, the only demonstration of the spirit and power we’ve seen is salvation and changed lives. These people were holy. They were pursuing moral blamelessness. They were fellowshipping with Jesus. These people were very powerful. And so the demonstration of the power is what these Corinthians’ changed lives, from homosexuality, adultery, prostitution, slavery, slave masters, all this debauchery that was going on. The power he’s talking about is the changed life. When I was young, they convinced me that we’re going to reach the world. We need miracles. And we need the [unclear]. My group had convinced me till God changed my thinking that we needed the gifts operating. But here in this church, we see the power of the spoken word, don’t we? And Christ backing up his word. Hallelujah.
Does it take great speaking to change lives?

1 Corinthians 2:1-5: And I, brethren, when I came to you, did not come with excellence of speech or of wisdom declaring to you the testimony of God. For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified. I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling. And my speech and my preaching were not with persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power, that your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God.
Can God really change a person?

He says he went to the altar and “really experienced salvation,” then was baptized in water and “the presence of God came on me and it scared me to death.” After he was filled with the Holy Ghost, he says, he left church that night “in love with everybody.” He says “the power of God is real” and “we keep changing.”
Can God really change a person?

And that’s what changed me, folks. I went to that altar and I really experienced salvation. It was real. These people weren’t lying to me. Two weeks later or one week later, I got baptized in water and the presence of God came on me and it scared me to death. I had never felt anything like that before. My goodness, I did [unclear] because I was resisting. What in the world is going on? One week after that or two weeks after [unclear], I was filled with the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues because that’s what they emphasize. And, you know, when you experience these things, it’s real. The power of God is real. He backs up what he says. And I remember leaving the church that night in love with everybody. I didn’t have any enemies. That Holy Spirit just made me fall in love with Jesus and the church and everybody. A changed person. And we keep changing. When we keep pursuing, we keep what? Changing.
Why does he recommend the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

He says your faith is “not in the wisdom of man, but in the power of God,” when the Spirit “ignites it in me and makes it real to me.” He highly recommends the baptism of the Holy Ghost and Spirit-filled churches “in spite of our problems and our extremism,” because they look for the presence of Christ, which can change you if you let it.
Why does he recommend the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

Number four is repeated again in this verse. Your faith is not in the wisdom of man, but in the power of God. What the Holy Spirit teaches. What what teaches? The Holy Spirit. So it’s not what Schuller [unclear] says. It’s not what [unclear] or Robert[unclear] says or Billy Graham says. It’s what they say and the Spirit ignites it in me and makes it real to me. That’s when I hear. That Holy Spirit is important. I keep telling you, I highly recommend the baptism of the Holy Ghost. I highly recommend the Spirit filled churches in spite of our problems and our extremism and all the rest. I highly recommend them because on a consistent basis, they’re looking for the presence of Christ, the presence of the Holy Spirit, which can change you if you let it, or it can just be an emotional experience that, you know, you don’t, you don’t change.
Why does he recommend the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
1 Corinthians 2:5: that your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God.
What is the difference between feeling God’s presence and being filled with the Holy Ghost?

He tells of a priest who said he was filled with the Holy Ghost, and says he told him “you experienced the presence of God,” but the Holy Ghost “comes within you and pours out of you. There’s a big difference.” We need to be filled, controlled and influenced by it from within, he says, and with that power “I don’t have to disfellowship people” because “I know who I am.”
What is the difference between feeling God’s presence and being filled with the Holy Ghost?

I told you before, I met a priest that said he was, in fact, I invited him to speak in the church. He said he was filled with the Holy Ghost and preached a good message. After the service, I was talking to him, he used profanity, he lit up a cigarette, and I go, sir, do you know the first name of the Spirit? He looks at me. What? The first name of the Spirit, first name of the Ghost. What is it? Holy. I go, yeah. How can you talk like that? How can you do these things? I said, tell me exactly how you got filled with the Holy Ghost. He said, well, I went down to the Anaheim Convention Center and there’s 10,000 Catholics in there. You know, there’s charismatic Catholics, you know, worshiping God and the presence of God was there. I go, yes, that’s exactly it. You experienced the presence of God. The Holy Ghost comes within you and pours out of you. There’s a big difference. Can I hear an amen? I said, you haven’t been filled with the Holy Ghost. And he’s looking at me, but he knew I was right. He experienced the presence of the Spirit, but we need to be what? Filled with it, controlled by it, influenced by it. From within, it needs to come out from within. It’s powerful, church. I tell you, that’s where you get power to think right, and act right and get up from your stupid actions and repent, really, and get in control of your life. That Holy Ghost drives you to be like Jesus and empowers you to do it. And so Paul is telling us what? Unity should be around the power, whether it’s Christ, whether it’s his gospel, whether it’s his death, burial and resurrection. It should be in the power, not in intellectual thinking and opinions. If the power is not working in my life, I’m missing it. And see, when I have the power, I don’t have to disfellowship people. I know who I am. I know where I’m going. They can talk about me. They can belittle me. They can be in a total different camp than I am at, and it doesn’t affect me. Why? Because I have power. I know who I am. I know who Christ is. And I know I was where they were at at one time. Are you there? I was just like them at one time. And Christ kept changing me.
Should you read the Bible with your mind or with the Holy Spirit?

He says the Holy Spirit “is what opens the Scriptures to you,” so when you read and study you should “lean on that Holy Spirit, not your mental intellect.” He says he has to make a transition from his natural mind to the mind of the Spirit, and that Jesus and the Holy Spirit are each a separate work in your life “and yet they’re all the same.”
Should you read the Bible with your mind or with the Holy Spirit?

The Holy Spirit, the Bible says is what opens the Scriptures to you. And when you read it and study it, you need to lean on that Holy Spirit, not your mental intellect. The natural man receives not the things of the Spirit, but he that is spiritual, judges, determines, examines all things. See, Dave Kincer has to make a transition from his natural mind to the mind of the Spirit, from his natural person to the person of the Spirit, Jesus. You can’t separate the Holy Ghost from Jesus. They’re separated in the Bible so that we understand more and all that. And the Trinity really explains it. But just knowing the word Trinity doesn’t work. See, Jesus is a separate work in your life. And the Holy Spirit is a separate work in your life. And yet they’re all the same. You say, how can that be? He is God. He’s supernatural.
Should you read the Bible with your mind or with the Holy Spirit?

1 Corinthians 2:14-15: But the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; nor can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. But he who is spiritual judges all things, yet he himself is rightly judged by no one.
Why does he say Paul has more credibility than modern authors?

He says Paul got saved five years after Christ ascended, wrote his epistles less than twenty years after, and mingled with Peter, John and Luke. “He’s got more credibility than any of these book authors,” he says, and more than any church growth seminar. Paul “used nothing but the scriptures and reasoning,” and then Christ backed it up.
Why does he say Paul has more credibility than modern authors?

And so we’ve got eight more points that Paul is going to bring out. And I’m purposely stopping because we need to get this stuff. And we can continue next week. But this is the Apostle Paul talking. This is a guy that got saved five years after Christ died on the cross and ascended. This is a guy that wrote these epistles just less than 20 years after Christ ascended. This is the guy that mingled with Paul, I mean with Peter and John and Luke and these guys that were with Christ. And I submit to you, he’s got more credibility than any of these book authors. He’s got more credibility than any of these church growth seminars you can go to. That’s why I said we’re at a church growth seminar conference. How to start a church, how to develop a church and how to govern a church. Because we need to get this stuff in us. And he used nothing but the scriptures and reasoning to get this done. And then Christ came in and backed it up. And he’s trying to get them to focus on the power, not people, not ministers, not a group.
Can your church, your denomination or a minister save you?

He says the problem in America is “my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I’m a Baptist, don’t bug me,” and the same with Catholics. Catholics, Baptists, Pentecostals and Jews “can’t save you,” he says, but “Jesus Christ can.” He says to put your confidence on Jesus and the gospel, because “you cannot undermine the power of the cross.”
Can your church, your denomination or a minister save you?

The problem in America is if my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I’m a Baptist, don’t bug me. If my granddad was a Catholic and my dad was a Catholic and I’m a Catholic, don’t bug me. No, you don’t focus. Catholics can’t save you, Baptists can’t save you, Pentecostals can’t save you, Jews can’t save you, they can’t change you, Jesus Christ can. You need to get your confidence out of that group and onto Jesus and the gospel and that’s a good place for an amen. You need to get your confidence in these ministers, [unclear], Jakes and [unclear] and [unclear] and all these people and get your confidence on who? Jesus Christ. You need to be seekers, not of ministers and a church group, you need to be seekers of who? Jesus and his gospel and that cross. Everywhere I go I tell people you cannot undermine the power of the cross, the death of Christ. There’s no sin, it can’t forgive. There’s no Christian that backslid that he can’t restore. There’s such power in the cross that I never got saved again. I kept getting changed. I kept getting corrected but I never answered another salvation altar call. Hallelujah.

He says ministers can be wrong, and if you are trying to please a minister, your dad or your mom, remember “God does not have grandchildren. He does not have stepchildren. He has children.” You have to be born again and have “that initial first contact with him,” he says, and “I can’t use my parents for an excuse on judgment day.”

And ministers can be wrong. And if I’m trying to please a minister or I’m trying to please my dad or my mom, how many of you know God does not have grandchildren. He does not have stepchildren. He has children. In other words, you got to get born again by him. You got to have that initial first contact with him. I can’t use my parents for an excuse on judgment day. I can’t use my church or the minister on judgment day because I’m accountable to find him and serve him and follow him. Amen. And so Paul is hitting division. Is division a big problem in America? Yes. Are we losing the battle and one of the main reasons is the church is so divided? Yes. We’re preaching our own opinions. We’re acting the way we want.
John 3:3: Jesus answered and said to him, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

He says that after 9/11 the churches filled with people praying, but within 60 days they were empty again, because people “think God is only good for an immediate necessity.” In his own emergency, he says, he had already put in his prayer time, and he did not need “a healer to come in here. I need the healer. Jesus.”

And then we want God. 9/11 came and the churches were filled with people praying. See, that’s how quickly God can change things. But did it last? No. 60 days. Churches were empty again. Why? They think God is only good for an immediate necessity. And that God will be there at the snap of their finger. And they are totally wrong. We need him every day of our life. You see. I had a tragic come in my life and somebody says, man, you know, do you pray and what do you do? I said, I just do what I always do. I just live my life. I’ve already put in my prayer time for this emergency. I don’t need to call no 24 heartline. I don’t need to get frustrated. I don’t need to get depressed. I have done what I’m supposed to do. And all I got to do is just keep doing it. When I was dying in that hospital, they’d ask me these things. And I go, you know, I don’t need a healer to come in here. I need the healer. Jesus. I’m not panicked. Why, I’ve done what I was supposed to do. And I’m in his hands. He makes the decisions. I don’t have to get holy water or some magical formula. You know, people tried to get me to get into this magical formula for healing. I said, ain’t no magical formula for healing. He either heals you, or he doesn’t. He’s the healer. You ask him, he responds, or you die. We all got to die. Well, aren’t you depressed? Aren’t you worried? What am I going to [unclear]? Either I die today or would have died 20 years from now. I’ve got to die. I’ve got to face it today or I’ve got to face it later. And what’s the problem?
Can you call on God and expect him to come?

He says we shouldn’t settle for a service or a prayer time without him, and should say, “you said if I drew nigh to you, you’d draw nigh to me.” He says God is “more than glad to respond to the summons,” though “he doesn’t come except in his sovereign times.” He adds that when God summons us to assemble, pray and seek his word, we have to put it in our schedule.
Can you call on God and expect him to come?

But see, that’s what the Holy Ghost and the Word will do for you. And I’m sharing that with you. That’s the power. When you need it, it’s there. It’s there because you’ve been there. Now, how many could use a little holiness in your life? A little sainthood in your life where you are striving for moral blamelessness? A little fellowship with Jesus daily? Yeah. A little summoning Christ. Quit calling on him. But saying, hey, bud, you said you would come. I’m summoning you. I’m serving you papers. Get here. We need you. Without you, we’re nothing. And not settle for a service that doesn’t have him. Or a prayer time when you go in your closet at home. Don’t settle for him not coming. Say, hey, boy, you said if I drew nigh to you, you’d draw nigh to me. You said if I come to church and assembled, you would be there. We summon you. And he’s what? More than glad to respond to the summons. But when you just go, Jesus, would you please come? Jesus, we love you. Jesus, help me. You know, we don’t expect him to come. We don’t demand him to come. He doesn’t come except in his sovereign times. Hallelujah. But when you’re summoned, you never miss it, do you? You know the penalty of not answering a summons. Well, maybe you haven’t been summoned. I’ve been summoned. Let me tell you, it’s not fun getting that paper. I know I got to put it in my schedule. And how many of you know he’s summoning you to assemble together? And you got to put it in your schedule. Wow, that’s hot stuff. He’s summoning you for a prayer time. And you got to put it in your schedule. He’s summoning you to seek his word. And you got to put it into your schedule. If you want him to respond when you want him to respond, then you ought to back it up by what? You’re responding when he wants you to respond. Now that’s good stuff.
Can you call on God and expect him to come?
James 4:8: Draw near to God and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners; and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
Do we need the power of God, or just the motions?

He asks how many of us need to be speaking the same thing, with no division and making right judgments. He asks how many need to “possess the power” and not just lean on messages we have heard: “we just go through the motions when we need the power.”
Do we need the power of God, or just the motions?

Hallelujah. How many of us need to be speaking the same thing? And no division. Making right judgments. See, how many of us need to possess the power? And not just lean on, well, I’ve heard Moses’ tabernacle. I’ve heard David’s tabernacle. I’ve heard the cross message. And we just go through the motions when we need the power.
Do we need the power of God, or just the motions?

1 Corinthians 1:10: Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

He says you won’t get the power watching TV, and sports and recreation don’t give it either: he finds it “spending time with the sources of power.” Love, he says, is not only spelled L-O-V-E, “it’s spelled T-I-M-E,” and if he says he loves God he will spend time with him. He adds that he cannot separate love for Christ from love for his people.

And you’re not going to get the power watching TV. And I watch TV. But I tell you, don’t give me the power. I have to shut that thing off and find time for God. See, sports don’t give me the power. Recreation doesn’t give me the power. I need recreation, and the Bible emphasizes recreation. But I’m not going to find my power there. I’m going to find my power, spending time with the sources of power. I was telling my daughter yesterday, love is not only spelled L-O-V-E, it’s spelled T-I-M-E. If I say I love something, I will spend time with it. Am I correct? If I say I love my children, I’ll spend time with them. If I say I love God, I’ll spend time with him. And love is also, I cannot separate love for Christ from love for his people. And love is also,
Why did he stop in the middle of the message?
He says he doesn’t want to wear them out: they are in a conference, and conferences have breaks. He says they can pick up the message next week, and that Paul has eight more points to bring out.
Who was Apollos, according to this message?

He says Apollos could speak and “had the Toastmasters ability to speak,” but he lacked the fullness of the message until Priscilla and Aquila came along and enlarged his ability to speak the truth. “He was limited in the truth he spoke.”
What kind of changed lives did Paul’s preaching bring about in Corinth?

He says the power Paul talks about is the changed life. These people were pursuing moral blamelessness and fellowshipping with Jesus, and he says the Corinthians’ lives were changed from homosexuality, adultery, prostitution, slavery, slave masters and all the debauchery that was going on.
Is being filled with the Spirit just an emotional experience?
He says the presence of Christ and of the Holy Spirit can change you if you let it, “or it can just be an emotional experience that, you know, you don’t, you don’t change.”
What does he say the Holy Ghost does for you?
He says that is where you get power to think right and act right, to repent and get in control of your life. “That Holy Ghost drives you to be like Jesus and empowers you to do it.”
Does having God’s power mean you have to cut people off?

He says no: “when I have the power, I don’t have to disfellowship people. I know who I am.” People can talk about him or belittle him, he says, and it doesn’t affect him, because he has power and knows who Christ is.
What does he say we should be seekers of?
He says we should be seekers not of ministers and a church group but of “Jesus and his gospel and that cross.”
Is there any sin the cross can’t forgive?

He says you cannot undermine the power of the cross, the death of Christ: “There’s no sin, it can’t forgive.” He also says there is no Christian who backslid that he can’t restore, and that he himself never got saved again but kept getting changed and corrected.
Is division a big problem in America?
He says yes, and that we are losing the battle, and one of the main reasons is the church is so divided. He says we are preaching our own opinions and acting the way we want.
What does he say he did when a tragedy came?

He says he did what he always does: he lived his life, because he had already put in his prayer time for the emergency. He didn’t need to get frustrated or depressed, he says, because all he had to do was keep doing what he was supposed to do.
Does he say there is a magical formula for healing?

He says he doesn’t have to get holy water or some magical formula. People tried to get him into a magical formula for healing, he says, and he told them there is none: “He either heals you, or he doesn’t. He’s the healer.”
Why does he compare God’s call to a summons?

He says when you are summoned, “you never miss it,” and you put it in your schedule. He says God is summoning us to assemble together, to pray and to seek his word, and if we want him to respond when we want, we should respond when he wants.
Can you separate love for Christ from love for his people?
He says he cannot separate love for Christ from love for his people. The video ends as he begins to say more about love.

items.ser: The Corinthians series · Division Concluded, Part 1
p: In “Division Concluded Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer finishes the section of 1 Corinthians (chapter 4) where Paul deals with division. He contrasts how the Corinthians saw themselves with how real ministers lived, and lists Paul’s sufferings. Paul answers insults with good words, works with his own hands and asks for unity even when picked on. He says Paul wants fathers rather than mere talkers, and that the goal of the gospel is Christ formed in you.
What was wrong in the Corinthian church?

He says Paul spent the first four chapters of the letter on division, warning the Corinthians about their proud, arrogant thinking. They were saying “I’m of Paul, I’m of Apollos, I’m of Peter,” and only one fourth had it right: “we’re of Jesus.” He adds that they were quarreling, jealous, carnal, and still “on the milk” after several years.
What was wrong in the Corinthian church?

This is the words of Paul the Apostle. He got saved about five years after Christ died on the cross and ascended and he started preaching in Corinth in about 52 A.D. and wrote the letters in about 57. So, we are picking it up in chapter four. The first four chapters are focusing on division and he’s still addressing divisional members of the Corinthian church. He continues to warn them or alert them about their proud, arrogant thinking. Remember, they were saying, “I’m of Paul, I’m of Apollos, I’m of Peter,” and one fourth said, “We’re none of those guys, we’re of Jesus.” One fourth of the people had it right. Okay, three fourths had it wrong. And remember, he got them for quarreling, being splitting and dividing into groups, being jealous of one another, thinking like a natural man instead of a spiritual man, being carnal, being babies and on the milk. After these several years, he said, you’re still on milk. You should be taking meat. And he says, you judge other ministers and other believers that you do not approve of. That’s what we read in the past three chapters.

He says that when we distract from Jesus Christ and the power of the gospel, “the source of growth,” we stop growing. He adds that pride in our own beliefs and gifts crowds out the One who gave them: “if you receive them, what do you got to brag about?”

And with motives that elevate your own pride in your beliefs, in your gifts that you receive from Christ. And remember, he said, if you receive them, what do you got to brag about? It’s the one that gave you these things that should be the one you’re praising. Remember all that? And he said, you’re distracting from Jesus Christ and the power of the gospel that gives you growth. And when we distract from the source of growth, how many of you know we stopped growing? Yeah. It’s not the church group. It’s not the minister. It’s Jesus, his gospel and the cross. That’s the power of God that changes our life causes us to grow.
1 Corinthians 4:7: For who makes you differ from another? And what do you have that you did not receive? Now if you did indeed receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
What does “you are full, you are rich, you reign as kings without us” mean?

He says Paul is comparing the Corinthians’ opinion of themselves with how real ministers of God lived. In their own minds they were strong and full and had authority, and Paul says he wishes they did, “so we could have that authority with you to rule as kings.”
What does “you are full, you are rich, you reign as kings without us” mean?

Now, Paul is going to compare them in this verse eight and nine and the following verses. He’s going to compare their evaluation of themselves with real ministers of God. Did you hear that statement? He’s going to compare the two, the real ministers of God and their evaluation of themselves. Peter, Paul, Apollos and Jesus. They were the real ministers. So he says, you are full, you are rich, you reign as kings without us. And I would to God that you did reign, that we might reign with you. He says, in your mind, you are strong, you are full, you know, you don’t have any need. You have authority. He said, I wish you did have that authority. So we could have that authority with you to rule as kings.
What does “you are full, you are rich, you reign as kings without us” mean?
1 Corinthians 4:8: You are already full! You are already rich! You have reigned as kings without us—and indeed I could wish you did reign, that we also might reign with you!
Who is greatest in God’s kingdom?

He says everybody wants to be “the top dog,” but in the kingdom the one who serves the most is the one who has the authority, and recognition works differently there. Paul says the apostles were put last, “a spectacle” to the whole world, while the Corinthians thought they had it all together.
Who is greatest in God’s kingdom?

He says, I think that God has set us apostles first or last. See, everybody wants to be first. Everybody’s wanting to be the top dog. In the kingdom, Jesus said, he that is greatest is servant of all, the lowest person. In the kingdom is one that serves the most and they are the one that has the authority. And the recognition works different in the kingdom. He says, us apostles are last. We’re appointed to death, ruin, for we are made a spectacle, a theater to the whole world, to the angels and to men. He says, but not you guys. You think you are full, you know, of food, you don’t need anything materially, you don’t need anything spiritually, you know, you’re rich, you don’t need anything materially, you don’t need anything spiritually. You guys in your mind, you got it together and us apostles are all wrong or our ministers are all wrong.
Who is greatest in God’s kingdom?
1 Corinthians 4:9: For I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last, as men condemned to death; for we have been made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to men.

He says the world thinks of real ministers as fools with no common sense, such as Peter and John, who gave up a good fishing business to preach the gospel. Paul says “we are fools for Christ’s sake,” thought of that way “because we choose to put Christ first.” He calls that the mentality of people who divide.

Verse 10, he says, you think of us and so does the world as fools, as foolish people with no common sense. You know, Peter and John gave up a good fishing business to go and preach the gospel. Well, that’s crazy. There’s no common sense. You do that to preach the gospel. You take a, you stop a good paying job like some have here in the church and take a low paying job at the church because you got a compassion for people to reach them with the gospel. You are an idiot. Yeah, that’s no common sense. See, that’s the way divisors, divisionary people think they got the answers and real ministers are just idiots. And we are fools for Christ’s sake. We are thought of as fools because we choose to put Christ first and the things that he puts first first. He says, you look at us as weak, no great achievers. Yeah, we’re not out there making money. Yeah, we’re not out there, you know, being a hero in sports or a hero in the music industry or, you know, all this. You say we’re not achievers. Is this good? Yeah. And that’s the mentality of people that divide. We got to put down the real people.
1 Corinthians 4:10: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ! We are weak, but you are strong! You are distinguished, but we are dishonored!
How much did Paul suffer for the gospel?

He lists what Paul went through: hunger, thirst, cold, beatings, prison, a stoning, three shipwrecks and dangers from bandits and false brethren. On top of it all, Paul says, “I face daily the pressures of my concern for the churches.”
How much did Paul suffer for the gospel?

He says, we’re despised. We’re looked down on without any honor. We get no respect. We hunger, we thirst, we are, we, we, we are naked. We go without clothing. We’re cold because we don’t have clothing to warm us. We’re beaten. And in Second Corinthians 11:23 through 28, he says. Are they servants of Christ, ministers of Christ? He says, I am more and I feel like an idiot talking like this, but I work harder. I’ve been in prison more frequently. I’ve been flogged or beaten more severely. I’ve been exposed to death again and again. Five times the Jews beat me. Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a day and a night in the sea. I have been constantly on the move. I’ve been in dangers from rivers, from bandits, from my own countrymen, from the Gentiles, from in the city, in the country, in the sea, and false brethren. I have labored and toiled and have gone without sleep. I have known hunger and thirst and have often gone without food. I have been cold and naked. And besides all of this natural stuff, I face daily the pressures of my concern for the churches.
How much did Paul suffer for the gospel?

1 Corinthians 4:11: To the present hour we both hunger and thirst, and we are poorly clothed, and beaten, and homeless. 2 Corinthians 11:23-28: Are they ministers of Christ?—I speak as a fool—I am more: in labors more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequently, in deaths often. From the Jews five times I received forty stripes minus one. Three times I was beaten with rods; once I was stoned; three times I was shipwrecked; a night and a day I have been in the deep; in journeys often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils of my own countrymen, in perils of the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren; in weariness and toil, in sleeplessness often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness— besides the other things, what comes upon me daily: my deep concern for all the churches.
How do ministers today compare with New Testament ministers?

He says Paul and the apostles were taken to court, jailed and rejected, and did not stay at “the Hilton hotel.” He says some treat a new car and a nice house as the sign a church is successful, but Paul’s saying that “has nothing to do with anything. It’s the power of the gospel that has to do with everything.”
How do ministers today compare with New Testament ministers?

Quite a lot different than these TV and radio evangelists, huh? They’re not suffering anything. In fact, they’re living high off God’s people’s money. With a gospel that isn’t changing people’s lives. You see, where do you hear anybody preaching? If you’re really going to be a minister, they’re going to take you to court. They’re going to put you in jail. They’re going to reject you. They’re not going to have anything to do with you. You don’t hear that. You said, “No, man, you be a minister. You’re the man of God.” You know, nothing’s too good for the man of God. But it didn’t happen back there. Are you with me? If we compared ministers today to ministers in the New Testament, it’s a big difference. You know, our pastors today are successful if they got a new car. See, if the congregation buys them a new car, you know, and they got a nice house to live in and nice clothes. You know, that’s a sign that the church is successful. Paul’s saying that has nothing to do with anything. It’s the power of the gospel that has to do with everything. Isn’t this good? And this is Paul talking. This is not your modern day church growth seminar teachers. This is Paul talking. He says, this is the way you look at us because we are experiencing these things. We don’t even have a place to live in. We got to sleep wherever people will give us a room or we have to sleep on the ground. They didn’t stay at the Hilton hotel. Like we hear today. But you’re wise. You think you are intelligent in Christ. You think you’re strong in body and mind. You think you’re honorable.
Should a pastor work with his own hands?

He says Paul and the true ministers “labor with our own hands” and use their own money to reach people with the gospel. “If the church can’t support us, we work to keep the gospel moving,” he says, though some churches would object to seeing their pastor dig a ditch or paint a wall.
Should a pastor work with his own hands?

And you put us down. Verse 12. Now he’s saying the facts. Us true ministers. We labor with our own hands. Even above paying our own tithes. We use our money to reach people with the gospel. We don’t stop at tithe. And if the church can’t support us, we work to keep the gospel moving. Isn’t that beautiful? My goodness today, if some of these churches saw their pastor digging a ditch at the church to repair something or painting a wall, they go, what are you doing? That’s for a layman.
Should a pastor work with his own hands?

1 Corinthians 4:12-13: And we labor, working with our own hands. Being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we endure; being defamed, we entreat. We have been made as the filth of the world, the offscouring of all things until now.
How should you answer an insult?

He says Paul wrote “we are reviled,” and when we’re spoken evil of, “we give good words back.” He calls that the sign of a real believer: when verbally abused, they speak back kindness and goodness. When mistreated, he adds, “we permit it” and “don’t retaliate back.”
How should you answer an insult?

He says, we are reviled. We’re spoken evil of. And when we’re spoken evil of, we give good words back. Wow. Did you hear that? He says, that’s the sign of a real minister. That’s the sign of a real believer that’s thinking right. Even when they’re spoken evil of and verbally abused, they speak back kindness and goodness. Now I don’t know about you, but this is good stuff. See, this is the power that Paul is talking about, that God used to build the Corinthian church, the power of a moral, living, moral standard lifestyle of living and possessing the characteristics of God. Powerful. He says, we’re persecuted. We’re mistreated. And we permit it. Suffer means we permit it. We allow it. We just keep preaching to them. We just keep speaking the gospel. You know, we don’t retaliate back.
Why do divisive people put other people down?

He says that “we always try to build ourselves by putting down somebody else,” and that is what divisionary people and babies do. Paul’s answer to those who defame him is to ask them to “work together for the gospel,” and he says siding with one minister for your own advantage ends up “distracting from Jesus Christ.”
Why do divisive people put other people down?

We are defamed. Defamation of character. I’ve gone through it several times myself. Nothing they could prove. They just wanted to challenge my character and say things that weren’t true. Defamation of character. We always try to build ourselves by putting down somebody else. He says, that’s what divisionary people do. That’s what babies do. That’s what carnal people do. You have got to come into the spiritual thing of this. We entreat. We encourage these that defame us by saying, come along. Let’s work together for the gospel and the spreading of the kingdom. See, they’re asking for unity even when they are picked on. Has Paul got your attention? Now, is this Christianity? Yeah. This is real Christianity. He says, we’re made as the filth of the world, the offscouring of dirt, casting of dirt off of us like you wash off dirt, of all things, to this day. That’s how you people look at us. And yeah, you’re siding with Paul for your own advantage. You’re siding with Peter for your own advantage. You’re siding for Apollos for your own advantage. But then you in your bad attitude and your bad motives are knocking the other ministers and distracting from Jesus Christ and the power of the gospel. And, church, he’s right. He’s totally right. See, dividers don’t work. They don’t spend their own money above tithes. They probably don’t even tithe to get the gospel out to others. Verse 14, “I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn you.” I warn you, I’m alerting you that kind of thinking, that kind of pride, that kind of motive, that kind of attitude is not good. He said, and I’m here to warn you, I’m here to alert you.
Why do divisive people put other people down?

1 Corinthians 4:14-15: I do not write these things to shame you, but as my beloved children I warn you. For though you might have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.

He says Paul told the Corinthians they had “10,000 tutors in Christ” who just talk, but not many fathers. A father gives life and is also “a parental guide to bring that child up to maturity,” setting aside the time and labor to raise a child through every stage.

While you have 10,000 tutors in Christ, yeah, all you people get together and you tell each other about Jesus and you try to teach each other. He said there’s 10,000 like you, multitudes like you. You just talk. Your motives aren’t right. Your goals aren’t right. You just talk. You use Bible verses and you just talk. You got a lot of these kind of people talking, but you don’t have many fathers. What’s a father? A father is the one that gives life. To a child without the man, the woman’s worthless. The father gives life and the father is also a parental guide to bring that child up to maturity. See, anybody can have kids in the natural, but not anybody sets aside the time and the labor to raise this child up in every stage to be a normal, well -balanced person serving God and asset to the community and providing from their own self when they get an adult. He said, you guys are just talkers. You’re keeping people babies. You’re destroying the church. You need to listen to fathers. Amen. Go to a church because the pastor is going to flatter you. I can’t flatter my kids. I’ve got to be honest with them. This is a world where you got to work and it’s a tough world and it takes discipline and it takes responsibility. It takes an education. It takes a job training in the natural. It takes good hygiene and good eating habits. It takes a lot of things and in the spirit world it’s the same thing. It takes giving time to God, as Stephen said earlier, in prayer and in the Word and changing your life to represent what you read and that presence that comes when you pray. It takes work.

1 Corinthians 4:14-15: I do not write these things to shame you, but as my beloved children I warn you. For though you might have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.
Can the gospel really give you new life?

He says Paul wrote “I have begotten you through the gospel.” Fathers give birth, and “the gospel births.” His own opinions don’t bring life, he says, but if you receive the gospel and embrace it, it gives you “life that keeps growing.”
Can the gospel really give you new life?

Paul’s good, folks. I’ve told you for 40 years, you can’t beat Peter, John and Paul as authors. There is no book that supersedes them. And these other New Testament authors. “I have begotten you through the gospel.” I’ve birthed you. See, Father’s birth, the gospel births. See, my opinions don’t birth. They don’t bring life to you. But the gospel births you. If you will receive it and embrace it, it will give you life that keeps growing.
Are churches stopping new Christians from growing?

He compares conception to the start of a Christian life, with the power to “keep growing into something beautiful and something useful.” He says churches can stop that growth “with doctrines and stupid things,” and that we often “just want to make them feel good” when God’s concern is growing.
Are churches stopping new Christians from growing?

See, when that egg and that sperm come together, that’s just, we call that conception. That’s the beginning of life. But in that beginning, there is the power to just keep growing into something beautiful and something useful. Amen. See, and just like people abort babies today, churches are aborting Christians. We’re killing them. After conception, we’re killing them with doctrines and stupid things. So that they can’t grow anymore. Do you understand that? And the reason we don’t have any sensitivity for the unborn baby is because we don’t have any sensitivity for the Christian. See, Paul said the care of all the churches. We don’t care about people. We just want to make them feel good. Do you feel good about yourself? Are you happy? It’s got nothing to do with feeling good and being happy. It’s got to do with growing. And it’s the gospel, it’s the cross, and it’s Jesus that causes us to grow.
Should you follow a minister, a denomination, or Jesus?

He says that when we distract from the gospel, the cross and Jesus by saying “I’m a Methodist person” or “I’m a Catholic person,” we lose what causes growth. It should always be, “I’m a Jesus boy. I’m a Jesus girl. I’m a gospel man.” Paul can say “Be followers of me,” he says, because Paul follows Christ.
Should you follow a minister, a denomination, or Jesus?

And when you distract from that and say, well, you know, I’m a Vineyard person. I’m a [unclear] person. I’m a Methodist person. I’m a Catholic person. Listen, you should never talk that way. It should always be, “I’m a Jesus boy. I’m a Jesus girl. I’m a gospel man.” Hallelujah. And then he says, “Be followers of me.” And later, in the same book, he’ll say, “Be followers of me as I follow Christ.” He said, don’t follow one another. Don’t follow these little groups. Follow me. I’m a real minister. I am faithful. I have the mysteries of God. I live it. I speak it. And you can follow me. You can follow my lifestyle. You can follow what I teach that I live the lifestyle. Follow me because I’m following Christ.
Should you follow a minister, a denomination, or Jesus?
1 Corinthians 4:16: Therefore I urge you, imitate me. 1 Corinthians 11:1: Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ.
What does it mean for Christ to be formed in you?

He says the objective of the gospel is “to form Christ in you so that you are a light to the world.” The goal isn’t just to be a believer or a disciple, but to let your faith and discipline bring you to where Christ is formed in you. As a young Christian struggling to live for Christ, he says, that gave him “tremendous hope.”
What does it mean for Christ to be formed in you?

And look at this. “My little children,” Galatians 4:19, “of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you.” So what’s the objective of the gospel? To form Christ in you so that you are a light to the world. A city set on a hill that everybody can see that imitates Jesus Christ. See, the goal isn’t to be a believer. The goal isn’t to be a disciple. The goal is to let your faith and your discipline in Christ bring you to where Christ is formed in you. I don’t know about you, but when I read that verse as a young Christian man, that just really gave me tremendous hope because I was struggling living for Christ. And then that Holy Ghost came along. Wow, that was a big boost in my ability to say no to sin and yes to right. And then these scriptures, God is in me and he’s shaping me into himself, so I could accept where I was at while I was pursuing the goal.
What does it mean for Christ to be formed in you?
Galatians 4:19: My little children, for whom I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you,

He says it is the words of Paul the Apostle, who got saved about five years after Christ died on the cross and ascended. Paul started preaching in Corinth in about 52 A.D. and wrote the letters in about 57.
What are the first four chapters of 1 Corinthians about?
He says the first four chapters focus on division. Paul is still addressing the divisional members of the Corinthian church and continues to warn them about their proud, arrogant thinking.
Why does Paul say the Corinthians were still on milk?

He says that after several years they were still on milk when they should have been taking meat. They were quarreling, splitting into groups, being jealous, and judging other ministers and believers they did not approve of.
Is it right to brag about the gifts you have received?
He says Paul’s point is that if you received your gifts from Christ, “what do you got to brag about?” It is the one who gave them who should be praised.
What does Paul mean by “fools for Christ’s sake”?

He says it means being thought of as fools because we choose to put Christ first and the things he puts first. He adds that the world calls such people weak and not great achievers, not out making money or being heroes in sports or music.
What hardships did Paul list in 2 Corinthians 11?

He reads Paul’s list: more labor, more prison, more beatings, five times by the Jews, three times with rods, once stoned, three times shipwrecked, a day and a night in the sea, and many dangers. Besides all this, he says, Paul faced daily the pressure of his concern for the churches.
Is a successful pastor one with a new car and a nice house?

He says that many see a new car, a nice house and nice clothes as a sign a church is successful, but Paul’s saying that has nothing to do with anything. “It’s the power of the gospel that has to do with everything.”
What is defamation of character, and how should you respond?

He describes it as people wanting to challenge your character and say things that weren’t true. He says he has gone through it several times himself, and that Paul’s response was to encourage those who defame, saying “come along. Let’s work together for the gospel.”
Does growing as a Christian take work?

He says it does: he can’t flatter his kids, and in the natural it takes discipline, responsibility, education and job training. In the spirit world it is the same, he says. It takes giving time to God in prayer and in the Word, and changing your life to represent what you read. “It takes work.”
Why does he say no book supersedes Peter, John and Paul?
He says he has told the church for 40 years that you can’t beat Peter, John and Paul as authors. “There is no book that supersedes them.”
Is the goal of church to make people feel good?
He says that is not God’s concern: “It’s got nothing to do with feeling good and being happy. It’s got to do with growing.” He says the gospel, the cross and Jesus are what cause us to grow.
What does Paul mean by “be followers of me”?

He says Paul told them not to follow one another or follow these little groups, but to follow him: “Follow me because I’m following Christ.” Paul is a real minister, he says, who lives and speaks what he teaches.
What is the objective of the gospel?
He says it is to form Christ in you so that you are a light to the world, “a city set on a hill that everybody can see that imitates Jesus Christ.”
How did Galatians 4:19 help him as a young Christian?

He says that as a young Christian man he was struggling to live for Christ, and the verse gave him tremendous hope. Then the Holy Ghost came along, he says, and that was a big boost in his ability to say no to sin and yes to right.
