items.ser: The Corinthians series · Division Concluded, Part 2
p: In “Division Concluded Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer finishes the Corinthians series on division with 1 Corinthians 4:17-21. He uses the Marines to show that unity can be done, says we cannot pick and choose in church, and says the kingdom of God is in power, not words. He says Christians should unite around Jesus, the gospel and the cross rather than argue over details, and he closes by asking how we can tell a real minister, and what each member can contribute.
Why does the church need to teach the same gospel everywhere?

He reads that Paul sent Timothy to remind the Corinthians of his ways in Christ “as I teach everywhere in every church.” He says Timothy “didn’t come with his own gospel,” and that he himself needs to be “connected to the real ministers” who are getting a fresh word from God.
Why does the church need to teach the same gospel everywhere?

“I sent Timothy,” verse 17, “my beloved son, and faithful in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, as I teach everywhere in every church.” See, the team member wasn’t out preaching his own message. Are you there, church? You know, I can’t have a little Bible study at home and preach my own little [unclear] of the gospel. See, I need to be connected to the real ministers who are getting this fresh word from God and teaching it, and I pass it on. See, Timothy didn’t come with his own gospel. He come with the same gospel that they had been taken in everywhere in every church.
Why does the church need to teach the same gospel everywhere?
1 Corinthians 4:17: For this reason I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful son in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, as I teach everywhere in every church.
Can Christians really be united, like a military?

He uses the military as an example: everyone is given “the same book” and the same code of conduct, they work together, and they leave no one behind, though Marines come from “all walks of life.” He says that if the secular world can do it, “the church world can surely do it.”
Can Christians really be united, like a military?

And I use the military as an example. You know, they give you a code of conduct, and they give you rules to, you know, have to be in the military by, to win wars by, and all the rest. And one isn’t given a different book than the other. They’re all given the same book. They all have the same code of conduct. And so they work together, and that’s how they win wars. And no one is left behind. They fight for their wounded. They get them out of there. Even their dead bodies, they want to take them back, give respect and honor. And the church needs to learn this stuff. I’m giving you this because if the secular world can do it, the church world can surely do it. Amen? People say unity can’t happen. Well, the world does it. Corporations do it. Militaries do it. I was going to read you the Marine Code of Conduct. It’s very powerful at the end. It says your faith is in your God and in your country. You won’t leave anybody behind and you won’t surrender as long as you’ve got any chance of resisting. You don’t surrender and quit. And if you’re captured, you won’t do anything to put your fellow soldiers in danger. You’ll give your life up rather than do anything and say anything that will cause your fellow soldiers to be in danger. Folks, those are good things. And if these blockheaded Marines could do it, surely us Christians could do it. These Marines come from all walks of life. A lot of them dropped out of high school or they come from bad neighborhoods or the country where there is no chance of success. So they went into the military to get some stability in their life or whatever. And the different religions and different cultures and different races and all that. And the Marines put them together and they fight and they work as a team. And they win battles. Hallelujah. So it can be done.
Can you pick and choose in church?

He asks whether a Marine could show up late for reveille or skip calisthenics, and answers “No way.” In church, he says, “we show up when we want to,” and the church has been led to believe “we can pick and choose.” He says that is Paul’s argument: it is the Corinthians’ own prideful thinking, and it cripples those who follow them.
Can you pick and choose in church?

Can you imagine a Marine showing up late for reveille? Can you imagine him skipping calisthenics? Well, I don’t want to do exercises today. Does that work, Marines? No way. But in the church world? We show up when we want to. We get involved in what we want to get involved with and don’t get involved with what we don’t. It’s like Marines can pick and choose. Calisthenics is out. I’ll be the sharpshooter. That’s it. No marching. None of that marching. I don’t believe in marching. It embarrasses me out there. I was raised timid. My culture background just don’t allow that public marching like that. Are you getting my point? But in the church world, we use all these excuses. “Raise my hands? Lift my voice? Oh my God, I wasn’t raised that way.” When they’re out there marching and that drill sergeant tells them to sound out cadence, is there anybody silent? No. They’re all sounding out cadence. They’re in unity. But in the church world, we have been led to believe that we can pick and choose. And this is Paul’s argument. This is what Paul is driving home. It’s your own prideful thinking that makes you want to pick and choose. It’s your own wrong motive. It’s your own wrong attitude. And you’re crippling those that follow you. How are you crippling? They’re not going to grow. I say amen, Paul.
What does “the kingdom of God is not in word but in power” mean?

He says Paul wrote that some were “puffed up,” which means proud, as though he would not come to deal with it. Paul says he will not look at their speech but for the power: “I want to see God growing people, changing people.” Anybody can quote and speak, he says, but not everybody is connected with the gospel and Jesus and the cross to bring results.
What does “the kingdom of God is not in word but in power” mean?

Hallelujah. Hallelujah. He says, “Now some are puffed up, as though I would not come to you.” You know, you’re proud. Puffed up means you’re proud. Paul’s not going to do anything about this. He doesn’t have the authority. He doesn’t have the skills. He says, you know, you guys are proud. I’m over here in Asia. You’re over there and you’re proud and you’re cocky. As though I’m not going to come and deal with this. And that’s the problem. Churches don’t deal with this. See, real ministers will deal with things. To win them all. And so they’re all cocky. And you know, we’re the strong ones. We have the authority. Oh man, we’re it baby. Hallelujah. Paul, he’s gone nuts on him. You know, Paul has gone nuts on him. We’re it. He says, I will come to you shortly. If the Lord will. And I will know not the speech of them that are proud. He said, I’m not going to be looking for your words. He said, I’m going to be looking for the power. What power do you possess? And what power is being manifested that’s causing God’s people to grow because of your prideful opinions? I’m going to be looking for the power. I could [unclear] the least if you can quote some scriptures. I want to see the result. I want to see God growing people, changing people. And how many of you know Paul, like Moses, had the authority to do this? Yeah, he’s taking these people on. He’s taking them on and he’s over in Asia. He said, the kingdom of God is not in word, but in what? Power. Anybody can quote Wesley and Calvin and Oral Roberts and Billy Graham and, you know, all these book writers, Dobson and whatever anybody can quote, anybody can speak. But not anybody is connected with the gospel and Jesus and the cross to bring results because it’s those things that bring results. And it’s those things that we should be united around. Jesus Christ.
What does “the kingdom of God is not in word but in power” mean?

1 Corinthians 4:18-20: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you. But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord wills, and I will know, not the word of those who are puffed up, but the power. For the kingdom of God is not in word but in power.
Is Jesus really the only way?

He says that if someone claims there is another way or another source of truth, “Jesus is the only way.” He points to the Bible saying he is the only way, the only truth and the only life, and says “all roads lead to the same God” is not what Paul would say. Unity, he says, is around Jesus, his gospel, his word and the cross.
Is Jesus really the only way?

And if somebody says there’s another way, I’m sorry, I’m sorry. Jesus is the only way. Somebody says there’s another source of truth. I’m sorry. Muhammad out. Joseph Smith out. Jesus in. Amen. Doesn’t the Bible say he is the only way, the only truth and the only life? Does it say that no man comes unto the Father but by Jesus Christ? Then how can we change this gospel? Paul is saying how can we change it and say, well, you know, all roads lead to the same God and, you know, you’re okay. I’m okay. Everybody’s okay. You’re not. The unity is around Jesus, his gospel, his word and the cross that gives us the right to inherit all of these promises. Amen. He laid down his life. He picked it up again. No man could kill him. That’s the power of the cross and he lives in you. Nobody has more power than Jesus Christ. That’s why a Christian can’t have a demon and a Christian, you know, is not under the influence of Satan because Jesus is in us. He’s the big boss. He’s the power. Hallelujah.
Is Jesus really the only way?
John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
What does living your faith look like?

He points to Tebow, who he says “stands up for the Bible, the moral standards of the Bible.” He says Tebow is “not putting on an act” but is “bowing to the king of his life,” and that when interviewed the first thing he says is “I just want to praise my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” He says Tebow has a right to, because he is living what he believes.
What does living your faith look like?

And this is the God that Tebow talks about. I was asking one with Tebow on their T-shirt: “Do you have the character of Tebow?” Tebow stands up for the Bible, the moral standards of the Bible. Powerful. So he has a right when he Tebows. He’s not putting on an act. He is bowing to the king of his life. And I love it. He’s got more influence in America, in this world, than any preacher that I know of right now. Simply for living for Christ. He gets on TV and they want to interview him about the game. First thing he says, “I just want to praise my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” Hallelujah. And he has a right to because he’s living like Paul did what he believes in.

He sums up that Paul’s team teaches “the same gospel” everywhere, and nobody is teaching anything different than Jesus Christ, his gospel and his cross. He says we should be unified around that, not details about the second coming: “the bottom line is Jesus is coming and he’s coming to judge the world.”

In closing. Let’s sum this up here. My team, Paul says, my and my team’s ways in Christ I teach everywhere. I don’t have a gospel different in Asia than I do in Rome. Or I do for the Jews. The Jews get the same gospel that the people in Turkey get. The people in Iran, the people in Greece get the same gospel. He says, my team teaches the same thing. Nobody’s out there teaching anything different than Jesus Christ, his gospel and his cross. Now folks, shouldn’t we be unified around that? Has nothing to do with the second coming. He’s going to come. I don’t care what your theories are. He’s going to come. And I have tested out every theory. They’re all wrong but mine. No, I’m just kidding. They all have a flaw in them. The bottom line is Jesus is coming and he’s coming to judge the world. So get over it if you’re wrong. And why try to reach details about something that doesn’t matter. Let’s keep the focus on Jesus, the gospel and the cross so people can grow.
Does the way you are baptized matter?

He says we divide over how someone is baptized, but asks “who gives a hoot” whether it is in a creek or a bathtub. “It’s the power of the baptism that makes the thing work,” he says, and you are supposed to come up “a new creature.” He says we can be united around Jesus Christ, his gospel and the cross.
Does the way you are baptized matter?

The way you’re baptized. Who gives a hoot if you’re baptized in the name of Jesus, the Father, Son, the Holy Ghost, or 500 gallons of water, or in a creek, or in a bathtub. Who cares? It’s the power of the baptism that makes the thing work. You are supposed to come up a new creature. Your old man of sin dies in water baptism. Not the method. See, we divide over all this nonsense. But I submit to you today. We can be united around Jesus Christ, his gospel and the cross.
Was Jesus just a good man, or is he God?

He says that “without the cross, we’re doomed,” and that people who say Jesus was just a nice human man are wrong: “He had no sin. That’s not human.” He adds that no human can die and pick their life up again three days later: “He’s supernatural. He is God.”
Was Jesus just a good man, or is he God?

These people that say that Jesus didn’t die, they’re crazy. Without the cross, we’re doomed. And these people that say that Jesus was just a human, nice man. They’re nuts. He had no sin. That’s not human. Are you there? He didn’t have any sin. That’s not normal. And no human can die and pick their life up again three days later. He’s supernatural. He is God. No pride in ministers, in religions, self, or talk. But in the power of God, which is Jesus, the gospel and the cross, that changes life. That sums it up. That is his argument. And I say amen, Paul. I’ve been around a long time. And let me tell you, I say amen. Amen.
What does “shall I come to you with a rod?” mean?

He says Paul is coming, and how he comes depends on their attitude toward his letter: with “a rod of correction,” or, if they correct themselves and focus on Jesus, the gospel and the cross, “in love and in the spirit of meekness.” He adds that since Paul gave one-fourth of the letter to division, it is an important topic for the church today.
What does “shall I come to you with a rod?” mean?

“What will you? Shall I come to you with a rod?” A rod of correction. He said, I’m coming. And your attitude toward this letter I’m writing is going to make the difference in how I’m coming. If I’ve got to come with a rod to correct, I’ll come. Or you can correct yourself and get with the program and start focusing on Jesus, the gospel and the cross. And accept people and love people. And I’ll come to you in love and in the spirit of meekness. Hallelujah. Not a lot of words, just a meek, humble. This is the way of walking in it. Isn’t that right? Now, folks, if he gave one-fourth of this letter to division, isn’t it an important topic? Yes. Is it something the American church needs to address? Is it something we need to confront in our life? Listen to me. I’m going to give you some real nuggets here. Are you ready? You young ones, listen to me.
What does “shall I come to you with a rod?” mean?
1 Corinthians 4:21: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?
How can you tell a real minister?

He says Jesus said, “You’ll know them by their fruits.” He asks whether a real minister would be late for service, ignore worship, prayer and Bible study, or fail to support the church with his actions, his finances and his time. “You’ll know if they’re babies by how they act,” he says.
How can you tell a real minister?

Jesus said, “You’ll know them by their fruits.” Would a real minister be late for service? Would a real minister ignore worship? Prayer? Reading and studying the Bible? Would a real minister substitute anything for the Bible? No. Would a real minister show his care for the church by his actions? Would he support it with his finances? Yes. Would he support it with his time? Yes. By their fruits, you shall what? Know them. You’ll know if they’re babies by how they act. Amen.
How can you tell a real minister?
Matthew 7:20: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.

He asks whether the Bible says “we are all priests unto the Lord,” and says we are a kingdom of priests. We may not be official preachers and ministers, he says, “but we’re all priests to minister to him, to minister to others.” He says a testimony that night showed people getting saved by someone’s life as he lived for Christ.

Now, let me ask you this. Does the Bible say that we are all priests unto the Lord? First Peter, we are a kingdom of priests. We may not be official preachers and official ministers, which is a gift, but we’re all priests to minister to him, to minister to others. See, in that testimony tonight, you notice that people got saved by his sharing and by his life. It wasn’t actually a purposeful thing. It was just a normal thing as he lived for Christ. Wasn’t that good? And see, we can do that. But we got to decide to be people that focus on Jesus, not ministers, not church groups, not our little clique.

1 Peter 2:9: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light;
Does it matter if you show up to church?

He says he comes to church on Friday night because he cares. He has no speaking or singing part, but “the power of one member just being present” is something God uses to touch people’s lives. He says you also don’t understand what God can do “through a simple obedience to his word,” because “he’s the one that causes the growth.”
Does it matter if you show up to church?

You see, I come to church on Friday night because I care. See, I care. I don’t have any speaking part. I don’t have any singing part. But as I was telling someone last week, the power of one member just being present, God uses to touch people’s lives. I said, you don’t understand the power you have just by being in the assembly. Yeah. And you don’t understand the power you have when you lift your hands and you just worship because the Bible says so. You don’t understand what God can do through a simple obedience to his word. See, he’s the one that causes the growth. It’s not you. And if you will contribute, God will empower and cause people to grow.
How can you tell if young people are growing in God?

He says growth shows when they take responsibility, such as cleaning up the room before they leave. It also shows when worship time comes and “they don’t need a lot of coaching”: they get in and worship, and “that’s maturity.” He says they come for Jesus and then enjoy the games and the camaraderie.
How can you tell if young people are growing in God?

Hallelujah. See, we need to know these things so we can size ourselves up. Where am I at? See, like Friday night, when I know these young people are growing, they’ll clean up this room before they leave. So this old man doesn’t have to come in on Sunday morning and clean this room up. And I already see some growth. They’re in the kitchen working. Don’t get me wrong. You know, they’re taking responsibility. They’re doing things that’s great. And the more they grow, the more God’s going to say, hey, be responsible. Don’t wait for that old man to come in here and sweep on Sunday before you leave. Clean this place up. That shows maturity. Amen. That includes us adults. Why should we leave this place dirty for somebody else to come along and clean when we can clean up our mess? Am I talking to the right church? Yeah. Hallelujah. See, I’ll know how young people are growing is when worship time comes, they don’t need a lot of coaching. When it’s time to worship, they just get in and worship. See, that’s maturity. That’s God’s growing. And they don’t come to play games and stuff. They come for Jesus. And then they enjoy the games and stuff. And the camaraderie. Which young people need. You young and [unclear]. Hallelujah. But let me tell you something. They’re here this morning. Look at them. Does that show growth? Yes. Can they grow more? Yes. Yes. See, they could be out doing what other teens are doing on Sunday. But they’re here. And some of you may not like them talking every once in a while in the thing. Actually, leave the discipline to me. Or the youth leaders. We don’t need everybody in the world telling these young Christians and these young teens what to do. Yes. I’m very capable of saying, look at me. Get your attention on me. And I was a teen once. Geez, you know. I was a jitterbug. I couldn’t sit still.
What causes division, and what cures it?

He says Paul has given a very powerful message of unity and division: how to recognize it, and “the cause and the cure of division.” Paul has shown what causes it and what cures it, he says, “and it starts with us.”
What causes division, and what cures it?

I submit to you today that Paul has given us a very powerful message of unity and division. How to recognize it. The cause and the cure of division. He has showed us what causes it. He has showed us what cures it. And it starts with us.
Why did Paul send Timothy to Corinth?

He reads that Paul sent Timothy, “my beloved son, and faithful in the Lord,” to remind the Corinthians of Paul’s ways in Christ, as Paul teaches everywhere in every church. He says the team member wasn’t out preaching his own message.
Why should you be connected to real ministers instead of preaching your own gospel?

He says he can’t just have a little Bible study at home and preach his own version. He needs to be connected to the real ministers who are getting a fresh word from God and teaching it, and then he passes it on.
What does the Marine Code of Conduct say, according to this message?

He says it is very powerful at the end: your faith is in your God and in your country, you won’t leave anybody behind, and you won’t surrender as long as you have any chance of resisting. If captured, you won’t do anything to put your fellow soldiers in danger.
What does “puffed up” mean in 1 Corinthians 4?
He says “puffed up means you’re proud.” The Corinthians were cocky, thinking they were “the strong ones” with the authority, and Paul says he is coming shortly, if the Lord wills.
What will Paul look for when he comes to Corinth?

He says Paul will not be looking for their words but for the power: what power is being manifested that is causing God’s people to grow. “I want to see the result,” he says, God growing and changing people.
Who has more power than Jesus?
He says Jesus laid down his life and picked it up again, and no man could kill him. That is the power of the cross, he says, and “nobody has more power than Jesus Christ.”
Should Christians divide over the second coming?

He says he doesn’t care what your theories are: he’s going to come. “The bottom line is Jesus is coming and he’s coming to judge the world,” and he asks why try to reach details about something that doesn’t matter.
What happens in water baptism, according to this message?
He says you are supposed to come up a new creature, and your “old man of sin dies in water baptism.” He says it is the power of the baptism that makes it work, not the method.
Why does he say division is an important topic?

He says that if Paul gave one-fourth of this letter to division, it is an important topic. He asks whether it is something the American church needs to address and something we need to confront in our own lives.
What does he say about the young people at church?
He says they could be out doing what other teens do on Sunday, but they are here, and asks, “Does that show growth?” He says yes, and that they can grow more.

items.d: In “A More Excellent Way,” preached March 25, 2012, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 12:31–13:13 that love is the more excellent way to the spiritual manifestations. Without love, he says…
p: In “A More Excellent Way,” preached March 25, 2012, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 12:31–13:13 that love is the more excellent way to the spiritual manifestations. Without love, he says, tongues, prophecy, knowledge, faith, giving and even martyrdom are worth nothing. He defines love from 1 Corinthians 13, says everyone in the church has a part and must grow up out of childish things, and says the goal of the commandment is love out of a pure heart.
What does “a more excellent way” mean in 1 Corinthians 12–13?

He says Paul ends 1 Corinthians 12 by saying he will show a more excellent, more superior way to get spiritual manifestations, and that way is love. Without love, he says, tongues of men and angels are like a clanging cymbal, and prophecy, knowledge and all faith without love leave you “nothing.” He gives the man of God in 1 Kings 13 and Solomon as people who had the message or the wisdom but not the love.
What does “a more excellent way” mean in 1 Corinthians 12–13?

And today we’re going to look at this subject, love, the more excellent way to spiritual manifestations. Remember, in 1 Corinthians 12:31, Paul ended that chapter by saying, “Desire the best gifts, and I will show you a more excellent, more superior way to get spiritual manifestations.” And then in 1 Corinthians 13:1 he says, “Though, or if, I speak with tongues of men and angels, but have not love, I am become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.” And if I had someone over there just clang the cymbals together, you know, in about thirty seconds you would go, “You’re driving me nuts. What’s the point?” See, cymbals without anything around them are worthless. And he says that’s people that speak with tongues of men. He describes two kinds of languages here. Tongues is nothing but languages. There’s languages of men, like they spoke on the day of Pentecost, and there are languages of angels. But the key is, love is more important than both of those. In verse two, he says, “If I have prophecy, understand all mysteries, all knowledge, and have all faith, so I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.” I am worthless. I am zero. Now, remember in 1 Kings 13, when the man of God was chosen by God to take a message to the king of Israel, Jeroboam, that God was going to disrespect the bones of the very leaders who chose to worship God out of his method? They used an improper method to worship God. And he told that prophet, “You go and you give the message, and you don’t tarry; you turn around and you come back. Do not stay there.” Well, he gave the great message. He even gave the name of the guy that was going to do it: Josiah is going to come and he’s going to, you know, desecrate the bones of these people that worship God wrongly. And you can worship God wrongly. But he didn’t listen. He let one of those lion prophets talk to him into staying. And so when he did leave, a lion got him and killed him. See, love is to obey God. He had the message, but he didn’t have the love. Solomon had the wisdom and mysteries and knowledge of everything, but in his last years he let his wives, which he had many of, hundreds, thousands altogether, lead him away from God, and his heart wasn’t right before God.
What does “a more excellent way” mean in 1 Corinthians 12–13?

1 Corinthians 12:31: But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way. 1 Corinthians 13:1: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. 1 Corinthians 13:2: And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. 1 Kings 13:1-2: And behold, a man of God went from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD, and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense. Then he cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD, and said, “O altar, altar! Thus says the LORD: ‘Behold, a child, Josiah by name, shall be born to the house of David; and on you he shall sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and men’s bones shall be burned on you.’ ”
What did Jesus mean when He said “I never knew you”?

He reads Matthew 7:22, where many say “Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name,” and says they had faith and the spiritual manifestations were working in them. Jesus still said, “I never knew you,” and he says, “You might have been used of God to do things, but you missed the important thing, and that is love.” He adds that Jesus used moving a mountain as a metaphor, and Paul says that even if you could and do not have love, “you are zero.”
What did Jesus mean when He said “I never knew you”?

See, all this without love, Paul says, is worthless, if I have all faith. And in Matthew 7:22, remember Jesus said, “Many will come to me in that day” and said, “Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name, cast out devils in your name, and in your day, and done many mighty works and many mighty miracles?” See, they had faith to do all these things, and these gifts and these spiritual manifestations were working in them. And Jesus said, “I will say to them, I never knew you. Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.” You see, you didn’t have love. You might have been used of God to do things, but you missed the important thing, and that is love. Are you with me? Hallelujah. And he says, and he quotes this, you could remove mountains. Jesus used that in Matthew. He said, “If you say to this mountain” — if you believe and say to this mountain, “Be removed, cast into the sea,” and not doubt in your heart, that mountain will be removed and go into the sea. Jesus used that as a metaphor, as an illustration. Believe me, there’s no mountains being moved by anybody. But Paul used it to say, even if you could, and you don’t have love, you are zero.
What did Jesus mean when He said “I never knew you”?

Matthew 7:22-23: Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’ Matthew 21:21: So Jesus answered and said to them, “Assuredly, I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but also if you say to this mountain, ‘Be removed and be cast into the sea,’ it will be done.
Do good works and sacrifice count if you don’t have love?

He says that if you give all your goods to feed the hungry or give your body to be burned and have not love, “it profits me nothing.” He says Judas wanted a humanitarian program rather than a Jesus program, and that “ministering to Jesus is above alms and helping the poor.” He adds that we can give our bodies for religion and our beliefs, and it can benefit us nothing.
Do good works and sacrifice count if you don’t have love?

And then he says in verse three, “If I bestow all my goods to feed those that are hungry, and I give my body to be burned” — I die, I become a martyr — “and have not love, it profits me nothing.” It benefits me nothing. Judas was one. Mary came in and she anointed Jesus’s feet with alabaster perfume, and Judas said, “Oh man, this stuff could be sold and it could be given to the poor.” The Bible even says there he didn’t care about the poor. He just wanted a humanitarian program. He wanted social programs rather than a Jesus program. This woman was ministering unto Jesus. And we all like social programs above ministering-to-Jesus programs. We think we’re really doing great when we’re helping people. But if you don’t have the Jesus program in your life, all your humanitarian things are worthless. Are you with me? And you remember the disciples, in Matthew 26, when they saw the woman pour the ointment on Jesus’s head, they said the same thing. In fact, they had indignation, and they said, “What purpose is this waste? This could have been sold and we could have given the money to the poor.” And Jesus says, “What’s the matter with you guys? This woman’s anointing me for my burial, and this act that she’s doing will be remembered all around the world.” And God put it in the Scriptures. Why? Ministering to Jesus is above alms and helping the poor and giving clothing. Are you with me? See, if we don’t have love, we’re missing it. And the Jews would die for their temple and their traditions. And not only the Jews, but a couple of guys in the Bible, Theudas and Judas, in Acts, the Bible says they caused insurrection against the Roman Empire. And they claimed to be a prophet, one of them, and got the people to follow them, and the Romans killed them. See, they died a worthless death. Why? Because that was God’s timing for the Jews at that time to be under Roman, the Roman Empire. And we can give our bodies for religion and our beliefs, and it can benefit us nothing.
Do good works and sacrifice count if you don’t have love?

1 Corinthians 13:3: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. John 12:4-6: But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, who would betray Him, said, “Why was this fragrant oil not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?” This he said, not that he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief, and had the money box; and he used to take what was put in it. Matthew 26:8-13: But when His disciples saw it, they were indignant, saying, “Why this waste? For this fragrant oil might have been sold for much and given to the poor.” But when Jesus was aware of it, He said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a good work for Me. For you have the poor with you always, but Me you do not have always. For in pouring this fragrant oil on My body, she did it for My burial. Assuredly, I say to you, wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told as a memorial to her.” Acts 5:36-37: For some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody. A number of men, about four hundred, joined him. He was slain, and all who obeyed him were scattered and came to nothing. After this man, Judas of Galilee rose up in the days of the census, and drew away many people after him. He also perished, and all who obeyed him were dispersed.
What does love look like in 1 Corinthians 13:4–7?

He walks through Paul’s definition: love is patient, kind and mannerly, does not envy, brag or behave rudely, and is not easily provoked. He says “love doesn’t demand its own way, in the family, in the church, or in the community. It demands the right way, the truth.” He says love bears all things, believes what the Bible says to trust, hopes that God will perform what he said, and remains, staying in the home and steadfast in the church.
What does love look like in 1 Corinthians 13:4–7?

And then he gives the definition of love. 1 Corinthians 13:4: Love is patient. It suffers long. Love is kind. It’s mannerly. Love doesn’t envy. It’s not jealous. Love doesn’t brag about itself. Love is not prideful, not puffed up. Love does not behave rudely, not ill-mannered. Love does not seek its own way. Well, it’s going to be my way, I’m going to hit the highway. You know, love doesn’t demand its own way, in the family, in the church, or in the community. It demands the right way, the truth. Love is not easily provoked. It, you know, they’re not touchy. You know, if you don’t say the right thing or do the right thing, they’re all ticked off. And love doesn’t do that. It thinks no evil about people, no harm. It keeps no record of wrongs done to it. One version says, you see, love does not rejoice in iniquity, but in the truth. It’s not happy when the community goes wrong. It’s happy when the community goes right, or the church goes the right direction. And check this out in verse 7. Love bears all things, which means covers with silence all things said to it. Pause for heart checking. Believes all things that the Bible says to put your trust in. They put their trust in all things the Bible says to. They hope; they expect that God would perform everything that he said he would perform. Not what people want, but what God wants. And love bears, or remains, in all things. No matter how it’s treated, no matter how mistreatment or whatever, it remains. It stays in the home and it stays steadfast in the church. It sticks right there. It doesn’t move.
What does love look like in 1 Corinthians 13:4–7?

1 Corinthians 13:4-7: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
Can you have the gifts of the Spirit without the fruit of the Spirit?

He says love is at the first fruit of the fruit of the Spirit, that “God is love,” and that love is at the top of being a partaker of the divine nature. He says, “you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without the fruit and the divine character of God,” and that this is the way to get it.
Can you have the gifts of the Spirit without the fruit of the Spirit?

And remember, love is at the first fruit of the gifts of the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace. It’s the first fruit. 1 John 4:8 says, “God is love.” See, that is exactly what God is. He just gave us the description of God. And 2 Peter 1:4: love is at the top of being a partaker of the divine nature. We add to our faith virtue; virtue, knowledge; knowledge, temperance, or self-control; patience, godliness, brotherly kindness; and the last one we add to is what? Love. So love is at the peak of divine character, and it’s at the beginning of the fruits of the Spirit. And believe me, Paul is telling us, you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without the fruit and the divine character of God. That’s what he’s telling us. This is the way to get it.
Can you have the gifts of the Spirit without the fruit of the Spirit?

Galatians 5:22-23: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law. 1 John 4:8: He who does not love does not know God, for God is love. 2 Peter 1:4-7: by which have been given to us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.

He reads that love never fails but prophecies fail, tongues cease and knowledge vanishes away, and says those are the same Greek word. He tells of Baptist leaders who said tongues and prophecies ceased when the last disciple died, and says he answered that the same verse says knowledge ceases, so if one goes you cannot take out two without the third. He also says that if prophecy ceased, Jesus would not be coming back, since that was prophesied.

Now he goes on to say, “Love never fails.” It never gets inactive. But in verse eight, he says if prophecies, they will fail; they will get inactive. If tongues, they will cease; they will get inactive. If knowledge, it will vanish away; it will be inactive. All of those three red statements up there is the same word in the Greek, just translated a little differently, but the same word. So, I have been in Pentecost ever since I was saved. Spirit-filled church, Spirit-filled person. I got Spirit-filled a couple of weeks after I got saved. I’ve worked with the Baptists and other churches. God taught me at the beginning not to be segregated. I’ve always worked with other churches and did things with other churches. I was working with some Baptist people for several years here in California, and they invited me one day into the room with the top leader of California. The Southern California leader was there, the local leaders were there, and then the new preachers coming up through the ranks were there. They brought me in, and they said, “We have never met a Spirit-filled person like you.” My reply was, “How many have you met?” I said, “You are judging us because of what you see on TV, these guys whoosh, and everybody falling over and knocking over in the Spirit and all this. You’re judging the whole group of us by what you see on TV or hear on radio or something like that. If you got to know more of us, you’d know we’re not like that.” And so then they quoted this scripture: “We believe that tongues and prophecies ceased when the last disciple died.” And they’re just quoting the verse. I said, “Sir, you didn’t finish the verse. Knowledge is there. And it says knowledge ceased. Now, if knowledge has ceased, not just tongues and prophecy, then that means people can’t come to the knowledge of salvation. People can’t have the knowledge of God, the knowledge of Christ, the knowledge of sin.” Are you with me? And they said, “Well, no, no, not knowledge.” I said, “You can’t take two out and do something with them without taking a third out.” “And number two, if prophecies really cease, then Jesus isn’t coming back again, because it was prophesied in the New Testament that he would return.” I said, “It’s also prophesied that we come back for a glorious church without spot or wrinkle or any such thing. So that can’t happen. It’s also prophesied in Revelation that every kindred, tribe, tongue and nation, a multitude that no man can number, will be brought in. That can’t happen.” Are you there? And they looked at me like, “Where’s this guy coming from?” See, it pays to know your Bible.

1 Corinthians 13:8-10: Love never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will fail; whether there are tongues, they will cease; whether there is knowledge, it will vanish away. For we know in part and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part will be done away. Ephesians 5:27: that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish. Revelation 7:9: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands,
Should we stop using spiritual gifts because people misuse them?

He says that when the Baptist leaders said Pentecostals have made a mess of tongues and prophecy, he answered, “Just because a plane crashes does not mean we stop using planes.” He says Paul is talking about edifying the body of Christ, such as a prophecy, a tongue and an interpretation one Sunday, and not about the office of a prophet or the unchangeable words of God.
Should we stop using spiritual gifts because people misuse them?

I said, “You’ve gotten rid of tongues and you’ve gotten rid of prophecy because you’ve seen the mess that us Pentecostals have done with it.” And I said this famous statement: “Just because a plane crashes does not mean we stop using planes. Just because someone messes up a salvation verse or some other verse, we don’t stop using the verses, do we?” Amen. Truly, he’s talking about edifying the body of Christ. You see, we can have a prophecy one Sunday, or a word, a tongue, an interpretation, and we forget it the next day. Isn’t that true? He’s talking about edifying the body of Christ. He’s not talking about the office of a prophet, these substantial, unchangeable words of God. Hallelujah.
Does everyone in the church have a part, or only the pastor?

He says all of us have a part: “This minister only has a part.” He says we have been taught for decades that the man of God or the woman of God will do everything and the rest are “little nobodies,” but we can all have a part. He says we do not have to wait for Jesus’s return, since 2 Corinthians 3:18 says we are changed now, and that is why we need everyone being a part.
Does everyone in the church have a part, or only the pastor?

And he goes on to prove it. We know in part and prophesy in part. And remember, in 1 Corinthians 12 he said, “To one is given the word of knowledge, to another the word of wisdom, to another faith, to another working of miracles, to another gifts of healing, to another tongues, to another discerning of spirits, to another interpretation.” So all of us have a part, and this is the thing that God wants this church to understand. This minister only has a part. We have been taught for decades that the man of God or the woman of God is going to do everything and we’re just little nobodies running around behind them. But we can all have a part. All right? “But when that which is perfect is come, that which is in part will be done away.” Okay? Now, he’s saying that yes, there are parts, but perfection is coming, maturity is coming, completeness is coming. Verse 12, same chapter: “Now we see in a mirror obscurely, but then we will see face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know just as I am known.” He’s obviously talking about the second return, isn’t he? I mean, when Jesus comes, we’re not blind anymore. I mean, everything is going to be understandable to us and fulfilled. But in 2 Corinthians 3:18, we don’t have to wait for his return. Look at this: “We all” — how many of us? All — “with an open face, seeing in a mirror the word of God” — both of those are the word of God, the mirror — “the glory of the Lord, are changed into the” what? “Same image from glory to glory by the Spirit of God.” That’s why we need the Spirit of God active in our services. And that’s why we need everyone being a part. Ephesians 4:13: “Till we all” — how many of us? All — “come into the unity of the faith, to the knowledge of the Son of God, to a” what? Perfect, complete spiritual man, “to the measure” — the standard — “of the stature of the fullness of Christ.” That’s the goal. Now, and when every part supplies, we can attain that. He says we are “no more children, tossed to and fro by every wind of doctrine.” And that’s the problem in the church. We got too many children, and they don’t even know that they can be complete and full in God. And that’s sad. It is very sad.
Does everyone in the church have a part, or only the pastor?

1 Corinthians 12:8-10: for to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. 1 Corinthians 13:12: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know just as I also am known. 2 Corinthians 3:18: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord. Ephesians 4:13-14: till we all come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ; that we should no longer be children, tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in the cunning craftiness of deceitful plotting,
What does “be perfect” mean in Matthew 5:48?

He says that when he challenged the church with Matthew 5:48 as a young Christian, they told him no one can be perfect. He says perfect is not living a life with no flaws: “it’s coming to what? Spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness.” He points to Hebrews 5:14 and James 1:4 and says God is taking his church somewhere and chooses for all of us to be a part.
What does “be perfect” mean in Matthew 5:48?

They don’t even know they can be a contributor. They just go to church to let the man of God do his thing. Could that be true? Yeah. And he goes on to say in Matthew 5:48, “Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is Jesus talking. And when I challenged the church with that as a young Christian, they go, “Well, you can’t be perfect. All of us are sin.” Well, I said, “You told me when I was a sinner I was going to hell. Now you’re telling me I got to sin because I’m not perfect.” And they thought “perfect” was just living a life that had no flaws in it. No, it’s coming to what? Spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness. Hebrews 5:14: strong meat belongs to those that are mature. You see? And then in James 1:4, it says, “Let patience have her perfect work, that you may be” what? “Perfect and entire, lacking” what? “Nothing.”
What does “be perfect” mean in Matthew 5:48?

Matthew 5:48: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. Hebrews 5:14: But solid food belongs to those who are of full age, that is, those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil. James 1:4: But let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.
What does it mean to put away childish things?

He reads 1 Corinthians 13:11 and says the childish things are being tossed about by every wind of doctrine and not coming into the unity of the faith or the stature of Jesus Christ. He says, “too many American Christians are talking like baby Christians, thinking like baby Christians, and acting like baby Christians.” He says we contribute, and that God did not intend for church people to come and just sit and watch the preacher or the song leader.
What does it mean to put away childish things?

See, God is taking his church somewhere, and he chooses for all of us to be a part. 1 Corinthians 13:11: “When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child. But when I became a man” — a mature, complete believer — “I put away childish things.” Now, what was one of the childish things we heard back there? “Tossed about by every wind of doctrine,” not coming into the unity of the faith, not coming into the stature of Jesus Christ. But here he says in the positive that I can become a man and put away childish things. I can become a man and put away childish things. I submit to you, too many American Christians are talking like baby Christians, thinking like baby Christians, and acting like baby Christians. And Paul has been dealing with this for eleven chapters: this baby Christianity, division, sexual immorality, challenging ministers. They challenged Paul, “You’re really an apostle?” You know, idolatry, doing things that didn’t please the Lord. See, not pressing toward the prize of the high mark of the calling of God by bringing their body into subjection. By what? Bringing their body into subjection. You know, we want to pray and we expect some lightning bolt to transform us, but it says we bring what? Our body into submission, and we press toward the high mark. Why? Because we contribute. We are participators in this thing God is doing. We’re not looking for a man of God or a woman of God or some J.B. Fireball to come and do everything for us. We contribute, and when all of us put our part in, then we get the full picture. Hallelujah. And this is a great program that God has. He didn’t intend for the church people to come and just sit and watch the preacher or watch the song leader. And this is why it’s important that we get 1 Corinthians 12, 13 and 14 in us, because now Paul’s talking about the real stuff, the spiritual stuff, the things that will transform people’s lives.
What does it mean to put away childish things?
1 Corinthians 13:11: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I put away childish things.
Is faith the greatest, or is love?

He reads “the greatest of these is” and says “faith” is how American preachers and believers see it: “All I hear is faith. My faith.” He says our faith must be in the power of God to perform what he promised, and that in America the church puts faith in first place and “love isn’t even on the scale.” Later he says, “The greatest of these is love.”
Is faith the greatest, or is love?

“Now abides faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is” faith. That’s the way American preachers see it. That’s the way believers see it. All I hear is faith. My faith. Even our politicians: my faith. Who cares about your faith? Our faith must be in the power of God to perform what he promised. Faith is preached all the time. And people say, “Well, I believe.” So you believe. Is it what God said to believe? Is it what God said to have faith in? And is your faith in your faith? Have you got faith above everything else? And I submit to you, in America the church puts faith in first place, and love isn’t even on the scale. How do I know that? Because they’re impatient. They don’t cover things with silence. They come to church not expecting anything. They come to church not even thinking about contributing at all. If you can get them to church. Is Paul right?
Is faith the greatest, or is love?
1 Corinthians 13:13: And now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.
Is there a free ride in church?

He says people want a ticket on the heavenbound train to sit and enjoy the scenery, but that is not the train God has: “You’ve got to shovel the coal. You’ve got to blow the whistle.” He says “There ain’t no free ride,” and that to see the manifestations of the Spirit of God we have to take on responsibility to be a participator. He says that when people take responsibility in a church service, “you will be shocked at what God can do.”
Is there a free ride in church?

See, they want a free ride. They want a ticket to get on the heavenbound train and just sit there, enjoy the scenery. And that isn’t the train God has. You’ve got to shovel the coal. You’ve got to blow the whistle. You’ve got to be active in this thing. There ain’t no free ride. If we really want to attain to great things here on this earth and see the manifestations of the Spirit of God, then we’ve got to humble ourselves, take on responsibility to be a participator. I mean, Paul is saying it plainly. See, we all know in part, and we prophesy, or speak by the inspiration of God, in part. See, I don’t have it all. Mr. Barnes doesn’t have it all. But together, we got a lot more. And then you add Edie and Christina. Hey, now we’re broadening. See, when people start taking responsibility to be involved in a church service, you will be shocked at what God can do. And church, I have been in Spirit-filled churches all my life, and I have seen some powerful manifestations of God. And I have seen things that are just embarrassing. But you know, I can’t let the embarrassing things keep me from what? Pursuing God. Hallelujah. The greatest of these is love. It’s great to have faith. It’s great to have hope. And Paul sums it up here.
What is the goal of the commandment?

He reads 1 Timothy 1:5 and says the word “end” means the goal: the goal of the word of God is love out of a pure heart, a good conscience and sincere faith. He says people think the goal is eternal life or the gifts of the Spirit, “And it’s not. It’s love.” He says that is why there is such phoniness in the Spirit-filled world as people try to push something God isn’t doing.
What is the goal of the commandment?

This scripture, 1 Timothy 1:5: “Now the end of the commandment is love out of a pure heart.” The word “end” means the goal. You see, the goal of the word of God is love out of a pure heart. The purpose of the word of God is love out of a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith. See, genuine faith, not disguised faith. See, we think it’s eternal life. No, you’re going to live eternally no matter what. You realize that, whether you believe in God or you don’t believe in God, do you realize you’re an eternal being? Yeah. Only one’s going to spend their place in a punishment and one’s going to be rewarded. We think that it’s the gifts of the Spirit in our circles. The gifts of the Spirit. Hallelujah. Shakamula in the name of Jesus. And it’s not. It’s love. And that’s why we have such phoniness in the Spirit-filled world, as we try to push something that God isn’t doing.
What is the goal of the commandment?
1 Timothy 1:5: Now the purpose of the commandment is love from a pure heart, from a good conscience, and from sincere faith,
Are tongues, worship, prayer, soulwinning or rituals the goal?

He says God is the one who distributes these things as he wills. The baptism of the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues is not the goal; he says it is “one of the attributes that gives you power to live for God.” Worship and prayer are each “a means to the goal,” soulwinning is not the goal, and neither are church rituals such as holy water, incense, Lent or a Christmas tree: “Rituals are not the goal of the word of God. It’s love.”
Are tongues, worship, prayer, soulwinning or rituals the goal?

Remember in 1 Corinthians 12, it says God is the one that distributes these things as he wills. If God’s not healing, guess what? There ain’t going to be no healing. If God’s not speaking, there ain’t going to be no speaking. He’s the one that initiates these things and backs them up. Some of them believe it’s grace and faith. As I said, I mean, most people, they grace and faith it all through their life. They believe the goal of the commandment is the baptism of the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues. That’s not the goal of the commandment. That’s one of the attributes that gives you power to live for God. One of the peripheral important things. Worship, in our generation since about 1990. Oh, worship. Hallelujah. New song, worship. Oh man, we got the band, we got the music, we got worship. Oh, we’ve arrived. And they go home and they can’t love their family. They can’t love their husband. They can’t love their wife. Why? Because worship is not the goal. It is a means to the goal. Prayer: some people are just hyped up on a prayer meeting. Prayer is not the goal. It’s a means to the goal. Soulwinning. Oh man, you know, we led somebody to Christ, a 63-year-old man to Christ, me and Mr. Barnes did this week. That is one of the things we do, but that’s not the goal of the commandment. And people, they’re soulwinning every Thursday night. You know, “Hallelujah, I’m a [unclear] man. I’ve arrived.” Are you with me? And church rituals. “Got my holy water. Got my incense. Got the season of Lent. I’m keeping the feast of Pentecost. Christmas — oh yeah, I’m really into Christmas. Got my Christmas tree.” Rituals are not the goal of the word of God.
Are tongues, worship, prayer, soulwinning or rituals the goal?
1 Corinthians 12:11: But one and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing to each one individually as He wills.
Why are American Christians divorcing, and what strengthens a home and a church?

He answers the divorce question with “Lack of love. Somebody’s not loving. Somebody’s not patient. Somebody is demanding their own way,” and tells of a Quaker husband who chose the principle over the organ. He says that during a transition in a church you do the same thing you always do: minister to Christ, come to give and contribute. To strengthen your life, home and children, he says, “we’ve got to get this love. It’s above spiritual gifts. It’s above social programs.”
Why are American Christians divorcing, and what strengthens a home and a church?

It’s love. And why are American Christians divorcing? Lack of love. Somebody’s not loving. Somebody’s not patient. Somebody is demanding their own way. I saw a movie yesterday that was really cool. I’ve seen it before. I forgot his name, but anyway. And they were Quakers, and the woman was a preacher woman, and the guy bought an organ, and Quakers didn’t believe in music. He bought an organ for the house. And she says, “It’s either that organ or me. If that organ comes into the house, I’m leaving.” He says, “When thou ask me to do something, I am like butter in your hands. When thou commands me, I’m like, you know, a hard rock. Pick up the organ and put it in the house.” She goes, “You’re kidding me. You’re choosing the organ?” No, he wasn’t choosing an organ over his wife. He was choosing the principle. Amen. It was the principle of the thing. Now, church, Paul has given us tremendous advice. Someone asked me a few weeks ago, “What do we do during a transition of a church?” The same thing you always do. You minister to Christ. You come to give. You come to contribute. Nothing changes. Just because leadership changes, the real leader is who? Jesus Christ. Are we getting it, church? Do you want to strengthen your life? You want to strengthen your home, your children? We’ve got to get this love. It’s above spiritual gifts. It’s above social programs. Social programs is not enough. If we want the fullness of Christ, we’ve got to get this love.
What are the two kinds of tongues Paul describes in 1 Corinthians 13?

He says tongues is nothing but languages. There are languages of men, like they spoke on the day of Pentecost, and there are languages of angels. He says the key is that love is more important than both of those.
What happened to the man of God in 1 Kings 13?

He says the man of God was chosen to take a message to King Jeroboam and told to give it and come back without staying. He gave the message, but he did not listen and let one of the “lion prophets” talk him into staying, and a lion killed him when he left. He says, “love is to obey God.”
What does he say went wrong with Solomon?
He says Solomon had the wisdom and mysteries and knowledge of everything, but in his last years he let his many wives lead him away from God, and his heart wasn’t right before God.
Did Judas really care about the poor?

He says that when Mary anointed Jesus’s feet, Judas said the perfume could be sold and given to the poor, but the Bible says he didn’t care about the poor. He says Judas wanted a humanitarian program, social programs rather than a Jesus program.
Was the woman pouring ointment on Jesus a waste?

He says the disciples were indignant and asked, “What purpose is this waste?” and that Jesus told them the woman was anointing him for his burial and that her act would be remembered all around the world. He says God put it in the Scriptures because ministering to Jesus is above alms and helping the poor.
What does “love does not seek its own way” mean?

He says love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, in the church, or in the community, but demands the right way, the truth. He puts the opposite as “it’s going to be my way, I’m going to hit the highway.”
What does it mean that love “bears all things”?

He says it means covers with silence all things said to it. He says love also remains in all things: no matter how it’s treated, it stays in the home and stays steadfast in the church. It sticks right there; it doesn’t move.
Where does love fit in the fruit of the Spirit and the divine nature?

He says love is the first fruit of the Spirit, and in 2 Peter 1:4 it is the last thing we add to our faith, so love is at the peak of divine character and at the beginning of the fruits of the Spirit.
Is the Greek word the same for prophecies failing, tongues ceasing and knowledge vanishing?
He says all of those three red statements in the verse are the same word in the Greek, just translated a little differently, but the same word.
Should Spirit-filled churches work with other churches?

He says he has been in Pentecost ever since he was saved but that God taught him at the beginning not to be segregated, and that he has always worked with other churches and done things with them. He tells of working with Baptist people for several years in California.
Why does he say people want a free ride at church?

He says they come to church not expecting anything and not even thinking about contributing at all. They want a ticket on the heavenbound train to sit and enjoy the scenery, but he says you’ve got to be active in this thing.
Does he say everyone lives eternally?

He says, “you’re going to live eternally no matter what,” and asks whether the listener realizes that whether you believe in God or not, you are an eternal being. He says only one is going to spend their place in a punishment and one is going to be rewarded.
According to this message, who decides when healing or tongues happen?

He says that in 1 Corinthians 12 God is the one who distributes these things as he wills. He says, “If God’s not healing, guess what? There ain’t going to be no healing. If God’s not speaking, there ain’t going to be no speaking,” because he is the one who initiates these things and backs them up.
Does he say speaking in tongues is the goal?

No. He says that people believe the goal of the commandment is the baptism of the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues, but that is not the goal of the commandment. He says it is one of the attributes that gives you power to live for God, one of the peripheral important things.
What should a church do during a leadership transition?

He says someone asked him this a few weeks ago, and his answer was the same thing you always do: you minister to Christ, you come to give, you come to contribute. He says nothing changes, because even when leadership changes, the real leader is Jesus Christ.
