p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through 1 Corinthians 12–14 to show what a New Testament church service should look like. He gives four goals for coming to church, says the gifts of the Spirit must be pursued through love, and lists the utterance gifts and the guidelines for using them. He then teaches that tongues are for today, with an interpretation and in decent order.
What should a New Testament church service look like?

He says Paul gives clear instructions in 1 Corinthians 14 on how a New Testament church service should be, and that 1 Corinthians 12, 13 and 14 are three very important chapters. If you want a powerful church service you must understand them and exercise them, not let everybody “pick and choose how a church service goes.”
What should a New Testament church service look like?

And today we’re going to be looking in 1 Corinthians 14, a New Testament church service. I know today we have all kinds of ideas how a church service is supposed to be, even how long it should be. But Paul is going to give us clear instructions on how a New Testament church service should be. Are you ready? Remember 1 Corinthians 12, 1 Corinthians 13, and 1 Corinthians 14, the chapter we’re in: three very important chapters. If you want to have a powerful church, a powerful church service, you must understand these three chapters, and not only understand them, you must exercise them. We got to get away from this mentality that everybody can pick and choose how a church service goes and what must, should be done in the church service. Paul is going to explain it very clearly.
What does “spiritual gifts” mean in 1 Corinthians 12:1?

He says the word “gift” is not in that verse; it could mean “I don’t want you ignorant of spiritual things,” of spiritual manifestations and expressions. We come into a spiritual kingdom, he says, and need a spiritual understanding and a spiritual touch in our life, so there are four goals when we come to church.
What does “spiritual gifts” mean in 1 Corinthians 12:1?

Remember in 1 Corinthians 12:1 he says, “Concerning spiritual, I would not have you ignorant.” Now the King James and the other ones have “spiritual gifts,” but the word “gift” isn’t in that at all. It could be they just added it for clarification. It could be, “I don’t want you ignorant of spiritual things. I don’t want you ignorant of spiritual manifestations, spiritual expressions.” You see, coming to Christ we come into a spiritual kingdom. We’re already in a human kingdom, but what we need is a spiritual understanding and a spiritual touch in our life. And so there are four goals when we come to church. There should be four goals, four purposes.
What does “spiritual gifts” mean in 1 Corinthians 12:1?
1 Corinthians 12:1: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I do not want you to be ignorant:

He says the first goal is understanding how spiritual things work, and the second, in chapter 12:31, is that Paul says to “covet earnestly” the best gifts. We need to take spiritual things seriously and get away from the “concert mentality” and the programs, and “best gifts” means the higher gifts, a supernatural spiritual ability.

Number one, we should be coming with the understanding of how spiritual things work, not to be ignorant anymore of spiritual things. How many can raise your hand and say, “Lord, I don’t want to be ignorant anymore of spiritual things”? You know, it’s not a matter of what man says this and man says that; it’s what God says: spiritual to spiritual. And so we need understanding of spiritual things. Number two, in chapter 12:31 Paul said you got to covet. See, the Ten Commandments says, “Thou shalt not covet,” but here you’re allowed to covet. You’re allowed to covet spiritual gifts, and in fact he says the best gifts. And it says covet earnestly, or seriously. We need to take spiritual things seriously. Could that be an amen? Yeah. We got to get away from the concert mentality that’s in the America today. We got to get away from all these programs and everything, and we got to focus in on what the Bible tells us to focus in, and that is spiritual things, and we got to get serious about it. And “best gifts” means the higher gifts. There are levels of gifts, and he says you need to get serious about the higher level of gifts. Gifts is a spiritual ability, okay, a supernatural spiritual ability.

1 Corinthians 12:31: But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way. Exodus 20:17: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
Why must we pursue love to move in the gifts of the Spirit?

He says Paul shows “a superior way” to spiritual manifestations, and chapter 13 explains love in great detail. If you want spiritual manifestation you have to pursue love, so love is a goal: love is patient and kind, it does not rejoice in iniquity, and it never quits.
Why must we pursue love to move in the gifts of the Spirit?

Now, four goals; there’s two of them. 1 Corinthians 12:31, “I will show you a more excellent way.” 1 Corinthians 14:1, “Follow after charity.” And then chapter 13 was all about love, right? See, I’m going to show you a superior way to spiritual manifestations, and then he goes into chapter 13 and explains love in great detail. See, and he says if you want spiritual manifestation, you’ve got to have what? Love. You got to pursue love. And so we got to have a goal to love, you see. And it explains love: love is patient, love is kind, love doesn’t brag about itself, love doesn’t rejoice in iniquity but rejoices in the truth. In other words, love doesn’t sin. Love bears all things, believes all things, and endures all things. Love never quits. Now let me ask you this: how do I know if I’m loving? Okay, if I go out on my wife and have sex outside of my marriage, who am I not loving?
Why must we pursue love to move in the gifts of the Spirit?

1 Corinthians 12:31: But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way. 1 Corinthians 14:1: Pursue love, and desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy. 1 Corinthians 13:4-8: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will fail; whether there are tongues, they will cease; whether there is knowledge, it will vanish away.
How do I know if I am really loving people?

He says love does nothing to hurt, so sin like adultery or stealing shows you are not loving your spouse, your children, the person you steal from, or God. The church wants the power of spiritual expressions, he says, but it does not want to go through love.
How do I know if I am really loving people?

I’m not loving my wife, because, see, love does nothing to hurt. So see, that eliminates me from spiritual expressions. Who else am I not loving? My children. I’m a bad example to my children. So that eliminates me from spiritual expressions. Paul says you can’t get into the power of the Spirit but through love. Do we get that? Who else am I not loving? I’m not loving God, because God says, “Thou shalt not commit adultery.” See, that’s three strikes. Now if I go and steal, who am I not loving? Well, obviously the person that I stole from; I hurt them. Obviously I’m going to hurt my family, because if I wind up in jail and I’m not there to be a father and be a provider, that hurts the family. And obviously I’m not loving God, because God says, “Thou shalt not steal.” And see, the church wants power, of spiritual expressions, but they don’t want to go through love. Oh, they love to get, I mean, worship, when I was a young believer, was rare. You know, it was the church across the railroad tracks, it was the weirdos that did that. Now everybody’s worshiping, but not everybody’s loving. There’s something wrong.
How do I know if I am really loving people?
Exodus 20:14: “You shall not commit adultery. Exodus 20:15: “You shall not steal.

He says everybody is worshiping now, but “not everybody’s loving.” We are into the music but not into love, so the goal is to pursue love, and the peripheral thing given to us would be spiritual manifestations. We also have to come with a serious mentality about church.

We’re into the music, we’re into all that, but we’re not into love. Are you with me? And so, see, we need to have this goal to what? Pursue love. And in pursuing love, then the peripheral thing given to us would be spiritual manifestations. Now Paul’s clear. You agree with Paul? Yes. So see, somewhere we got to get serious about a church service. Could that be an amen? And we got to come with a serious mentality about church.
What is prophecy according to Paul?

He says prophecy is speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, not your own spirit or your “little hobby-horse doctrine.” The Spirit is the source, he says, and it has to be the Spirit that initiates it. This is the fourth goal for coming to church.
What is prophecy according to Paul?

Now the fourth goal we should have: 1 Corinthians 14:1, “Desire spiritual gifts, but rather that you may prophesy.” Now here is the best gift: prophecy. Prophecy means speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, not your spirit, not your little hobby-horse doctrine, not your Calvinist, Lutheran, or Catholic or whatever doctrine. It’s speaking by the inspiration; the source comes from the Spirit. See, the Spirit is the source of this thing. Are you with me? It can’t be you; it’s got to be the Spirit that initiates it. And so those are four goals we got to come to church for if we want to see God moving. These four goals are necessary.
What is prophecy according to Paul?
1 Corinthians 14:1: Pursue love, and desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.
What are the utterance gifts, and which can everyone do?

He lists the utterance expressions as word of wisdom, word of knowledge, prophecy, interpretation, revelation, doctrine, unknown languages, singing, praying and Psalms. Some of these we can all do, he says, like singing, praying and reading a Psalm, and Paul names these as the best gifts, with no mention of healing, miracles, discerning of spirits or faith.
What are the utterance gifts, and which can everyone do?

Now the utterance gifts. He’s going to be talking about the utterance spiritual abilities that God wants to manifest in a church service, and I’m just going to go through, instead of verse by verse, I’m just going to give you the outline of what he’s saying here. Word of wisdom, remember that in 1 Corinthians 12; the word of knowledge; prophecy; interpretation; revelation; doctrine; unknown languages; singing; praying; and Psalms. See, these are the utterance expressions that God is saying is the best spiritual manifestation in the church service. Now some of these we all can’t do, but some of them we can. Can we all sing? Yeah. Can we all pray? Yes. Could we all read a Psalm? Psalms are Scriptures; they’re spiritually anointed Scripture. Yeah. And we can all prophesy, one by one. Paul says when that certain presence of prophecies is there. But he also said not all prophesy, not all speak in tongues, not all interpret, and so forth, but there is things that we can do. All right, and so here it is. These are the utterance gifts. The Spirit comes and moves us to speak things, and Paul says these are the best gifts. No mention of healing, no mention of miracles, no mention of discerning of spirits, no mention of faith. The utterance gifts, Paul is saying, is the high gifts. Are you with Paul? Hallelujah.
What are the utterance gifts, and which can everyone do?

1 Corinthians 12:8-10: for to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. 1 Corinthians 12:29-30: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles? Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret?
What should I check before I say something in church?

He says to judge it before you open your mouth: it has to edify, exhort and comfort, and above all it has to be easily understandable. Using Scripture without it making sense does not help, so ask whether it will profit people’s lives and whether they will understand it, and “if not zip the lip.”
What should I check before I say something in church?

Now here is the requirements. If you want to say something, these are your guidelines. See, judge it first before you open your mouth. Judge it by these four things. Are you ready? Number one, it’s got to edify, exhort, and comfort. See, it’s got to build up, it’s got to construct people’s lives, it’s got to encourage them. See, or it’s going to comfort them. See, when someone is down, they need comforted. And above all, it’s got to be easily understandable. I can lift up my voice and say, “There was an old oak tree, and as the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood.” So, I mean, there’s not much understanding there, is there? But yet both of those were Scriptures. So you can’t just use Scripture without it making sense. Hallelujah. So you judge it of what am I going to say. Is it going to profit people’s life, and are they going to understand it? If not, zip the lip. Could that be an amen?
What should I check before I say something in church?

1 Corinthians 14:3: But he who prophesies speaks edification and exhortation and comfort to men. Proverbs 30:33: For as the churning of milk produces butter, And wringing the nose produces blood, So the forcing of wrath produces strife.
Why must the Holy Spirit be the source of what we say in church?

He says that in Acts 2:4 the Spirit gave them the utterance, so the Spirit has to be the source and not our own mentality. We want to beat each other over the head and correct each other, he says, but the Spirit wants to change, encourage and build lives.
Why must the Holy Spirit be the source of what we say in church?

Secondly, 1 Corinthians 14:15, the Holy Spirit must be the source. “I will sing with the spirit, I will sing with the understanding; I will pray with the spirit, I will pray with the understanding.” Acts 2:4, they spoke in languages as the Spirit gave them utterance. Who gave the speech? Who gave the utterance? The Spirit. They didn’t do it on their own. So see, the Spirit has to be the source, not my mentality. I know something and know so-and-so should be changing their life, and so I speak a word: “Man, you’re a sinner and you’re going to hell, you got to repent today.” Yeah. Now the Spirit ignites it, and you obviously don’t know anything, but the Spirit does, and the Spirit knows how to say it. We want to beat each other over the head, we want to correct each other, and the Spirit wants to change and encourage and build lives. Hallelujah.
Why must the Holy Spirit be the source of what we say in church?

1 Corinthians 14:15: What is the conclusion then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the understanding. I will sing with the spirit, and I will also sing with the understanding. Acts 2:4: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
What does “let all things be done decently and in order” mean?

He says Spirit-filled churches had power because they had a purpose, but in old Pentecost and the charismatic circles there was no manners and no order, and that turned a lot of people off. We cannot stop seeking the Word of God because some people mess it up, he says, and we cannot be so mannerly that we do not care if we offend God in his house.
What does “let all things be done decently and in order” mean?

Now this, to me as a young believer, made the Spirit-filled churches quite a few notches above the other ones that did not believe in the baptism of the Holy Ghost with expressions. So I could walk into a Spirit-filled church, 90% of the time you could feel the power of His presence. It was there. Why? Because they purposed, they had a purpose. Did they do everything right? No, they didn’t. They made a lot of boo-boos, but they had some right goals. But Paul’s given us the total goals, and he’s going to clear everything up for us. 1 Corinthians 14:40, “Let all things be done decently, mannerly, and in order.” This is the problem that we had in old Pentecost and in the charismatic circles: there was no manners and there was no order, and so it turned a lot of people off. But I’m telling you, we can’t stop seeking and responding to the Word of God because some people mess it up. Could that be an amen?
What does “let all things be done decently and in order” mean?
1 Corinthians 14:40: Let all things be done decently and in order.
How many people should speak in tongues or prophesy in one service?

He says prophecies and tongues should be spoken two or at the most three, and after the third one you stop. Each one should add to the part before it so that in three expressions you have the clarity of the whole thing, and tongues should be spoken the same way, with an interpretation.
How many people should speak in tongues or prophesy in one service?

We can’t go to our own mentality and have a church service where we’re so mannerly that God can’t even get, you know, we get rid of Him. We’re so worried about offending people, we don’t care if we offend God, and it’s His house. Hallelujah. And this is the mistakes we make, and I had to work through all this as a young Christian. I was baffled for a year or two with some of this stuff until God began to give me understanding. All right. 1 Corinthians 14:27 through [unclear]: prophecies and tongues should be spoken two, or at the most, three. It’s not [unclear]. Hallelujah, bam. See, just one. I used to call them tongue tournaments, you know, [unclear], you know, just [unclear]. And prophecy, you can’t just keep prophesying after the third one. What do you do? Stop. And it says “in course.” What’s that mean? See, a part, and it’s a part added to a part. If someone prophesies about having a heart after God, and the next person prophesies about Judas betraying Christ, see, it’s not adding to the part. It’s got to build. See, build, and in three expressions you should have the clarity of the whole thing. Amen. And watch this: tongues is the same way. He says the person speaks in an unknown tongue, let it be one or two, at the most three. And people are scared to death of tongues and languages today because us Pentecostals, charismatic, Spirit-filled churches have made a mess of this thing, and so people just want to throw it out of the Bible. And Paul plainly says that tongues should be spoken the same way, and there should be an interpretation. Isn’t that right? Hallelujah.
How many people should speak in tongues or prophesy in one service?

1 Corinthians 14:27-29: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let there be two or at the most three, each in turn, and let one interpret. But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in church, and let him speak to himself and to God. Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge.
Are speaking in tongues and spiritual gifts for today?

He says he wants to convince us that tongues are Bible and are for today, and that this is Paul’s teaching, not his: “I’m just his microphone.” When we speak in an unknown tongue we speak to God, he says, and there is nothing wrong with talking to God.
Are speaking in tongues and spiritual gifts for today?

That is the requirements. I want to take a closer look at tongues here. I want to convince you today that tongues are Bible, and they are for today, from Paul’s teaching, the chiefest apostle’s teaching. This is not my teaching; I’m just his microphone. It says in 1 Corinthians 14, when we speak in an unknown tongue, we speak to God, not to man. Now what’s wrong with us speaking to God? Is there anything wrong with me speaking to God? When I pray, am I supposed to be praying to men or to God? To God. So what’s wrong with talking to God? Nothing. It’s important.
Are speaking in tongues and spiritual gifts for today?
1 Corinthians 14:2: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men but to God, for no one understands him; however, in the spirit he speaks mysteries.
Is it wrong to build yourself up in the faith by speaking in tongues?

He says one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, and he sees nothing wrong with building yourself up in the faith; he should be encouraged to do it and not wait for someone else to do something for him. He adds that tongues are a sign to the unbeliever, and that if they get the unbeliever’s attention, that is a good thing.
Is it wrong to build yourself up in the faith by speaking in tongues?

Secondly, he edifies himself; he builds up himself. What’s wrong with me building up myself in the faith? Is there anything wrong with that? No, it’s not only not wrong, I should be encouraged to do it. I need to not wait for the J.B. [unclear], the mighty man of God, to do something for me. I should be, what? Building myself up. Are you with me? Now Paul’s good. I’m telling you, this apostle Paul’s good. Tongues are a sign to the unbeliever. What’s wrong with that? If tongues will get the unbeliever’s attention, is that a good thing? Yes. See, miracles also get the unbeliever’s attention. See, those are good things.
Is it wrong to build yourself up in the faith by speaking in tongues?

1 Corinthians 14:4: He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the church. 1 Corinthians 14:22: Therefore tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe but to unbelievers; but prophesying is not for unbelievers but for those who believe.
Should tongues be spoken in church without an interpretation?

He says if there is no interpretation the one who speaks mysteries is no profit to others, so it should not be done publicly in the service, but it can be done quietly during worship. If it is not done decently and in order, he says, people will say you are mad, and he says the spirit of the prophet is in control.
Should tongues be spoken in church without an interpretation?

But if there’s no interpretation, there should be an interpretation. If there’s no interpretation, the guy speaks mysteries, and it is no profit to others. Okay, so I shouldn’t be doing it publicly in the service, but I can be doing it quietly myself during worship, can’t I? [unclear], you know, I’m not bothering anybody. I’m building myself up, I’m talking to God. But when I leave decently and in order, I told [unclear] the people go, “Well, what’s going on?” Paul says they’re going to say you are what? Mad. You’re crazy. People, and that’s exactly what they said about us Pentecostals: they’re a bunch of nuts. Why? Because we didn’t do it mannerly and in proper order. “Well, the Spirit’s upon me.” Oh, shut up. Paul said that the spirit of the prophet is in control. You can control yourself and not say anything and just feel good. Amen.
Should tongues be spoken in church without an interpretation?

1 Corinthians 14:23: Therefore if the whole church comes together in one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those who are uninformed or unbelievers, will they not say that you are out of your mind? 1 Corinthians 14:32: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.
Does the Bible say not to forbid speaking in tongues?

He says Paul says “forbid not to speak in tongues,” yet in most churches it is taboo and has been said to be not for today. He says he wants these things: a sign for the unbeliever, edifying yourself, talking to God. The Holy Spirit must give the utterance, there will be an interpretation, and if there is none, keep silent.
Does the Bible say not to forbid speaking in tongues?

Hallelujah. Then Paul says, “Forbid not to speak in tongues.” Boy, you go to most churches, it’s taboo. In fact, they have said it’s not for today. They’ve rewritten the whole Bible. “Well, it’s just not for today.” Well, isn’t that nice. What else is not for today? A sign for the unbeliever, and it’s not for today. I can edify myself, and it’s not for today. I can talk to God, and it’s not for today. No, thank you. I want these things. And the Holy Spirit, again, must give the utterance. It can’t be you showing off with your [unclear], it can’t be you, you know, doing your little thing. The Holy Spirit’s got to move. There will be an interpretation if the Holy Spirit is moving in an unknown language to edify the body of Christ, to comfort it. There will be an interpretation, and if there isn’t, what does Paul say? Keep silent. But he still says what? Don’t forbid to speak in tongues. And so I submit to you today, tongues are important when it’s done right. As a young believer it touched my life, that power of the presence just touched my life. I might have not have known what was said, but the Holy Ghost was backing it up.
Does the Bible say not to forbid speaking in tongues?

1 Corinthians 14:39: Therefore, brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak with tongues. 1 Corinthians 14:28: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in church, and let him speak to himself and to God.
What are the goals when we come to church?
He says there are four goals: understanding how spiritual things work, taking spiritual things seriously (covet earnestly the best gifts), pursuing love, and prophecy, which he calls the best gift.
He says “gifts is a spiritual ability, okay, a supernatural spiritual ability,” and that “best gifts” means the higher gifts.
Is it ever right to covet?
He says the Ten Commandments say “Thou shalt not covet,” but here in 1 Corinthians you are allowed to covet spiritual gifts, and the best gifts, earnestly or seriously.
Does sin keep us from the power of the Spirit?

He says sin such as adultery or stealing hurts the people we should be loving, and that eliminates us from spiritual expressions. Paul says you cannot get into the power of the Spirit but through love.
What does he say is wrong with the church today?
He says everybody is worshiping now but not everybody is loving. “We’re into the music, we’re into all that, but we’re not into love.”
Is prophecy my own doctrine or opinion?
No, he says. Prophecy is speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, “not your little hobby-horse doctrine, not your Calvinist, Lutheran, or Catholic or whatever doctrine.”
Can everyone sing, pray and prophesy in church?

He says we can all sing, we can all pray, and we can all read a Psalm, which is spiritually anointed Scripture, and we can all prophesy one by one. But Paul also said not all prophesy, not all speak in tongues, and not all interpret.
Does Paul say healing and miracles are the best gifts?
He says Paul lists the utterance gifts as the best, and that there is “no mention of healing, no mention of miracles, no mention of discerning of spirits, no mention of faith.”
Why must what we say in church be understandable?
He says it has to be easily understandable, and gives the example of lifting up his voice with a mix of Scripture phrases that makes no sense. “You can’t just use scripture without it making sense.”
Why did Spirit-filled churches have the power of God’s presence?

He says that as a young believer he could walk into a Spirit-filled church and feel the power of his presence about 90% of the time, because they purposed and had a purpose. He adds that they did not do everything right and made a lot of mistakes.
Did he always understand all this?
No. He says he had to work through all of this as a young Christian and was baffled for a year or two with some of it until God began to give him understanding.
Why are people afraid of tongues?

He says people are scared to death of tongues because Pentecostal, charismatic, Spirit-filled churches have “made a mess of this thing,” so people want to throw it out of the Bible. Paul plainly says tongues should be spoken the same way, with an interpretation.
Can I speak in tongues quietly during worship?

He says that without an interpretation he should not be doing it publicly in the service, but he can do it quietly himself during worship. He is not bothering anybody, he is building himself up and talking to God.
Can you control yourself when the Spirit is upon you?
He says Paul said the spirit of the prophet is in control, so you can control yourself and not say anything and just feel good. “Well, the Spirit’s upon me. Oh, shut up.”
What if there is no interpretation of a tongue?

He says the Holy Spirit must give the utterance, and there will be an interpretation if the Holy Spirit is moving in an unknown language to edify the body of Christ. If there is none, he says, Paul says to keep silent.

items.d: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to…
p: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to prosperity preaching and other teaching he calls fractured. He plays recorded clips of public figures and ministers speaking about heaven, other religions and sin, and responds to them. He ends with the phrase “my faith,” saying the Bible uses it with works and with the faith of Jesus, and that our faith must be in Jesus Christ and his word, not in a group.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

Pastor Kincer says these were disciples who did not believe: they were disciplined to follow Christ to a certain degree, but they left when it came down to God being involved, and to accountability and responsibility. He says Jesus told them you cannot decide to serve God on your own, since the Father and the Spirit must be involved in your salvation, and it is not about joining a church or being a Jew, Protestant or Catholic.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

But this morning we’re going to talk about some deflective, defective disciples. Not everybody in the Bible turned out to be heroes. Deflective, defective disciples. They deflected because they had a defect. A disciple is one that’s disciplined, a pupil of Christ, a follower of Christ. And in John 6 we find him talking to what he called disciples, and he said, “There are some of you that believe not.” These are disciples that believe not. “For Jesus knew from the beginning who believe not and who should betray him.” Wow, powerful statement. “No man,” Jesus said, “can come unto me except it were given unto him by my Father.” Jesus said, listen, you can’t decide to serve God on your own. Me and my Father have to be involved in your conversion, in your salvation. It’s not joining a church, or being a Jew, or being a Protestant, or being a Catholic. Jesus said my Father has to be involved. The Spirit of God has to be involved. That’s why the Bible says you must be born again of the Spirit and of the word. Well, the disciples didn’t like this statement. Okay, now these are disciples. They’re disciples that didn’t believe. See, they were disciplined to follow Christ to a certain degree, but “from that time many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him.” They left him. And they were called disciples, but when it come down to God being involved, and accountability and responsibility, they left Jesus. And we’re going to show you what was really in their heart here.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

John 6:64-66: But there are some of you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who would betray Him. And He said, “Therefore I have said to you that no one can come to Me unless it has been granted to him by My Father.” From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

He says Jesus asked the twelve whether they would also go away, and he says that is what God is saying to the churches in America today: will you stop walking with me and join your little clique? He says Peter and the others answered that there is nowhere to go, because Jesus has the words of eternal life, and he says eternal life is to know God and Jesus Christ, not just live forever.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

What does God want us to give him?

He says God wants a Bible morality lifestyle: living right and stopping sinning. He says praise is wonderful and prayer is wonderful, but what God wants back from you is for you to live right, no matter if you are a Catholic, a Jew or a Protestant.
Why does he say the crowd followed Jesus in John 6?

He says they followed him because they saw the signs he performed on those who were diseased, and later because he fed them with the loaves and fishes. He says Jesus told them plainly that they now wanted free food, which he describes as wanting what we can get out of God.
What are the “P’s” he warns against?

He lists prosperity, psychotherapy, Purpose Driven, possibility thinking, positive thinking and individual prophecy. He says these followers are fractured and are deflecting from Christ, wanting something instead of giving him something.
What does he say the Bible calls for instead of therapy and positive thinking?
He says Jesus wants us to give him Bible morality, not grace and faith, prosperity, positive thinking or psychotherapy, and that in the Bible it is self-control: just stop what you’re doing.
What does he say the Mormon church told him about Jesus Christ?

He says he called their headquarters, did not act like somebody else, and asked questions. He says they told him Jesus Christ is not God, is not eternal without a beginning and an end, and did not exist until Mary, and he says the Bible teaches he existed before Mary.
Where does the Bible use the phrase “my faith”?

He says it is found only twice: once where someone says I will show you my faith by my works, and once in Jesus’s words to a church in Revelation, where he says you did not deny my faith. He says the phrase is used in conjunction with lifestyle, not just words.
Do the demons believe in God?

He says the demons believe and they are not going to heaven, they tremble, so saying you believe is not enough. He says what people say they believe is insignificant; it is what God told us to believe that is significant.
What does 1 Corinthians 2:5 say about where our faith should be?

He says it says your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. He says Paul meant that faith cannot be done intellectually: it has to be in the supernatural power of God involved in your life.
What does he say Jesus’s faith was in?
He says Jesus’s faith was in the scriptures and in the Father. He points to Jesus saying he does nothing except what the Father tells him to do.
Can your faith be in your church or denomination?

He says no: the problem with Catholics, Protestants and Jews alike is that their faith is in their group. He says your faith has to be in Jesus Christ and his word, and your faith cannot be in your faith but has to be in his faith.

items.d: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the previous message by saying the Bible’s “I believe” statements are about believing Jesus is the Son of God and that God will do…
p: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the previous message by saying the Bible’s “I believe” statements are about believing Jesus is the Son of God and that God will do what he said. He argues from Acts and 1 Corinthians that Christians and ministers are meant to judge, reads Revelation 21:8 on who goes to the lake of fire, and criticizes ministers he says flatter people. He points to Jeremiah 3:15 as God’s solution and calls believers to virtue and to speak up.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?

Pastor Kincer lists prosperity, positive thinking, possibility, Purpose Driven and psychotherapy thinking, and adds personal prophecy thinking, which he says is a dime a dozen in many Spirit-filled circles. He says he does not need personal prophecy; he needs the Bible, the sure word of prophecy. He says the claim that atheists, humanists and anyone who is good can go to heaven is lying, and that the end result of Jesus’s faith is a disciple pursuing the divine nature and doing good works.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?

Adultery, homosexuality, incest, intoxication. Okay, see, “my faith,” “I believe,” nothing’s wrong with it. Prosperity, positive thinking, possibility— you ever met these people that won’t say a negative thing? There: possibility thinking, prosperity thinking, Purpose Driven thinking, psychotherapy thinking, and one I didn’t have up there is this personal prophecy thinking. My gosh. And in a lot of Spirit-filled circles, you know, personal prophecy is just a dime a dozen. Just everybody’s giving out personal prophecies. Where is that in the Bible? They’re just flat out wrong. I don’t need no personal prophecy; I need the book. I need the Bible. Amen. It’s the sure word of prophecy, that’s what the Bible says. Atheist and humanist and everybody’s got their own ideas. And in one of these they talked about atheists, and they said, yeah, everybody can go to heaven. And as Oprah put it, if you’re good— generosity, kindness and love— you can go to heaven no matter what. They’re just lying. Now, over here the end result is a Christian, a disciple of the divine nature. They’re pursuing the divine nature. Hallelujah, because that’s what this faith, Jesus’s faith, whole focus is on: you being a light to the world, living for him by doing good works.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?
2 Peter 1:19: And so we have the prophetic word confirmed, which you do well to heed as a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts;
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

He reads Revelation 21:8 and says it plainly tells who is going to the lake of fire, including the unbelieving, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and all liars. He says homosexuals miss out on two counts, sexual immorality and abomination, and that you cannot change the Bible because you want to be nice to people. He says preachers are not challenging Christians living in sexual immorality, and that America and the homosexual need to hear it so he can get saved and change his ways.
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

Now, Revelation 21:8: “The cowardly, the unbelieving, the abominable”— abomination means God hates it, all right— “murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers,” which is witchcraft, “idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.” And Joel Osteen doesn’t know, and T. D. Jakes doesn’t know, that these people are going to hell, and Rick Warren doesn’t know, and Oprah doesn’t know. It’s very plain in Revelation. This is just one scripture. He tells us plainly who’s going to the lake of fire, and homosexuals miss out on two counts: sexual immorality and abomination. It’s listed under both. Adultery, incest— these sins, will you burn for them? You can’t change the Bible because you want to be nice to people. Can I hear an amen? And Christians are living in sexual immorality and doing all kinds of stupid things, and the preachers aren’t challenging them on Sunday to stop it, and everybody thinks they’re okay. Folks, you can’t change this. Idolatry is an abomination. Idolatry is listed twice up there, under abominations and under idolatry. Are you with me? And all liars: these guys are lying. How many liars go to hell? All of them. Now, folks, this is flagrant lying just so they can get crowds and money. They like the money, man. They live in million-dollar mansions and they drive big cars, and they got all these people coming wanting to hear their flattering messages. And America needs to hear that that’s wrong, and the Christians need to hear, the homosexual needs to hear that he’s wrong, so that he can get saved and change his ways. Can I hear an amen?
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

Revelation 21:8: But the cowardly, unbelieving, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.”
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

He says “I believe” is used four times in the passages he reads and every time it means believing that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the only begotten Son of God, or believing that God will do what he said he would do. He reads the statements in John 11, John 9, Acts 8 and Acts 27, and says that is what “I believe” should say, not that any sin is fine and you can still go to heaven.
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

But so, the adulterers. John 11:27, the statement of “I believe”: “I believe you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.” Okay. “I believe” is used four times, and every time it’s used this way. All right: I believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the only begotten Son of God. Lucifer is not a begotten Son of God. Lucifer was a created being. Jesus was birthed in the flesh by God. Amen. John 9:35: “Do you believe on the Son of God?” Jesus asked the man. He said, “Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him?” Jesus said, “You have seen him, and it is he that talks with you.” I’m him, Jesus said. The man quickly says, “I believe.” I believe what? That you are the Son of God, that Jesus is the Son of God. How many believe that Jesus is the only begotten Son of God? Yeah. See, that’s what “I believe” should say: not “I believe homos can go to heaven,” and, “Oh, you know, I can get intoxicated and still go to heaven,” and all the rest. No. Acts 8:37: Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may get baptized,” and the eunuch said, “I believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God.” He said it again. Paul, in Acts 27:25, on the island— or before he got to the island, on the boat: “Be of good cheer, I believe God.” What’s the statement? “I believe God that it shall be as it was told me.” Now, that sums it up: I believe that God will do what he said he would do. Amen. I can’t come up with my own little gizmo doctrines, my feel-good doctrines.
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

John 11:27: She said to Him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.” John 9:35-37: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when He had found him, He said to him, “Do you believe in the Son of God?” He answered and said, “Who is He, Lord, that I may believe in Him?” And Jesus said to him, “You have both seen Him and it is He who is talking with you.” Acts 8:37: Then Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may.” And he answered and said, “I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.” Acts 27:25: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be just as it was told me.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

He says ministers are supposed to preach the Bible, and the Bible already judges, so telling people they are going to hell is telling them what the Bible said, not judging them himself. He compares it to a doctor who will not tell a patient with cancer he is going to die, and says Paul boldly told the Jews who rejected the word that they had judged themselves unworthy of eternal life.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

The Bible, in judging: you hear them all say they wouldn’t judge. You hear that? I’m not going to judge anybody. Well, no, all sinned. T. D. Jakes, all not going to judge: I’m not going to judge. Well, the Bible already judges it. And ministers are supposed to be preaching the Bible. See, I’m not judging people when I, you know, when I tell people you’re going to hell. I’m telling them what the Bible said. God’s judgment is you’re going to hell. And I told you people last year said nobody talks like that. I said, the Bible talks like that. And can you imagine going in for cancer, and the doctors don’t want to make a judgment? They don’t want to tell you that you’re going to die, and they just say, oh, you’re just fine, you’re just fine, you’re not going to die, you don’t need treatment, you’re just— you don’t need any kind of treatment, you don’t need any kind of medicine or anything else, you know. And in the end you what? Die, when you could have got some treatment and lived. And these preachers don’t want to tell people they’re going to die. See, the lake of fire we read is the second death. You’re going to die for eternity. The Jews opposed things spoken by Paul, in Acts 13:45. So Paul boldly said— Paul what? Boldly said. He didn’t sit there silently and, well, I’m not going to judge. Well, you know, I haven’t read into that, I don’t have knowledge. No, he boldly said, “It was necessary the word of God be spoken to you first, you Jews, but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we’re going to the Gentiles.” See, they judged themselves. They made a decision themselves to miss out on eternal life.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

Acts 13:45-46: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy; and contradicting and blaspheming, they opposed the things spoken by Paul. Then Paul and Barnabas grew bold and said, “It was necessary that the word of God should be spoken to you first; but since you reject it, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

He says 1 Corinthians 6 asks whether the saints will judge the world and angels, so they are not unworthy to judge the smallest matters of this life. He reads Acts 15:19, where the decision is to write to the Gentiles to abstain from idols, sexual immorality, things strangled and blood, and he says ministers should make that judgment today.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

1 Corinthians 6:2: “Do you not know that the saints would judge the world?” Whoo! Are you out there, church? “If the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?” You can’t make decisions on the least little thing! You got these homosexuals and these Oprah telling you that— “Judge not, lest you be not judged. For what judgment you judge you shall be judged.” Come on! “Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more things that pertain to this life?” Are we supposed to make judgments concerning this life? Yeah. Are we to make judgment on the very smallest matters, whether we buy a car we can’t afford, or will we buy a car we can’t afford? Are we supposed to make judgments? Yeah. Good grief. Raise your child up in the way they should go, or raise them up the way Dr. Spock said they should go? We got to make— we’re to make judgment. They’re lying to you, people out there. Acts 15:19: “I judge.” What did he say? “I judge.” [Editor’s note: in Acts 15:19 the speaker is James, not Paul.] Oh my gosh, [unclear] is going to fall off his chair. Oprah and T. D. Jakes and Warren, what’s this? What are they going to do with this scripture? Paul’s judging. He’s making a decision. What’s his decision? “That we should not trouble the Gentiles who are turning to God, but that we write to them to abstain from things polluted by idols, sexual immorality, things strangled, and from blood.” Sexual immorality: no homosexuality, no adultery, no incest, no sex with kids, all sex in the marriage. That’s it. And he made that judgment. Don’t you think ministers should be making that judgment today? Absolutely.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

1 Corinthians 6:2-3: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters? Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life? Matthew 7:1-2: “Judge not, that you be not judged. For with what judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you. Acts 15:19-20: Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from among the Gentiles who are turning to God, but that we write to them to abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from things strangled, and from blood.
Why are so many Christians weak, and what should they do?

He says God’s people are weak because they listen to weak preachers and do not have enough discipline to read the Bible themselves every day. He says Christians in trouble are non-readers who go to Bible studies mostly to associate with a group, and that they should get a connection with Jesus and his word, since we go to church to spiritualize, not socialize.
Why are so many Christians weak, and what should they do?

God’s people are wimps because they’re listening to wimpy ministers. That’s right. They’re weak because they listen to weak preachers, and they ain’t got enough discipline to get on their knees and open that Bible up themselves and read a proverb a day and read [unclear] a day and read the Bible every day. I guarantee you, Christians that are in trouble are non-readers, and they don’t go to Bible studies where they actually hear somebody expound and open up the scriptures to them. They go to Bible studies mostly to associate, you know, they’re associating with this group, they got a connection with the group. You better get a connection with Jesus and his word. Yeah, that’s worth a clap. We don’t go to church to socialize. These churches, America’s churches, have got it wrong. We go to church to spiritualize. We need to become better spiritual people. Hallelujah.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

He reads 1 Corinthians 5 and says Paul told the church not to keep company with the sexually immoral and others in the list, and that those inside the church are to be judged while God judges those outside. He says the man there was committing incest, and Paul passed a judgment to kick him out of the church.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

1 Corinthians 5:9: “I wrote to you not to keep company with sexually immoral brethren, or greedy people, extortioners”— and revilers, they that blast people with their mouth— “drunkard, or idolaters. Not to eat with such a person. What have I to do with judging outsiders? Do you not judge those who are inside?” Did you hear that? “But those outside God judges. For this reason, put away yourselves from that evil person.” This guy was committing incest. He was having sex with his father’s wife, and Paul passed a judgment to kick this guy out of the church, and he told the Corinthian church, you got to make decisions.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

1 Corinthians 5:9-13: I wrote to you in my epistle not to keep company with sexually immoral people. Yet I certainly did not mean with the sexually immoral people of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or idolaters, since then you would need to go out of the world. But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone named a brother, who is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a person. For what have I to do with judging those also who are outside? Do you not judge those who are inside? But those who are outside God judges. Therefore “put away from yourselves the evil person.”
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

He reads 2 Corinthians 5:14 and calls it basic kindergarten Christianity: if Christ died for you, you should live not for yourself but for him. He says selfishness is why churches have problems, and that following Jesus’s example means laying down our life, working, getting married, staying married and raising children right.
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

2 Corinthians 5:14: “The love of Christ compels, because we judge this: if one died for all, then all died, and he died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves.” Good Lord, that’s so simple. That’s basic kindergarten Christianity: that if Christ died for you, you should be living not for yourself but for him who died for you and rose again. Can I hear an amen? I don’t have to live to please Rick Warren or T. D. Jakes or Joel Osteen. I’ve got to please Jesus Christ. Amen. And let me tell you something, church: selfishness is why you got your problems. You’re only thinking about yourself and your feelings and what you want, and it creates problems. You just want your own way because you feel it’s right. Jesus, our example, laid down his life for us. If we’re going to follow his example, we’re going to what? Lay down our life. We’re not going to do what we want to do; we’re going to do what he wants us to do. Amen. We’re going to work, we’re going to get married, we’re going to stay married, we’re going to raise children, we’re going to raise them right. We judge this way. Are we to judge? Yes.
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

2 Corinthians 5:14-15: For the love of Christ compels us, because we judge thus: that if One died for all, then all died; and He died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

He reads 1 Corinthians 14:29, let two or three prophets speak and let the others judge, and says he has a right to decide whether what ministers say is scripturally correct. He says personal prophecy has no one to verify it and that prophets should not be wrong, and that people must depend on the scriptures. He also says we are to judge ourselves, and that the Sermon on the Mount means start with yourself before helping a brother with a splinter.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

1 Corinthians 14:29: “Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others”— what? Judge. See, I have a right to take what Joel Osteen, Rick Warren, T. D. Jakes and Oprah and all these guys say. I have a right to make a decision if they’re scripturally correct. And I’m not out to lambaste the brethren or to divide the church. I am out to speak the truth so people can know the truth and the truth can set them free. Is that an amen? I mean, it plainly says when somebody’s talking, there’s got to be somebody checking out whether they’re saying it right or not. Hallelujah. And that’s where personal prophecy goes right out the tube. There’s no one there to verify you’re speaking right. And let me tell you, I’ve heard a lot of lousy personal prophecies, and I just flat out— to him, you’re wrong, you missed it, bud. I mean, no, I can prophesy too. I mean, they act like they’re the only ones that’s got the gift, but let me tell you, I can prophesy. And when these prophets come in and they said this, that and the other, I said, you’re wrong. And they go, no way. I said, I got the proof, you’re wrong. I know that person, and this is why you’re wrong. They got mad at me. But prophets should not be wrong. Can I hear an amen? And getting people dependent on your personal prophecies, that’s not scriptural. People have got to get dependent on the scriptures. Amen. And prophecies are good when they confirm and all that, but when they don’t, and they’re out of line, it’s destructive. 1 Corinthians 11:30: “Many are weak and sick among you, many are dead already, for if you would judge yourselves you would not be judged.” So we are to what? Judge ourselves. And that’s what the Sermon on the Mount is talking about when he says, “Judge not, lest you be judged. For with what judgment you judge you shall be judged,” and what you give out you’ll get given back to you. You better first get the 2x4 out of your eye, he said, so that you can see clearly to help the brother get a splinter out of his eye. All it’s saying is you start with yourself.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

1 Corinthians 14:29: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge. John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Corinthians 11:30-31: For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep. For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged. Matthew 7:1-5: “Judge not, that you be not judged. For with what judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you. And why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but do not consider the plank in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye’; and look, a plank is in your own eye? Hypocrite! First remove the plank from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

He reads Jeremiah 3:15, where God promises shepherds after his heart who feed with knowledge and understanding, and says people are destroyed for lack of knowledge because preachers in America are making them feel good instead of helping them grow and change. He says Christian divorce, children out of marriage and single-parent homes are as high as in the secular world, and that something is wrong.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

God’s solution for defective, deflective disciples and ministers: here’s his solution. Are you ready? Jeremiah 3:15: “I will give you shepherds according to my heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.” The Bible says, “For lack of knowledge my people are destroyed,” and gone into captivity. They lack knowledge. And why? Because preachers in America aren’t giving them the knowledge to make decisions during the week. They’re making them feel good where they’re at. They’re not growing, they’re not changing, and they wind up destroying themselves. Christian divorce is just as high as secular divorce. Christians having kids out of marriage is just as high as the secular. Christians in a single-parent home is just as high as the secular. Something’s wrong, church. Yes. The results aren’t there. At that time— I love this— he says he’s going to do it, and he tells us what’s going to happen at that time. Jerusalem— Hebrews 12 tells us Jerusalem is the church. Okay. At that time the church shall be called the Throne of the Lord. He is Lord; he’s ruling. We are following him. I love that. Do you see that? He’s not in a lot of churches. The throne is not in a lot of churches. The pastor is on the throne, because these people are worshiping pastors and ministers.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

Jeremiah 3:15: And I will give you shepherds according to My heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding. Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. Hebrews 12:22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

He says Jerusalem is the church and that at that time it shall be called the Throne of the Lord, with all nations gathered to the name of the Lord, which is Jesus. He says in a lot of churches the pastor is on the throne instead, and that we gather to the King, not a minister or a group. He says we know the time we are in when we are doing what he wants, not what we want.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

“And all nations shall be gathered to the throne” that’s in the church now. Is that Bible? We don’t gather to a minister or a group. We gather to the King on the throne in the church. Wow. “To the name of the Lord.” What’s his name? Jesus. Don’t give me no Buddha stuff. Don’t give me no Joseph Smith stuff. Don’t give me no [unclear]— I mean, Moroni, some angel that’s supposed to give— don’t give me that garbage. Give me Jesus. It’s his name I gather unto, it’s his throne together unto, and it’s his word that I must follow. Now, that was good. No more— listen to this. See, you can tell what the time is. Am I making sense to you? I’m trying to give you Revelation here that can change your life. See, we can know what time frame we’re in. Are we in the time where the church has the throne of the Lord, and nations are gathering to the throne, and the King on the throne, and his name? “No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.” See, we know what time and what season we’re in when we aren’t doing what we want to do; we’re doing what he wants us to do. Oh gosh, that was good.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
Should you leave a church where Jesus is not on the throne?

He says to stop listening to shepherds who flatter you, because it is the word that sets you free, heals you and makes you grow. He says that if you are going to a church where he is not on the throne and people are doing what they want to do, you are in the wrong group, so get to where you can get fed and grow.
Should you leave a church where Jesus is not on the throne?

Oh, church, and you got to make decisions, and you got to stop listening to these idiot shepherds, because they flatter you and make you feel good. It’s the word that sets you free. It’s the word that heals you. It’s the word that causes you to grow. When we get distracted and deflect from the word, and deflect from the living word, Jesus, we’re going to fall into problems. Christians don’t have any power and strength today. They can’t overcome sin, and the preacher just feeds them: they’re okay where they’re at. “No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil heart.” When you come to that place, you know you’re in this time, and you’re in the right group. And see, if you’re going to a church where he isn’t on the throne and not gathering to his name, and that people are doing what they want to do, you’re in the wrong group, man. Get out. Get to where you can get fed, get to where you can grow, get to where we can do something for Christ in this world together. Can I hear an amen?
Should you leave a church where Jesus is not on the throne?

Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
What is virtue, and why is cowardice listed as a sin?

He says the first thing added to baby doctrine is virtue, which is the courage to live and stand up for Bible morals, and you have to add it to your faith. He says that if you will not tell your spouse, children, parents, neighbors and enemies Bible truths and Bible morality you are a coward, and that it is still the foolishness of preaching that saves people.
What is virtue, and why is cowardice listed as a sin?

Cowardly. Are you a coward today? You know, the first thing added to baby doctrine is virtue. Virtue is the courage to live and stand up for Bible morals, and you got to add that to your faith. Am I right? I’m just giving you Bible scriptures. And when you are a coward and you won’t stand up— I’m talking about your spouse, your children, your parents, your brothers and sisters, your neighbors, your enemies— and you don’t tell them Bible truths and Bible morality, you are a coward. What’s going to save them? They got to know. It’s still the foolishness of preaching that saves people.
What is virtue, and why is cowardice listed as a sin?

2 Peter 1:5: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe.
What do abominations, hatred, witchcraft and lying mean in Revelation 21:8?

He says there are about thirty-three abominations in the Bible and that Christians who hate others over skin color or social status are included under the New Testament teaching that hatred is the same as murder. He says Christians should not be afraid of witches because there is no witchcraft against God’s people, and that liars will have their part in the lake of fire, so do not be afraid to say it.
What do abominations, hatred, witchcraft and lying mean in Revelation 21:8?

Unbelieving: and we saw these disciples were what? Unbelievers, in John 6. Abominable things that God hates, which is idolatry, homosexuality, rape, things like that. There’s a whole list. There’s about thirty-three abominations in the Bible. There’s a whole— God hates them. Murderers: Jesus said if you hate— or the New Testament says if you hate, that is the same as murder. And we got Christians that hate skin color, social status, whatever. We have hatred, despise, we look down on people. Sexually immoral, sorcerers, witchcraft. And I meet Christians in the witchcraft, and I meet Christians that are afraid of witches. Back at the Vine, these women got together and they read this book about how the witches were keeping Christian churches from growing and affecting the church, and I go, that’s not true. The Bible says there is no witchcraft against God’s people. Those witches can do all they want to do; it has no effect on the church. And they just look, well, you don’t know everything. I don’t, but the book knows everything. Ain’t no witch doctor can get outside the church and do the [unclear] thing and have any effect on us. Are you there? But silly women— Paul said led astray. But you know, silly women, you got to watch, women, don’t— don’t be silly. Amen. Don’t be foolish. And “all liars shall have their part in a lake of burns with fire.” Were these guys lying? Were they lying? Absolutely. Don’t be afraid to say it, and don’t be afraid to email them and say, that’s not scripture. You know, I learned from people telling me like it was, because I wanted to be told like it was. I didn’t learn from people that were wimps. I didn’t learn from people that didn’t take an interest in people. I learned from people that took an interest in people, the right interest.
What do abominations, hatred, witchcraft and lying mean in Revelation 21:8?

1 John 3:15: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. Numbers 23:23: “For there is no sorcery against Jacob, Nor any divination against Israel. It now must be said of Jacob And of Israel, ‘Oh, what God has done!’ 2 Timothy 3:6: For of this sort are those who creep into households and make captives of gullible women loaded down with sins, led away by various lusts,
Why should Christians speak up instead of staying silent?

He says people who come to church, never share Christ with anybody and go home are silent saints who have no effect in the kingdom. He says that when you really know something it is natural to talk about it, without pumping up courage, and that you should speak the truth and not argue, since if one person is silent the argument ends.
Why should Christians speak up instead of staying silent?

You know, there’s people that come to church and they never share Christ with anybody. They have no effect and [unclear] in the kingdom at all. They just come, hear a sermon, go, oh wow, what a great sermon. Hallelujah. Do their little thing that they do in their church and then go home, and they’re silent saints. They are worthless. And I’m looking at some today. We got the internet; you can talk to anybody. I told you I went right to Utah, talked right to headquarters. How you know it’s time to speak up, hallelujah: it’s natural. When you really experience something and you know something, it’s just natural to talk about it. It isn’t like you got to get the courage up and pump it up. It’s just natural. You know, when somebody’s into baseball, it’s natural that they talk about baseball, right? People that are into God and truth, it’s just natural to speak truth, and you don’t have to argue about it. Just speak it and shut up. The Bible says it takes two people to argue; if one is silent, the argument ends. If you read your Proverbs you would know, but most of you do not read your Proverbs every day, principles of life. Someone was telling me this week they got into a heated argument. I said, well, if you’d have just shut up after you said your statement, that wouldn’t have been a heated argument. Amen. I mean, what’s the sense, and just keep harping on it, harping on it, harping on it? Just say it and go on. Let God do the work. Can I hear an amen?
What responsibility do believers have to get this message out?

He says to whom much is given much is required, so the church has a responsibility to get organized and tell everyone, believer and unbeliever alike, that Bible morality is part of getting into heaven. He says Bible morality, not psychotherapy and positive thinking, is what blesses a family and helps people in the church, and that it challenges immoral people to change.
What responsibility do believers have to get this message out?

They’re all going to the lake of fire, folks. Now, because we know that to whom much is given, much is required, we have a responsibility to get this word out. We have a responsibility, church, to get organized and get out this message to everyone, believer and unbeliever alike, that Bible morality is part of getting into heaven. Amen. And Bible morality is what blesses my family. That’s what’s going to encourage my children, being an example and teaching them and directing them that way. That’s what’s going to help my family. It isn’t psychotherapy and positive thinking. Bible morality is what’s going to help people in the church, and it’s going to challenge the unmoral people to change their way. And that’s what the basic gospel is all about.
What responsibility do believers have to get this message out?

Luke 12:48: But he who did not know, yet committed things deserving of stripes, shall be beaten with few. For everyone to whom much is given, from him much will be required; and to whom much has been committed, of him they will ask the more.
What does he say prosperity, positive thinking and similar movements have in common?

He lists prosperity, positive, possibility, Purpose Driven, psychotherapy and personal prophecy thinking together, tied to the idea of saying “my faith” and “I believe” with nothing wrong with it. He says that in the Bible there is no place for personal prophecy and that he needs the book.
Does he say Lucifer is a son of God?
He says Lucifer is not a begotten Son of God, and was a created being. He says Jesus was birthed in the flesh by God and is the only begotten Son of God.
Why does he compare telling people the truth to a doctor and cancer?

He says a doctor who tells a patient he is fine and does not need treatment lets the patient die when he could have got treatment and lived. He says preachers who will not tell people they are going to die for eternity, the second death of the lake of fire, are doing the same.
Why does he say we go to church?

He says we do not go to church to socialize but to spiritualize, to become better spiritual people. He says many go to Bible studies mostly to associate with a group, and that they should get a connection with Jesus and his word.
What does he say the Corinthian church was told to do about a man who had his father’s wife?

He says Paul passed a judgment to kick the man out of the church and told the Corinthian church they had to make decisions. He points to the passage that says to judge those inside the church while God judges those outside.
What does he call basic kindergarten Christianity?

He says it is that if Christ died for you, you should be living not for yourself but for him who died for you and rose again. He says he does not have to live to please any minister but has to please Jesus Christ.
Why does he say selfishness is the cause of problems in the church?

He says people are only thinking about themselves, their feelings and what they want, and they just want their own way because they feel it is right. He says Jesus laid down his life for us, so if we follow his example we lay down our life and do what he wants, not what we want.
What does he say about prophets who are wrong?

He says that he has heard a lot of lousy personal prophecies and told the prophets they were wrong, and some got mad at him. He says prophets should not be wrong, and that prophecies are good when they confirm but destructive when they are out of line.
What does he say about Christian divorce and single-parent homes?

He says Christian divorce, Christians having kids out of marriage and Christians in single-parent homes are each just as high as in the secular world. He says something is wrong in the church and that the results are not there.
What does he say about witchcraft and the church?

He says he meets Christians who are afraid of witches, and that some women in the church read a book about how witches were keeping churches from growing. He says that is not true: the Bible says there is no witchcraft against God’s people, and no witch doctor can have an effect on the church.
How does he say you know it is time to speak up?

He says it is natural when you really experience something to talk about it, like someone into baseball talking about baseball. He says people into God and truth naturally speak truth, and you do not have to argue about it.
What does he say about avoiding heated arguments?

He says you can say your statement and shut up, since it takes two people to argue and if one is silent the argument ends. He says there is no sense in harping on it again and again; just say it and go on and let God do the work.

items.d: In “God Destroys Nations,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the Old Testament events are real and written for our learning, and uses Sodom and Lot to say what God judges a nation for. He reads Jude 7 and Ezekiel…
p: In “God Destroys Nations,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the Old Testament events are real and written for our learning, and uses Sodom and Lot to say what God judges a nation for. He reads Jude 7 and Ezekiel 16:49 to list Sodom’s sins, including sexual immorality, pride, idleness and not strengthening the poor, and compares them to America. He closes with what he says the church must do and why the judgment message has to be preached.
Did the events in the Bible really happen, or are they just allegories?

Pastor Kincer says the things written in the Old Testament happened: the six-day creation, the flood, Noah’s ark, Jonah’s great fish and the virgin birth all occurred. He says science can only explain natural things, not supernatural ones, and that these real events were written for our learning, as illustrations.
Did the events in the Bible really happen, or are they just allegories?

And when God decides to destroy a nation, it’s just going to fall. That’s the bottom line. “Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for” what? Our learning. So what we want to learn something, where do we go? The Bible, the Old Testament, the New Testament. They’re written for us to learn. 1 Corinthians 10:11: “All these things happened”— they what? Happened. They occurred. Bill O’Reilly on Fox News is wrong. The homosexuals are wrong, the atheists are wrong, the humanists are wrong, that say the Bible is a book of myths and allegories and so forth. “These things happened.” They occurred. They took place. God created the world in six days: it happened. God flooded the world: it happened. God had Noah to build an ark: it happened. God prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah: it happened. Are you with me? Jesus was born of a virgin: it happened. It occurred. And Bill O’Reilly’s wrong when he says he proves that the Bible is a book of allegories by using science. Science can never explain supernatural things. Science only explains natural things that any bird brain can look into and figure out how it worked. God is the one that created the working.
Did the events in the Bible really happen, or are they just allegories?
1 Corinthians 10:11: Now all these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.
Is all Scripture inspired by God, and what is it for?

He says all scripture is given by the inspiration of God and you cannot take anything out, such as the virgin birth or the atonement, as liberal churches do. He says the purpose of the Bible is teaching us how to live right, and that we were saved by Jesus to live right, and if we are not living right we are not saved.
Is all Scripture inspired by God, and what is it for?

“And it happened to them for examples”— illustrations. This is the allegorical part: these real occurrences happened to teach us, illustrations, so we can learn by, and “written for our admonition”— our warning, our encouragement, correction— “upon whom the ends of the world are come.” “All scripture is given by the inspiration of God.” How many scriptures? All of it. You can’t take it out. You can’t take the virgin birth out. You can’t take the atonement, the blood of Christ, out of the Bible like the liberal churches do. You can’t do that. “All scripture is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.” Instruction in what? Righteousness. The purpose of the Bible: teaching us how to live right, “that the man of God might be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all” what? Good works. These people that say that, you know, we don’t have works— we do. We have good works. “Let your light so shine before men that they may see your” what? Good works. You were saved by Jesus to live right, and if you’re not living right, you’re not saved.
Is all Scripture inspired by God, and what is it for?
