items.ser: To Cover or Not to Cover · Part 2
tg: To Cover or Not to Cover
p: In “To Cover or Not to Cover Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer finishes his study of 1 Corinthians 11, saying Paul answers male ego arguments with the truth that man and woman were both made in God’s image and are one in Christ. He argues that “power on her head because of the angels” means real authority, not a symbol, and that Paul’s phrase about nature and long hair is about origin and a woman’s hair being given to her as a covering. He ends with Paul’s final answer, that the churches of God have no such custom.
Were both men and women made in the image of God?

He says Genesis 1:26-28 shows both were made in the image of God and given dominion, and that Paul knows this but is “concentrating on these male egos.” God said “let us,” not “I will,” so the Godhead is plural, and “mankind” means the human race, not male. He adds that the woman was given the same blessing, “but Paul left that part out.”
Were both men and women made in the image of God?

Genesis 1:26, we got to make it clear that both were made in the image of God. See, Paul knows this, but he didn’t bring out the fact that the woman was made in the image of God also. See, Paul knows this, but he didn’t bring it out. Why? He is concentrating on these male egos that he is going to bury here in a couple of verses. “Let us make man in our image.” There’s the plural: “let us.” God didn’t say “I will,” He said “let us.” The Godhead is plural. Do you understand that? Jesus was back there at the beginning. “Let us make man,” mankind; it’s not man, male; it’s mankind. A lot of words for man in the Bible is mankind, the human race. It’s not male at all. “Let us make the human race in our” what? “Image.” There’s the plural again: “our” is plural. “After our likeness, and let them have dominion.” So God created man. Verse 27, “in His own image, male and female created He” what? “Them.” And both of them what? Were made in the image of God, the likeness of God, and had dominion; they had rulership. Yes. Jeez. Now more ego, self-important arguments: “for the man is not of the woman, but the woman of the man; neither was the man created for the woman, but the woman was created for the man.” Man, he’s really got him going. Genesis 1:28, “God blessed” what? Plural: man and woman. And God said to what? “Them,” plural, man and woman, Adam and Eve: “Be fruitful, multiply, replenish the earth, subdue it, and have dominion and authority over every living thing.” We got to understand that the woman was given the same blessing, but Paul left that part out. Why? He’s feeding these guys. They’re really feeling good right now. Yeah, man. “Get that babushka on your head. Woman, keep quiet in the church. Woman.”
Were both men and women made in the image of God?

Genesis 1:26-28: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness; let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over the cattle, over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.” So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them. Then God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it; have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.” 1 Corinthians 11:8-9: For man is not from woman, but woman from man. Nor was man created for the woman, but woman for the man.
What does “power on her head because of the angels” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:10?

He says nowhere in the Bible does it say a woman has to have power over her head because of the angels, and that several translations say “power” is the sign of the husband’s authority, which he calls “a big mistake.” He says the word means real supernatural power, as in Matthew 28:18 and Luke 10:19, and that angels are spirit beings who do not need a covering, while Satan acts like an angel of light.
What does “power on her head because of the angels” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:10?

Now verse 10, “For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.” Now, folks, nowhere in the Bible does it say a woman’s got to have power over her head because of the angels, and you got to watch your translations here. Here’s a good example: the New King James, the NIV, New International Version, the Living Bible, the Amplified Bible, the American Standard Bible all say “power” is the sign of the husband’s authority, and that’s a big mistake. If you’re going to deal with angels, you don’t want a sign, you don’t want a symbol, you want power. Are you there? And see, we read our Bible and we just accept; we don’t dig. King James has it right, the Darby Bible has it right. The word “power” there is the same word that the Bible uses all through, showing that there’s supernatural power, there is authority. Okay, in Matthew 9:6, “the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins.” Now do you want Him to have a symbol of that, or you want Him to have the power? The power. All right, Matthew 10:1, Jesus gave His twelve disciples power over unclean spirits, and to heal all manner of sicknesses, and to preach. Did He give them a symbol of power? You know, here’s a dove, here, go preach, you; a symbol of a dove, or symbol of a fish, or whatever we symbolize? No, He gave them power. He gave authority. Matthew 28:18, “All power is given unto Me in heaven and earth.” Does He have a symbol of power? Does He have power? Is He the authority over all the earth? You see, He is. And listen to this, Luke 10:19, “I give you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions,” talking to us, “and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.” Now do you want a symbol of power or do you want the power? Yeah. The Devil don’t care if you got a symbol. He doesn’t care if you wear a cross; it doesn’t bother him a bit. What he cares is who the strong man of your house is. Jesus Christ is living in you, and he can’t do anything without Jesus’s permission. That’s power. And so he’s really got these guys right where he wants them, right? Now, angels. What angels? We know there are angels of God, messengers that minister to us, isn’t that right? Hebrews 1, yes. Okay, that, you know, if the angel comes to a woman to minister to her and she doesn’t have a babushka on her head, “Yeah, oh, I can’t come. You know, oh, I can’t talk to you, you don’t have a covering.” I mean, what kind of wimpy angel is he? See, when the angel came to Rebecca and showed her about the two boys that she had, and didn’t reveal it to Isaac, it doesn’t say anything about, “Well, she’s got a covering on her head, so I can talk to her,” or “If she doesn’t have a covering, I can’t talk to her.” Come on. Angels could care the least; they’re spirit beings. Are you with me? Okay, but Satan is as an angel of light. Whoa, that changes everything, doesn’t it? He acts like an angel of light, and he’s not.
What does “power on her head because of the angels” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:10?

1 Corinthians 11:10: For this reason the woman ought to have a symbol of authority on her head, because of the angels. Matthew 9:6: But that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins”—then He said to the paralytic, “Arise, take up your bed, and go to your house.” Matthew 10:1: And when He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease. Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Luke 10:19: Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you. Hebrews 1:14: Are they not all ministering spirits sent forth to minister for those who will inherit salvation? 2 Corinthians 11:14: And no wonder! For Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.
Do husbands and pastors need real authority or a symbol of authority?

He says a husband needs real authority and power, not a symbol of it, and that real leadership is not pushing and kicking people around: like a cord, if you lead, it follows. He says husbands should follow Christ and their wife will have no problem following, and a pastor should lead the church and not “beat them up every Sunday.”
Do husbands and pastors need real authority or a symbol of authority?

Does she need authority or a symbol of authority when Satan comes to tempt and seduce and test her? She needs authority, and she needs a husband with authority. She don’t need no husband with a symbol of authority. “I’m a delegated authority; I’m a big deal, bud.” We need some action in this home. Amen. That husband needs authority; he needs power. Okay, I want to get this cord over there. I can push, kick, push, and nothing is happening. And this is what a lot of people think leadership is: just beat people up, push them, kick them around, get moving. But if I just lead this cord, it follows me. No effort, no nothing. I get it where it belongs, we both get there, and the key, husbands, is to be a leader. Do what Paul said: follow Christ, and your wife will have no problem following you. You try to push your ways on her and force your ways on her, and especially when they’re your traditions, she’s got no choice but to follow Christ. Now that was good. Amen. Same with a pastor of a church. If you want your church to get to the high mark of the calling of God, lead them into it. Don’t beat them up every Sunday; lead them there. That way they can reject you for leading, but they can’t reject you for bullying and pushing and being lord over you. That’s a good place for an amen. I told you this Paul’s good.
How do we stand against Satan and his angels, with a symbol or real authority?

He says another word for angels is messenger, and that when demons come around you need the real authority of Christ, not a symbol, with both husband and wife under the power of Christ. He says if people reject you they are rejecting the one who sent you, and that the bigger problem than demons is people who follow Satan with their own traditions and doctrines, which you need authority to withstand.
How do we stand against Satan and his angels, with a symbol or real authority?

Now Satan has angels, Satan and his angels. Another word for angels is messenger. Okay, when these little demons come around trying to mess with you and all that, do you need a symbol of authority or do you need real authority? You need the real thing. Husband, we need to get with it in the home. We need to get under that power of Christ, and a woman needs to be under the power of Christ, and as a team nothing’s going to mess with that home. Hallelujah. And we both lead these kids in the ways that are right. Now John the Baptist was called a messenger. John’s disciples were called messengers. Jesus sent His disciples to a Samaritan village to announce He was coming there, and it says they were messengers, and when they got there and said, “Jesus has come,” they said, “We don’t want Him,” and so they rejected the messengers because they rejected the One who sent the messengers. And if people reject you, it’s not you they’re rejecting; they’re rejecting the One that sent you with the message. Now Satan has children, the children of the wicked one, and Matthew 13, the parable of the sower. So demons aren’t really your big problem once you get Christ; it’s these people that follow Satan, and they come up with their own traditions, their own doctrines, their own way of doing things, and you need authority to withstand them. You need authority to reject their message. Ain’t that right? And a scarf isn’t going to do nothing. You know, I got a scarf on me, man, Hitler ain’t going to bother me, I got a scarf.
How do we stand against Satan and his angels, with a symbol or real authority?

Luke 9:52-53: and sent messengers before His face. And as they went, they entered a village of the Samaritans, to prepare for Him. But they did not receive Him, because His face was set for the journey to Jerusalem. Matthew 13:38: The field is the world, the good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, but the tares are the sons of the wicked one.
What does “neither is the man without the woman” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:11-12?

He says Paul concludes his ego arguments by showing they prove nothing: in the Lord neither is the man without the woman nor the woman without the man, and all things come from God. He says that “when we come to Christ, this nonsense is gone,” and that men did not get here unless a woman brought them into the world, so get your ego back “down to earth.”
What does “neither is the man without the woman” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:11-12?

Now Paul concludes these ego arguments. He’s going to conclude that these things prove nothing. I told you he set them up to pop their balloon, and he’s going to prove it by pointing to them that all things come forth from God. “Nevertheless,” but however, “neither is the man without the woman, and the woman without the man, in the Lord.” Say “in the Lord.” In the Lord. See, when we come to Christ, this nonsense is gone. “For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman.” Men, you didn’t get here unless some woman brought you into this world, so let’s just get your ego back down to earth. Ain’t that right? Ain’t Paul good? Yeah. All of a sudden, bam, man, they went from up here to right below the rug real quick.
What does “neither is the man without the woman” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:11-12?

1 Corinthians 11:11-12: Nevertheless, neither is man independent of woman, nor woman independent of man, in the Lord. For as woman came from man, even so man also comes through woman; but all things are from God.
What does it mean to be baptized into Christ and “put on Christ”?

He says everything comes from God, and that in water baptism the sinful nature is put to death and the new creature comes out of the water. It is “not a symbol, an outward sign of an inward work,” he says, but an inward work that God does, as we identify with the death, burial and resurrection of Christ.
What does it mean to be baptized into Christ and “put on Christ”?

“But all things are of,” come forth from who? God. Everything comes from God: the prayer, the prophecy, the traditions, the customs, the rules, the laws, the image, the likeness, the glory, the dominion, the authority, all come from who? God. Now I know you guys knew all this stuff. I’m just boring you with warmed-over meals here, but look here, it’s backed up also in the Scriptures. Galatians 3:27, “As many of you have been baptized into Christ have” what? “Put on Christ.” In water baptism you kill the sinful nature. Water baptism is not a symbol, an outward sign of an inward work; it is an inward work God does. Things in water baptism that you need to know: the old nature of man, of sin, is put to death, and the new creature, the man of righteousness, Christ, we put on Him, comes out of that water. Amen. Water baptism is important. We identify with the death, burial and resurrection of Christ.
What does it mean to be baptized into Christ and “put on Christ”?
Galatians 3:27: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
Are men and women equal in Christ?

He says that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, “male nor female,” and that God does not see those differences. He says we are all one in Christ Jesus, heirs of the promise, and that Acts 2 says sons and daughters, male and female, will prophesy.
Are men and women equal in Christ?

“There is neither Jew nor Greek.” Greek is a non-Jew, a heathen, unbeliever. “There is no bond or free”: slave. They had slaves there in Corinth, and masters over them. He says you in God, He don’t look at a slave when they come in; He don’t look at a Gentile, a non-Jew. You know, an African comes in or an Asian comes in, God don’t see that, because in Christ these things just don’t happen. “Neither is there” what? “Male nor female.” Wow, he’s plain English there. Amen. “For you are all” what? “One in Christ Jesus. And if you be Christ’s, you’re Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.” Heirs of the image, heirs of the likeness, heirs of prophecy. It says in Acts 2 that “upon your sons and daughters I will pour out My Spirit,” and the son and the daughter, the male and the female, shall what? Prophesy. That’s why that utterance was good today. We should come to the house of God with something to give, not just get. See, you’re contributors. We are heirs. We have authority, we are under authority, we inherited it all, and together we can do great things in the earth. Amen.
Are men and women equal in Christ?

Galatians 3:28-29: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus. And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise. Acts 2:17-18: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy.
Can women be leaders and pastors in the church? What about Deborah?

He says women have been mistreated by people twisting Scriptures to say they cannot speak in church, have a leadership position or be a pastor, and says God is “no respecter of persons.” He says a prophet is higher than a pastor, and points to Deborah as a real leader whom the men followed, with Barak saying he would not go unless she went.
Can women be leaders and pastors in the church? What about Deborah?

Now Acts 10:34 said God is “no respecter of persons.” And this message is getting long, but I got to get this out. Women have experienced mistreatment from people taking Scriptures and twisting them for a long time and misinterpreting them. Long hair, you know, you can’t cut your hair, you got to have long hair; you can’t have styled hair; you can’t have jewelry; you can’t wear pants because men wear pants; you can’t speak in church services; you can’t have a leadership position; you can’t be a pastor. And look, a prophet is higher than a pastor, I don’t know if you know that, and she can prophesy. See, the reason men like that is they don’t want a woman to tell them what to do. Well, don’t that show you you got a heart problem? If the woman is a real leader, Deborah was a real leader, the men did what she said. When Barak was told to go out and defeat the army, he said, “I ain’t going anywhere unless you go, lady.” So here’s Deborah right on the front lines. Man, go get them, boys. Yeah, yeah, whip them, man, beat these guys down. She was on the front lines of that battle. Are you there? Hallelujah. And yes, it’s used a lot less, but it’s still used, and let me tell you, if God depended on men to get everything done in the kingdom, we wouldn’t even be where we’re at today, because men are just big talkers and not doers. That’s the truth. They like to sit there. “Oh yeah, hallelujah, let’s go witnessing.” “No, I’m going to watch football.” You know, “Let’s learn an instrument and let’s prophesy unto the Lord.” “No, no, I’m going to learn how to eat pretzels while I’m watching football.” But boy, when you ask the man anything, he knows it all. Hallelujah. Aren’t you glad you came to church today? They don’t read the Bible, they don’t pray, they don’t learn anything, they can’t even pay attention in Bible studies, you just ask them anything and they know it all.
Can women be leaders and pastors in the church? What about Deborah?

Acts 10:34: Then Peter opened his mouth and said: “In truth I perceive that God shows no partiality. Judges 4:8: And Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go!”
Have women been ministers and leaders throughout church history?

He says history is filled with women ministers: the Methodist movement, the Quakers and the Baptists had women leaders until about the turn of the twentieth century, when someone twisted Paul’s Scriptures. He says the Pentecostals and the Salvation Army kept women in leadership, and describes how limited women’s rights were in the early part of the nation.
Have women been ministers and leaders throughout church history?

Now women in our nation, early part of our nation, could not own property. If they had kids when they divorced, they didn’t get the kids. It was unheard of; you couldn’t do it. You’re a woman, you don’t know how to raise kids. They couldn’t hold political office, they couldn’t vote, they couldn’t be a leader in the workforce, they couldn’t be a leader anywhere. They couldn’t be educated above eighth grade, because they’re just there to take care of the home. And that’s, I mean, that’s true in our nation. Yeah, and yet history is filled with women ministers. John Wesley’s movement, the Methodist movement, had many women preachers and leaders. The Quakers and the Baptists had women leaders till the turn of the twentieth century, when somebody came in, twisted Paul’s Scriptures, and said women got to shut up, and the Baptists and the Quakers accepted it. But the Pentecostals came along at that time, and the Salvation Army, and the Pentecostals had a black leader at Azusa; blacks could not rule over whites back then, do you know that? But when God’s into something, there is neither Jew nor Gentile, Pentecost or Protestant or whatever, black or white; they were just touching God, and everybody wanted God, and women helped him lead the church on Azusa Street.
Why is the woman called “the glory of the man”?

He says “the woman is the glory and the splendor of the man,” the brightness of the man, and that we like our women with their hair fixed up. He goes back to Adam, who named all the animals and could not find a helpmate, and says that when God made the woman from the rib and brought her to Adam, Adam lit up.
Why is the woman called “the glory of the man”?

And in the Pentecostal churches women had a part, most of them anyway. The holiness movement came along. The head of the Salvation, Booth, he got convinced that women should not be preachers. The head of the Salvation Army started the Salvation Army, and then he met this woman called Catherine. And man, you know, remember back there, the woman is the glory and the splendor of the man, the brightness of the man, and we like our women with hair and fixed-up hair. Huh. Yeah. Now you go back to Adam and Eve. Adam, the Bible says, he named all the animals, and yet he couldn’t find a helpmate for him. We’re going to talk about the glory and the splendor of the man. And then God took a rib out, made a woman, woke Adam up, and brought the woman to Adam. Naked. I mean, wow. Can you just see, man, he lit up. I mean, those lions and tigers did nothing, the fishing did nothing. Man, when this, what? And she’s new, she’s naked. Then God brought her. [unclear] And this is where Adam got the first idea of a fig leaf. Man.
Why is the woman called “the glory of the man”?

Genesis 2:19-22: Out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam called each living creature, that was its name. So Adam gave names to all cattle, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper comparable to him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place. Then the rib which the LORD God had taken from man He made into a woman, and He brought her to the man.
Did the Salvation Army’s Booth change his mind about women preachers?

He says Booth had been convinced that women should not be preachers, then married Catherine, a woman preacher who kept on preaching, and when he went to hear her he came back converted. He says the proof was there because people got saved and the Word worked: “what matters is God moved and He used the woman.”
Did the Salvation Army’s Booth change his mind about women preachers?

Yeah, man, he had things in him he didn’t know was there yet. And then God’s given them this big long sermon like I’m giving you today: “Replenish the earth, you know, subdue it, have dominion, I’m making you my likeness in your image, I want you to replenish the earth.” And man, you can just see Adam: “I wish he’d hurry up and shut up. I’ll get [unclear] busy with replenishing this here if he leaves.” And she’s over there [unclear] this guy’s turned on, man, and she’s over there, takes a flower and puts it in her hair. Man, he’s all worked up, and she’s worked up because he’s worked up. Now she’s saying, “When’s this guy going to get done telling us all this? We got to get busy fulfilling replenish and fill the earth.” So when Booth married, guess who he married? Catherine. And guess what? She was a woman preacher. He don’t believe in women preachers. They got a big clash at the beginning, and these two get married. Did she stop preaching because her husband didn’t believe in women preachers anymore? No way. She just kept on doing what she was doing before they got married. And so one day Booth said, “I’m going to go down, check this thing out,” so he goes down to listen to his wife preach, and he came back converted. You see, the evidence was there, the proof was there. People got saved, people got touched, the Word worked. It didn’t matter if it was a woman or what; what matters is God moved and He used the woman. So the proof is there. And so Booth threw his women [unclear] preach doctrine right out the door with one visit, and it was his own wife. See, you can’t argue with the evidence, and if they haven’t got anything to say, then shut up. “We can’t have women speaking,” because women want to speak, they got to have something to say, ain’t that right? “I’m a woman, I’m tired of being beat down all these years, I want to preach.” “You ain’t got anything to say.” “I know, but I’m a woman, I got to make up for all these years of getting persecuted.” Yeah, now you’re going to persecute us, we got to sit there and listen to you say nothing. Anyway, Lutheran, Calvin came up with this “women can’t preach” stuff, and a lot of people fell for it.
Did the Salvation Army’s Booth change his mind about women preachers?

Genesis 1:28: Then God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it; have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
What does “nature itself teach you” about long hair mean in 1 Corinthians 11:14?

He says Paul is always using the word “judge” and telling us to make judgments, and here asks whether it is proper for a woman to pray uncovered. When he tried “nature” as the animal kingdom, the lion did not work, so he says the word means origin, the birthing: men and women are born with certain things about them, and the long hair in the verse is a decorated lock or ornament, not just length.
What does “nature itself teach you” about long hair mean in 1 Corinthians 11:14?

Now Paul gives the answer to the question. Okay, judging yourselves: is it proper that a woman, a wife, pray unto God covered or uncovered? Okay, now here it is again. Paul’s always using this word “judge,” and yet out there in the world they’re saying, “Judge not, let [unclear] be not [unclear].” They take one Scripture of the Bible they don’t even believe in, yet they take the one Scripture when we try to tell them, “You got to change your way,” and, you know, “You judge not, lest you be [unclear], man. Don’t be judging anybody.” And Paul’s always telling us to make judgments, isn’t he? And he’s telling you now, you judge, you make a decision: is it proper that a woman pray and prophesy uncovered, unveiled? “Doesn’t nature itself teach you if a man have long hair it’s a shame to him?” Now when I was a young Christian, you know, I read the books and all that, and the first thing I read about this verse is nature teaches you, the animal kingdom teaches you. And I thought, “Wow, yeah, that’s great, men can’t have long hair because of the animal kingdom.” And the first animal I went to was the lion. And the lioness had no hair, and the lion had all kinds of hair, long hair. I go, “That didn’t work.” I didn’t go any further; I just, it didn’t work. But when I began to look at this word, it doesn’t mean that kind of nature, it means origin, the birthing. You see, us men are birthed with certain things about us, and the women are birthed with certain things about them, and this long hair does not mean long hair as just long hair. All right, he repeats it, and it’s only used two times in the Bible, this word “long hair” here, two times. But if the woman have long hair, you see, it is a glory, a splendor to her. Now here’s the difference: the long hair there is a tassel, a lock, a decorated lock, an ornamental. Women do things with their hair that us men don’t have it in us to do. Are you there?
What does “nature itself teach you” about long hair mean in 1 Corinthians 11:14?

1 Corinthians 11:13-14: Judge among yourselves. Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered? Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him? Matthew 7:1: “Judge not, that you be not judged. 1 Corinthians 11:15: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her; for her hair is given to her for a covering.
Is a woman’s hair her covering?

He says hair is given to her for a covering, so “she don’t need a babushka,” a scarf or a veil. He says it is her splendor and her brightness, and it is about what women do with their hair and why they do it, not its length, and he says Paul gave the Corinthians a bunch of nonsense to bring the truth to them.
Is a woman’s hair her covering?

I mean, when I married Rebecca, she was a gorgeous woman, and she had this hairstyle. Man, I tell you, if she’d have been baldheaded, I’d have went right on by. Why? Because he’s showing us it’s, we’re born, women were born to make their hair attractive and, you know, to decorate it and do things with it. Men weren’t born for that, and it’s got nothing to do with the length; it’s got to do with why they do it. See, no man goes around doing things to their hair. It’s in their right mind that women do, and if they did, they still wouldn’t look good, and I’ll show you that in a minute. And here he answers their question: “her hair is given to her for a” what? “Covering.” She don’t need a babushka, she doesn’t need a scarf, she doesn’t need a veil. Her hair was given to her by God. That’s her splendor, that’s her brightness, and men like her for it. Hallelujah. Now when the hippies were here, they used this to beat the hippies up, and you can’t do that. It’s got to do with what women do with their hair and the look they have. I mean, when Rebecca walked down the street, man, she turned all heads with that hair and that face of hers, and every, wow. Wow. You shave her head and they would know about it, they’d be looking all right. Amen. Now isn’t Paul good? I mean, he gave them a bunch of nonsense to bring the truth to them, and they fell for it, just like you have been falling for it all these years reading these Scriptures. Here is a Jewish couple back in Christ’s day; they both have a covering on their head. All right, here is a Greek couple. Okay, you see the little decoration she’s got, these little curly things hanging down, and this braid going across the front and all that. That’s what women do. They think up these ways to, yeah, get their men all excited, in love with it, and we love it. Okay, here’s an Asian couple. Now check that guy. I mean, what’s that thing on his head? Good Lord. But look at his wife, man, she’s got long hair, and it’s all, I mean, oh wow. Here’s the Egyptians during that time. Look at her hair, it’s real long. His hair is long. See, her hair is long, and it’s got little tassels, little decorations at the end. And here’s some more long hair, and a guy has longer long hair too, but not as long, and, you know, not styled. Are you there? And here’s the real agents of civilization. We got Steven Tyler there. He’s got long hair and puts a little gray streak in it or something like that, and none of us men would ever want to kiss him. But look at that lady by him. They both have long hair, but wow, [unclear]. See, that’s what Paul’s talking about. The woman’s hair was given to her by God, not only to excite that man, but that’s what God did to women, made them special in that area, and he says their hair is their covering, they don’t need anything. And then he’s really going to lay them out. You ready for this? I mean, he’s going to lay them out good. He’s got them that their natural hair is their covering.
Is a woman’s hair her covering?
1 Corinthians 11:15: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her; for her hair is given to her for a covering.
Is the blood of Jesus our covering?

He says Hebrews 10:19 says nothing about a covering for the head: “the blood of Jesus is our covering.” We go in by His blood and by the body that took the pain, and it does not matter if we have long hair, short hair, or coats and ties, but whether we accept the blood, His sacrifice and His authority.
Is the blood of Jesus our covering?

Hebrews 10:19. Before he lays them out, I want to confirm what Paul said. “Therefore, brethren, have boldness to enter the Holiest” where God is, by the what? Blood. Anything about a covering? No. The blood of Jesus is our covering. Okay, “by a new and living way which He has consecrated,” He has set apart for us, “through the veil, that is, His flesh.” See, He took the beating, He took the nails in His hand, He took the spear in His side, He took the crown of thorns. He is our covering. We go in by His blood, we go in by that body that took the pain and all that; we go in that way. “Let us draw near, and having a High Priest over the house of God.” He is the High Priest, He is the Shepherd. Amen, He is the authority. “Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith,” having our, number one, going back to number one, “hearts sprinkled”, they sprinkled things in the Old Testament with the blood, “from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.” That’s water baptism and the washing of the water of the Word. And we can go in. It doesn’t matter if we got long hair, short hair, coats and ties; that ain’t got anything to do with it. It’s do we accept the blood, do we accept His sacrifice of His body, do we accept His authority, and we can go in, and we can touch God, and we can be used of God.
Is the blood of Jesus our covering?

Hebrews 10:19-22: Therefore, brethren, having boldness to enter the Holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way which He consecrated for us, through the veil, that is, His flesh, and having a High Priest over the house of God, let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Does the Bible command women to wear a head covering (1 Corinthians 11:16)?

He calls the covering question “a silly issue,” and says Paul’s final answer is that we have “no such custom,” and neither do the churches of God, including Corinth, Jerusalem and Antioch. He ends: “There is no commandment that women have to do anything but pray and prophesy.”
Does the Bible command women to wear a head covering (1 Corinthians 11:16)?

And this covering thing was a silly issue. And then here’s his final answer, after saying the woman’s hair is her covering. This is his final answer. He says, “If any of you seem to be contentious,” quarrel, “some question in this, we have” what? “No such custom,” tradition, rule, “neither the churches of God,” not only the Corinthian church but the church in Jerusalem, the church at Antioch, and all the other churches. There is no commandment that women have to do anything but pray and prophesy.
Does the Bible command women to wear a head covering (1 Corinthians 11:16)?
1 Corinthians 11:16: But if anyone seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.
Why does he say “let us make man” shows the Godhead is plural?
He says God did not say “I will,” He said “let us,” so the Godhead is plural, and Jesus was there at the beginning. He adds that “mankind” is the human race, not male.
What does he say about “the woman was created for the man”?
He calls these “ego, self-important arguments” that Paul is using to feed the men, and says Paul left out that the woman was given the same blessing and dominion.
Which Bible translations does he say get “power on her head” wrong?

He says the New King James, the NIV, the Living Bible, the Amplified Bible and the American Standard Bible all say power is the sign of the husband’s authority, and that King James and the Darby Bible have it right.
Did Jesus give His disciples a symbol of power or real power?
He says Jesus gave His twelve disciples power over unclean spirits, to heal and to preach, not a symbol like a dove or a fish. “No, He gave them power.”
Does the Devil care if you wear a cross?
He says the Devil doesn’t care if you wear a cross; “what he cares is who the strong man of your house is,” and whether Jesus Christ is living in you.
Would an angel refuse to speak to a woman without a covering?
He says no: “what kind of wimpy angel is he?” When the angel came to Rebecca, he says, the Bible says nothing about her having a covering, and angels are spirit beings who “could care the least.”
What does he say is a bigger problem than demons?

He says once you have Christ, demons “aren’t really your big problem”; it is people who follow Satan and come up with their own traditions, doctrines and way of doing things. You need authority to withstand them and reject their message.
What happens to these arguments when we come to Christ?
He says “when we come to Christ, this nonsense is gone,” because in the Lord neither is the man without the woman nor the woman without the man.
Where does he say everything comes from?
From God: the prayer, the prophecy, the traditions, the customs, the rules, the laws, the image, the likeness, the glory, the dominion and the authority all come from God.
Who was Deborah, and why does he mention her?
He says Deborah was a real leader whom the men followed; when Barak was told to go out and defeat the army, he said he would not go unless she went, and she was “on the front lines of that battle.”
What does he say about men and the work of the kingdom?

He says if God depended on men to get everything done in the kingdom, “we wouldn’t even be where we’re at today,” because men are big talkers and not doers, and he jokes about men who would rather watch football than go witnessing.
What does he say about women in the early part of the nation?

He says they could not own property, did not get the kids when they divorced, could not hold political office or vote, and could not be educated above eighth grade, and that this twisting of Paul’s Scriptures carried into the church.
Why does he say Paul keeps using the word “judge”?

He says Paul is always telling us to make judgments, and yet people in the world say “judge not,” taking one Scripture of the Bible they don’t even believe in when we try to tell them they have to change.
Is a woman’s hair covering about how long it is?
He says no: “it’s got nothing to do with the length; it’s got to do with why they do it.” Women are born to make their hair attractive and decorate it, which men were not.
Did people use this passage against long-haired men?
He says that when the hippies were around, people used this passage to beat them up, “and you can’t do that,” because it is about what women do with their hair and the look they have.

items.d: In “Two Mothers of Revelation Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer preaches from Revelation on the two mothers it mentions. He says the woman of Revelation 12 is a spiritual mother, the church, whose children…
p: In “Two Mothers of Revelation Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer preaches from Revelation on the two mothers it mentions. He says the woman of Revelation 12 is a spiritual mother, the church, whose children overcome Satan and are persecuted by him, then turns to the second woman of Revelation 17, whom he describes as people who use Christ’s name but do not follow him, serving God their own way. He teaches that Revelation is a spiritual illustration, not a list of natural kingdoms, and speaks about the beast, the seven mountains and spiritual fornication.
What are the two mothers mentioned in the book of Revelation?

Pastor Kincer says there are two mothers in the book of Revelation, and he had already gone through one of them. He reads Revelation 12, where a woman gives birth, a dragon tries to devour her child, and she is kept safe in the wilderness. He first honors his own mother and says he is preaching this lesson for Mother’s Day.
What are the two mothers mentioned in the book of Revelation?

My mother passed away a few years ago, but I would just like to let you know that I had the best mother in the world. And my mother’s God today is mine, and I’m still living on my mother’s testimony of Jesus Christ. Her testimony is still being lived out by her son — and more than one of her sons now. It had a good testimony. I had a very good family, I had a very good mother. I was one of the fortunate ones in America to be raised in a family like I had. So, Mom, God bless you. We’re going to continue in Revelation. I had to jump over a lesson to get to this one so I would have this for Mother’s Day, so that next week we’ll bounce back and pick up the chapter that we missed. But there are two mothers mentioned in the book of Revelation. We’ve already gone through one of them, and so we’re just going to remind you. Revelation 12:1: “I saw a great sign in heaven, a woman clothed with a son, being with child. She cried out in labor to give birth. Another sign appeared: a great fiery red dragon, that old serpent of old, called the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world, having seven heads and ten horns. His tail drew a third of the stars to the earth. The dragon stood before the woman to devour her child. She bore a male child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron. Her child was caught up to God. Then the woman fled into the wilderness from Satan’s persecution, where she had a place prepared by God. The dragon persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child, but the woman was given two wings of an eagle that she might fly into the wilderness, where she is nourished from the presence of the serpent, the devil, Satan, the dragon.”
What are the two mothers mentioned in the book of Revelation?

Revelation 12:1-6: Now a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a garland of twelve stars. Then being with child, she cried out in labor and in pain to give birth. And another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great, fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. His tail drew a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her Child as soon as it was born. She bore a male Child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron. And her Child was caught up to God and His throne. Then the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that they should feed her there one thousand two hundred and sixty days. Revelation 12:13-14: Now when the dragon saw that he had been cast to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male Child. But the woman was given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, from the presence of the serpent.
Who is the woman of Revelation 12 and her children?

He says that mother is obviously not a natural mother but a spiritual one: the church, God’s people, with Christ birthed in them. Her offspring keep God’s commandments and have the testimony of Jesus Christ, and they overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony.
Who is the woman of Revelation 12 and her children?

In Revelation 12:17 he was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, her children, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ. Revelation 12:11: the mother and her offspring overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb, by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives even unto death. Now, that mother is obviously not a natural mother. We’re talking about a spiritual mother there. We’re talking about the church. We’re talking about God’s people, and having Christ birthed in them.
Who is the woman of Revelation 12 and her children?

Revelation 12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ. Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death.
Why does Satan persecute people who live for God?

He says the children of this mother did not give into sin and were disliked and persecuted by Satan. If you do not live godly, Satan does not care about you, but if you choose to follow Christ and live right he will come after you, usually through people. He calls that a big plus, because it means you are doing something right.
Why does Satan persecute people who live for God?

And this mother, just to sum it up, she bore children that ruled on earth. You see, they didn’t give into sin, they didn’t give in to the kingdom of darkness; they rule and reign. Now, her children was disliked and persecuted by Satan. The Bible says they that live godly in this world will suffer persecution. If you don’t live godly, of course Satan doesn’t care about you. But if you’re going to choose to follow Christ and live right, he’s going to come after you. All right, so if Satan dislikes you, that’s a big plus for you, amen. And if Satan is persecuting you through people — now, it isn’t Satan coming and persecuting you directly, but he uses people — then that’s a big plus for you. You’re doing something right when people don’t like the right you’re doing.
Why does Satan persecute people who live for God?
2 Timothy 3:12: Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.
What is the wilderness experience in the Christian life?

He says God has a place prepared for his people in the wilderness, that is, in difficult times, and he will take care of them there, so they can relax. He says those times of troubles and problems are important because it is God shaping us up, and he points to Song of Solomon, where we come out of the wilderness leaning on our Beloved.
What is the wilderness experience in the Christian life?

She was kept safe, and so was her children, and nourished in the wilderness, prepared by God from Satan’s persecution. A lot of people say they do not like the wilderness experience, going through difficult times. God has a place prepared. He’ll take care of you there, so relax. The Bible says in Song of Solomon that we’ll come out of the wilderness leaning on our Beloved. So relax. That wilderness is an important time. Those times of troubles, problems — it’s God shaping us up. Now, obviously this is the church, this is God’s people who are birthing Christ, and the nature of Christ and the character of Christ, in others.
What is the wilderness experience in the Christian life?

Song of Solomon 8:5: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? I awakened you under the apple tree. There your mother brought you forth; There she who bore you brought you forth.
Who is the bride of Christ in the Bible?

He says the church is likened to a virgin woman, the bride of Christ, and when we accept Christ we become the bride. He ties this to Revelation, where the Lamb’s wife has made herself ready, and says this means the real believers, whom Satan does not like.
Who is the bride of Christ in the Bible?

And then we’ve got another woman. This one we’re going to call the real Christian, the real church, got it? See, Satan doesn’t like the real church, all right? Now, just to show you that it is talking about the church, I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife. “And he showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God.” 2 Corinthians 11:2: “I have betrothed you,” or engaged you, “to one husband, and I present you as a chaste virgin,” a pure virgin, “to Christ.” See, the church is likened into a woman, a virgin woman, the bride of Christ. And when we accept Christ we become the bride of Christ, and then there’s a big marriage supper up in heaven. Revelation tells us, “The marriage of the Lamb has come, and the wife has made herself ready.” See, that’s the believers, that’s the real believers. So I’m not just telling you that; that’s what the Bible explains the church is, got it?
Who is the bride of Christ in the Bible?

Revelation 21:9-10: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls filled with the seven last plagues came to me and talked with me, saying, “Come, I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, 2 Corinthians 11:2: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. Revelation 19:7: Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.”
What does fornication mean in Revelation 17?

He says the second woman is shown in Revelation 17, and the fornication there is not permissive sexual relationships outside of marriage, which he says the Bible does call wrong. He says it is obviously not talking about natural fornication.
What does fornication mean in Revelation 17?

Now let’s take a look at this second woman. I have an artist’s rendition of this thing up on the screen. Revelation 17 through chapter 19, verse 2, he says: “I will show you the judgment of the great [unclear] that sits upon many waters, with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants have drunk and got intoxicated from her fornication.” Now, you got to understand he’s not talking about fornication is permissive sexual relationships outside of the marriage, whether it’s homosexuality or incest or adultery or whatever. And of course the Bible tells us that’s wrong, and if we’re going to be good moms we’re not going to do that, right? But it’s obvious he’s not talking about the natural fornication.
What does fornication mean in Revelation 17?

Revelation 17:1-2: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and talked with me, saying to me, “Come, I will show you the judgment of the great harlot who sits on many waters, with whom the kings of the earth committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth were made drunk with the wine of her fornication.”
Is worshiping God your own way called spiritual adultery?

He says that in the Old Testament and the New, the Bible speaks of worshiping other gods and worshiping God your own way as being an adulterer or fornicator, because you have not kept your relationship with the one God. He adds that the beast has the names of blasphemy, which he defines as speaking evil of God, of the Bible, of truth and of right, and says this woman is connected with the kingdom of darkness.
Is worshiping God your own way called spiritual adultery?

In the Old Testament and in the New, the Bible talks about worshiping other gods and doing things your own way, worshiping God your own way, as being an adulterer, a fornicator. See why? Because you haven’t kept your relationship with the one God. Got it? Yes. Now, it also says that the beast have on their head the names of the blasphemy. Blasphemy is to speak evil of God, evil of the Bible, evil of truth, evil of right. And so it’s obvious that this beast is connected with Satan. And if you remember Satan there that we just read you, that was opposing the woman, had seven heads and ten horns, like this one. So see, it’s connected. This woman is connected with the kingdom of darkness, you got it? See, Satan has no problem with this woman. Satan has no problem with this beast. Satan is involved here.
Is worshiping God your own way called spiritual adultery?
Revelation 17:3: So he carried me away in the Spirit into the wilderness. And I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet beast which was full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.
Who is Mystery Babylon, the mother of harlots?

He says she is the mystery Babylon, the mother of harlots and of abomination, and that a mother is a full-grown woman who can reproduce. In this spiritual illustration the offspring are people who keep doing idolatry, spiritual fornication and abominations, which he says the Bible uses for hateful things that God despises.
Who is Mystery Babylon, the mother of harlots?

So it goes on to say she is the “mystery, Babylon the great,” the great city of Babylon. She is “the mother of harlots, whores,” and she’s “the mother of abomination.” See, a mother is a full-grown woman that can reproduce, and this spiritual illustration of this woman is she is reproducing. What offspring? People that keep doing idolatry, you know, spiritual fornication, spiritual adultery, and abominations. Abominations — in the Bible is a word, a disgusting thing, a hateful thing. The Bible calls idolatry an abomination. It calls sexual immorality abomination. God looks down on that; that’s not a good thing. It isn’t some magical word that you’re worse than anybody else in the world. It’s just a word that means it’s a hateful thing. God hates it, God despises it, God looks down on that.
Who is Mystery Babylon, the mother of harlots?
Revelation 17:5: And on her forehead a name was written: MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.
Can a church have people who only want the name of Christ?

He says that in the church world some people live for God and reproduce offspring who follow him, but in the same church others serve God their own way and lead people astray. He says this woman is drunk on the blood of the saints, and that many Christians in America just want to be called Christians with no relationship, accountability or responsibility.
Can a church have people who only want the name of Christ?

All right, but she reproduces this. Now, in the church world we can have people living for God that are reproducing offspring that follow God and keep his commandments and his testimony, isn’t that right? But also, in the same church, you can have people not living for Christ, serving God their own way, doing it the way they want, and leading people astray from what God said to do. And this is the illustration here. This woman is drunk on the blood of the saints and the martyrs of Jesus Christ. See, the people that just want Christ’s name, as it says in Isaiah — seven women will take hold of one man and say, “We just want your name; we don’t want any responsibility, accountability. We just want your name.” And that’s what a lot of Christians in America is: they just want to be called Christians. They just want the name of Christ, no relationship, no accountability, no responsibility. And this is what Revelation is illustrating to us. Are you starting to see that? Hallelujah!
Can a church have people who only want the name of Christ?

Revelation 17:6: I saw the woman, drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. And when I saw her, I marveled with great amazement. Isaiah 4:1: And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, “We will eat our own food and wear our own apparel; Only let us be called by your name, To take away our reproach.”
Why does Revelation picture the false church as a woman instead of a warring beast?

He says Satan and his beast were pictured as male, with authority, going to war with the saints, but the feminine form does not go to war. It stands for people who use the Bible and use Christ but do not follow it, and bring others down through deception rather than war. He points to Samson, brought down twice by women, as the picture of lust and desire overcoming common sense and commitment to truth.
Why does Revelation picture the false church as a woman instead of a warring beast?

Now, you got to remember, Satan and his beast were referred to as males in our past lessons, as masculine. They had authority, and they went at war with the saints and the Christian believers. But the feminine form doesn’t go to war. See, the feminine form is illustrated as just a— it’s like a harlot woman, a loose woman who just uses her body to bring men down and people around her down, and use it for her own gain, amen. And that’s the way it is in the natural. But in the spiritual, it’s people who use the Bible and use Christ but don’t follow it, and they bring people down not through war but through deception, saying, “This is the right way, this is the real thing.” And they’ll get intimate with you, and they’ll be your friend and a close acquaintance and all the rest. They’re not at war with you, they’re not going to persecute you; they’re going to use their opinions, what they believe is true, to deceive you to follow something that is not true. And that’s why it’s illustrated as a female. You see, Samson — what brought Samson down twice? Was it the Philistine army? No. Did he lose to some Philistine hero in battle? No. What brought him down twice? Two women. He was the strongest man that ever existed, and yet a woman, through sexual intimacy, brought him down, caused him to break God’s laws, caused him to have his eyes put out, and caused him to go into captivity. You see, the masculine is the persecution and the warfare, but the feminine illustration is our lust, our desires overcoming our common sense and our commitment to truth, and doing things we shouldn’t do. Are you there? You say, “I’ve never heard Revelation like this before.” Well, stick around. Stick around, it gets better.
What is the mystery of the woman and the beast in Revelation 17?

He says the angel tells John the mystery of the woman and the beast, and the first part is that the beast was, is not, and yet is now. He explains this beast as a nation, government, ruler or kingdom that existed, died and existed again, rising from the bottomless pit, which is Satan’s domain, so it is directly connected to Satan.
What is the mystery of the woman and the beast in Revelation 17?

You see — anyway, let’s continue here. Then the angel comes to him and says, “Hey, I’m going to tell you the mystery of the woman and the beast.” I’m going to tell you this secret, this mystery, this hidden thing. I’m going to tell you both what the beast means and the woman. All these artists draw these beasts that look like amphibious dinosaurs all the time. Now, if I would have drawn this thing it would have been entirely different. We don’t know exactly what this beast look like, but I tell you it didn’t look like that. But it’s a good illustration, all right? Now, you see the ten horns up here on one of the heads, right at the top in the middle? Okay, remember that. Then a couple of these have horns — that’s too many horns. It only had ten horns and we got fourteen up there. But anyway, it’s still a great illustration. Whoever did it was very clever. Now, here’s the mystery of the woman. Mystery number one: the beast was, and is not, and yet is now. I know that just cleared everything up for you, didn’t it? Don’t you like how the Bible says, “Hey, we’re going to explain to you what we’re talking about,” and then they just confuse us more? Okay. In other words, this beast, which is referred to in the Bible as a nation, as a government, as a ruler, as a kingdom, was, and then it died, and then it existed again. Okay? And remember, the first beast was the same way — the first beast that came out of the waters that we talked about, same thing. This beast shall ascend out of the bottomless pit. Now, the first beast came out of the waters; this one came out of the bottomless pit. Bottomless pit is Satan’s domain. So this beast is directly connected to who? Satan himself, yes. All right, the Bible tells us Satan the destroyer is king of the bottomless pit.
What is the mystery of the woman and the beast in Revelation 17?

Revelation 17:8: The beast that you saw was, and is not, and will ascend out of the bottomless pit and go to perdition. And those who dwell on the earth will marvel, whose names are not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world, when they see the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.
Is the great city in Revelation 11 the literal Jerusalem?

He says Revelation 11:7 shows the beast from the bottomless pit making war on the two witnesses, whose bodies lie in the street of the great city, which is called spiritually Sodom and Egypt and is the city where the Lord was crucified. He stresses the word “spiritually” and says too many people interpret Revelation as natural kingdoms and rulers when it is a spiritual illustration.
Is the great city in Revelation 11 the literal Jerusalem?

Okay, Revelation 11:7 says the beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them. This is in chapter 11, the two witnesses. It’s the beast making war with the witnesses, the two prophets. Their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, you see, which spiritually is called what? Sodom and Egypt. Have you ever read in the Bible the word Rahab? That is a Bible shadow of Egypt relating to God’s people. When God’s people are bad, God referred to them as Rahab, Egypt, bad. Okay? When God’s people were bad, the prophets would relate to them as Sodom, you see? Okay, and then it plainly tells us, thank God, who this city is: “where the Lord was—“ what? “—crucified.” Now, what city is that? Jerusalem. Say it: Jerusalem. Okay, but the key word is this word right here. What’s the word? Spiritually. See, he’s talking to us about spiritual things, not natural things. And too many people want to take Revelation and try to interpret it as something natural, trying to raise up kingdoms here and kingdoms there and rulers here and rulers there. And it’s what? A spiritual illustration. Can I hear an amen? Now, so it is very doubtful they’re really going to be lying on the street of Jerusalem like all these theorists say. Are you out there? Because he’s talking about what Jerusalem — the natural or the spiritual? The spiritual.
Is the great city in Revelation 11 the literal Jerusalem?

Revelation 11:7-8: When they finish their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit will make war against them, overcome them, and kill them. And their dead bodies will lie in the street of the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.
What are the seven heads, seven mountains and seven kings of Revelation 17?

He says the beast has seven heads, which are seven mountains and seven kings, and that five had already fallen when John received the revelation. He says the beast was active before John got the revelation and is not just something that will be activated at the end time. He says the bottom line is that this is happening in every generation.
What are the seven heads, seven mountains and seven kings of Revelation 17?

Okay, let’s continue. The beast has seven heads, which are seven mountains and seven kings. Five are fallen — okay, they’ve come and gone. Now, at the time John got this revelation, five of these heads have already passed. One is, and one more is to come, and after that the eighth beast himself is going to be the last king. Now, I know that’s clear as a bell now, isn’t it? I mean, aren’t you glad the angel told him that? But it’s very important you got to understand then that this beast has been active before John got the revelation. It isn’t some beast that’s just going to be activated up here at the end time. Are you there? But this is what the theorists will tell you, it’s something in the future. But no, most of it has already happened before John got the revelation, and then it was happening while he had it, and the bottom line is this is happening in every generation. That’s the bottom line. Amen.
What are the seven heads, seven mountains and seven kings of Revelation 17?

Revelation 17:9-11: “Here is the mind which has wisdom: The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits. There are also seven kings. Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come. And when he comes, he must continue a short time. The beast that was, and is not, is himself also the eighth, and is of the seven, and is going to perdition.
Are the seven mountains of Revelation the seven hills of Rome?

He says the mountains in Psalm 125:2 are the mountains round about Jerusalem, not Rome. He says some fundamentalists attack the Catholic Church by saying it is founded on seven hills in Rome, and that others make similar claims against Protestants, which he calls nonsense that comes from looking at things in the natural when the text is talking about the spiritual.
Are the seven mountains of Revelation the seven hills of Rome?

All right, Psalms 125:2: “The mountains are round about Jerusalem, as the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the Lord is round about his people.” Are you there? So where’s— where’s these mountains round about Jerusalem? Not Rome. You see, your fundamentalists attack the Catholic Church by saying the Catholic church is founded on seven hills in Rome, and so they are the beast, they’re the big bad people. If you just read your Bible — how many of you didn’t know that? Only a few of you didn’t know. How many did know that? Yeah, this is a popular teaching out there now. If you go to the Catholic group, they’re telling you that the Protestants are this. That’s a fact, yeah. Lu— Martin Luther was the Antichrist, you know, mark 666. They found out how to calculate his name to 666. This nonsense has been going on because we look at things in the natural, when it plainly is talking about what? The spiritual. And somehow they leave that word out of there.
Are the seven mountains of Revelation the seven hills of Rome?
Psalm 125:2: As the mountains surround Jerusalem, So the LORD surrounds His people From this time forth and forever.
What are the mountains of Jerusalem, and what is spiritual fornication?

He says Jerusalem is founded around mountains and the Bible names six of them, and that God’s foundation is in the holy mountains. He says that when Jehoram made high places, the people committed fornication by worshiping God the way they wanted, not the way God said. He says the world’s fornication is spiritual, not sexual: serving God the way God said not to and living a lifestyle God said not to live.
What are the mountains of Jerusalem, and what is spiritual fornication?

And Jerusalem is founded around mountains. Are you aware of that? The Bible names six of them, plainly named six of them. Now, his foundation is in the— what? —holy mountains. Jesus Christ, God’s foundation is in the holy mountains. 2 Chronicles 21:22 [Editor’s note: the passage he reads is 2 Chronicles 21:11.]: Jehoram, the king of Judah, made high places in the mountains of Jerusalem and caused the people to commit— what’s the word? Fornication. They weren’t out there having sex; they were out there worshiping God the way they wanted to worship him, not the way God said. Are you with me? And these, the world, is committing fornication with this. It is not a sexual fornication; it is a spiritual fornication. They are serving God the way God said not to serve him, and they’re living a lifestyle that God said not to live.
What are the mountains of Jerusalem, and what is spiritual fornication?

Psalm 87:1: His foundation is in the holy mountains. 2 Chronicles 21:11: Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit harlotry, and led Judah astray.
Why did Pastor Kincer preach on the two mothers of Revelation for Mother’s Day?

He says he had to jump over a lesson in his Revelation series to get to this one so he would have it for Mother’s Day, and that next week he will go back and pick up the chapter that was missed. He says there are two mothers in Revelation, and he had already gone through one of them.
Is the woman in Revelation 12 a natural mother?
No, he says. He calls her obviously not a natural mother but a spiritual one, which he says is the church and God’s people, having Christ birthed in them.
Is it a bad sign if Satan dislikes you?

He says it is a big plus for you. If you do not live godly, Satan does not care about you, but if you choose to follow Christ and live right he will come after you, and he says it is a good sign when people do not like the right you are doing.
What should I do when I am going through a wilderness season?
He says to relax, because God has a place prepared and will take care of you there. He says those times of troubles and problems are an important time in which God is shaping us up.
What does he say about the marriage supper of the Lamb?
He says that when we accept Christ we become the bride of Christ, and then there is a big marriage supper up in heaven. He says the Lamb’s wife making herself ready refers to the real believers.
What does blasphemy mean in this message?
He defines blasphemy as speaking evil of God, evil of the Bible, evil of truth and evil of right. He says it shows the beast with the names of blasphemy is connected with Satan.
What does he say the word abomination means?

He says it is a word for a disgusting thing, a hateful thing, and that the Bible calls idolatry and sexual immorality abominations. He says it is not some magical word saying you are worse than anybody else in the world, but a word that means God hates it, despises it and looks down on it.
What does it look like to want only the name of Christ?

He points to Isaiah, where seven women take hold of one man and say they just want his name, with no responsibility or accountability. He says that is what a lot of Christians in America are like: they want to be called Christians, with no relationship, accountability or responsibility.
What does Samson show about why the second woman is a woman?

He says Samson was brought down twice, not by an army or a Philistine hero in battle, but by two women. He says the strongest man who ever existed was caused by a woman, through sexual intimacy, to break God’s laws, lose his eyes and go into captivity, and that the feminine illustration pictures our lust and desires overcoming our common sense and commitment to truth.
What does it mean that the beast “was, and is not, and yet is”?

He says it means the beast, which the Bible uses for a nation, government, ruler or kingdom, existed, then died, then existed again. He says the first beast was the same way, and that this beast ascends out of the bottomless pit, which is Satan’s domain.
Why does the Bible call God’s people Sodom or Egypt?

He says that when God’s people were bad, God referred to them as Rahab, Egypt, and the prophets related to them as Sodom. He says the key word in Revelation 11 is “spiritually,” because the great city that is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt is where the Lord was crucified.
Is the beast of Revelation only an end-time figure?

He says no: the beast was active before John got the revelation and is not some beast that will just be activated at the end time. He says most of it had already happened before John got the revelation, and the bottom line is that it is happening in every generation.

p: In “Two Mothers of Revelation Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues his teaching on the harlot and the beast of Revelation 17, saying Babylon is not the Catholic Church and that the waters, nations and tongues describe a spiritual condition found in every nation. He says believing in Jesus and using his name while living your own way is spiritual fornication, explains John 8:41, and says Jesus calls his people, who are still here on earth, to come out of false religion and come to him. He closes with a Mother’s Day word to mothers and fathers about leading children well.
What does the Bible mean by Babylon, the “destroying mountain”?

He says Babylon is called a destroying mountain in Jeremiah: a nation, a group of people destroying other people for all the evil done in Zion, which he says is the church, the people of God. He says they lead astray not just Christians but people who do not believe in Jesus, and that the shepherds in Jeremiah 50:6 lead people astray on the mountains, serving God the way they should not, so that they forget their resting place, Jesus Christ.
What does the Bible mean by Babylon, the “destroying mountain”?

Shepherds cause my people, in Jeremiah 50:6, to go astray on the what? Mountains. And what are they doing on the mountains? Serving God the way they shouldn’t be serving. And they forget their resting place. Who is our resting place? Jesus Christ. Jeremiah 51:24: “I’m against Babylon, O destroying mountain.” [Editor’s note: the words “destroying mountain” are in Jeremiah 51:25; verse 24 speaks of the evil done in Zion.] So Babylon is referred to as a what? Destroying mountain. A nation, a group of people that are destroying other people for all the evil done in Zion. Zion is the church, the people of God, and destroying all the earth. They don’t just lead Christians astray and people who believe in Jesus astray; they lead people who don’t believe in Jesus astray. Are you there? Hallelujah.
What does the Bible mean by Babylon, the “destroying mountain”?

Jeremiah 50:6: “My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds have led them astray; They have turned them away on the mountains. They have gone from mountain to hill; They have forgotten their resting place. Is Babylon in the book of Revelation the Catholic Church?

It’s not the Catholic Church at all. And I’ve debated this with my fundamentalist pastors and all the rest. It’s got nothing to do. I have met good Catholics, folks. I have met good Baptists. He says the ten spiritual horns make war with the Lamb for one hour, and the Lamb defeats them with those who are called, chosen and faithful. He says that is us: Jesus called us to himself, he chose us when we accepted his sacrifice, and we are faithful when we keep pursuing him and living a lifestyle that pleases him.
Who are the called, chosen and faithful with the Lamb?

There’s ten horns are going to be ten kings for one hour with the beast. Now, obviously, these are ten spiritual horns, and for one hour they’re going to make war with the Lamb. And the Lamb is going to defeat him. And he has some people following with him, and defeats him with him, and they are called “chosen and what? Faithful.” “With him are those called, chosen, and faithful.” Didn’t Jesus call us to himself? Yes. And when we accepted his sacrifice on the cross for our sins, admitted we were sinners and accepted forgiveness and deliverance from our sins because of him, did he choose us? Yes. And when we follow up and we pursue him and learn of him and keep living a lifestyle, we keep growing in a lifestyle pleasing him, isn’t that being faithful? Yeah, that’s us. So if that’s true, we’re still here.

Revelation 17:12-14: “The ten horns which you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority for one hour as kings with the beast. He says the theory has Christians going out of this earth before these events, but he says he has shown in every chapter that we are still here. He says a God who could only forgive sins but could not keep us when difficult times come would be worthless, and a powerful God can also deliver us from the influence and control of sin.
Will Christians be taken out of the earth before the difficult times?

I’m just letting it sink in. You see, the theory has got us going out of this earth before all this happens. But I’ve showed you in every chapter where we’re still here. And it makes sense. Jesus can only save us and forgive us of sins, and he cannot keep us when the difficult times come? What kind of God is that? He’s a worthless God. A powerful God can not only save us from hell and forgive us for sins, he can deliver us from the influence and control of sin. That is a God that’s got some worth, amen. And Revelation shows us that God has got a people that show in their lifestyle and serving him his power.

He says the waters where the harlot sits are people, multitudes, nations and tongues, so trying to match the beast to the United Nations or a group of European nations misses it. He says this beast is in every nation, about 190 of them, and that God has no prejudice or preference toward any nation.
What do the waters in Revelation 17 mean, and is it about the United Nations or Europe?

Now listen to this. The waters where the [unclear] sits are what? People, multitudes, nations, and tongues. So when they want to go try to get the United Nations, or, you know, the Atlantic Treaty Organization, or the ten European nations, or whatever they were that bound together over there in Europe to get the euro, their own money, and all that, they’re missing it. This beast — and this is in every nation. There is 190— approximately 190 nations. They’re in every one of them. Can I hear an amen? But the theorists have us pondering these little packs of nations, and they always take the industrial nations. Well, you know, God loves Uganda. God loves Paraguay. God loves all these nations everywhere on the earth. He has no prejudice. He has no preference. All are the same. And every nation and every people and every language is important to him. Can I hear an amen? But they don’t make the news. It’s these bigger nations that make the news.

Revelation 17:15: Then he said to me, “The waters which you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues.

As Juliana found out, she went back to where I came from and found out, “Boy, things are different back there.” I said, “Yeah, you got it. And how many know the kingdom of God is a culture, a tradition, and we’re to learn that and keep that tradition and culture?
