He says that when Satan showed Jesus all the kingdoms in the third temptation and offered them for worship, Satan was lying, because Jesus is the Lord of the whole earth and Satan can do nothing without Jesus’s permission. He says Jesus had all the authority but delegated the nations to Satan, a limited delegated authority.
Did Jesus give Satan authority over the nations?

All right. “The woman is the great city which rules over the kings of the earth.” Now, the Bible tells us in the garden that Jesus was tempted by Satan. And the third temptation, he came and showed him all the kingdoms of the earth and said, “Hey, these kingdoms are given to me to give to whomsoever I want. And if you’ll worship me, I’ll give you the whole earth. You’ll be the king of the earth, and all the prosperity and everything that goes with it.” Well, Satan was lying there, because Jesus is the Lord of the whole earth, and Satan cannot do anything without Jesus’s permission. And I mean, this is, you know, be like me going to President Obama and telling him, “Hey, man, I’ll give you all the conservative vote in America and Republican votes, you know, if you just follow my way.” Well, he’s the one that’s got all the authority. He’ll just say, “Who are you?” And that’s the way it is with Jesus. See, Jesus had all the authority. He had all the power, but he delegated the nations to Satan. A limited delegated authority. Are you with me?

Revelation 17:18: And the woman whom you saw is that great city which reigns over the kings of the earth.” Matthew 4:8-9: Again, the devil took Him up on an exceedingly high mountain, and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory. He says God cannot do evil, so any evil done in the earth is done by what the Old Testament calls the waster, whom he says God created to do what God has no character to do. Why does God allow Satan to do evil if God cannot do evil?

Because — okay, did you guys hear that? Why would he give it? Because God cannot do evil. Okay? So any evil done in the earth, he created what the Old Testament calls the waster to destroy. He created Satan to do what God has no character to do. See, there’s things God cannot do. Are you aware of that? Like, God can’t lie. Ain’t that right? God can’t reject you if you come to him. People say, “Well, God can do anything.” No, there’s things that God can’t do. Why? Because God is good. He can’t do evil. See, God can’t lie. And the Bible says when we come to him, he will not what? Cast us away. When we come to Christ, I don’t care how big a sinner you think you are, Jesus cannot reject you. It’s not in his nature. Does that answer that? But see, Satan can’t. And so Satan comes and he can tempt you. He can test you. He can put little things in your mind to do wrong and all the rest. But if you follow Christ, you’ll overcome that. See, Satan is there trying to lead you away from right. Jesus is there trying to lead you away from wrong. And the darkness and the light are at war. There’s only two roads: one, the wide road to hell; the other one, the narrow road to heaven. This is not a complicated Bible. Amen.
Why does God allow Satan to do evil if God cannot do evil?

Matthew 7:13-14: “Enter by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and there are many who go in by it. Because narrow is the gate and difficult is the way which leads to life, and there are few who find it.
What is spiritual fornication, and what did Jesus say to the Jews who said they were not born of fornication?

He says the woman used wrongly illustrates the kingdom of darkness, people who choose their own way of religion, and that we commit spiritual fornication when we follow them. He says the Jews of John 8:41 were believers who read the scriptures and had legitimate parents, but created their own way of serving God. He says Jesus told them that if God were their father they would love him, since love does no harm, and that they were harming others by leading them astray.
What is spiritual fornication, and what did Jesus say to the Jews who said they were not born of fornication?

So it’s obvious this woman and this beast is connected to which kingdom? Satan’s kingdom. The kingdom of darkness. And when we listen to these people, follow in this way, we become like them. We commit spiritual fornication. John 8:41. Now, I want to prove this to you. Here we go. You ready? I’m trying to back up that the woman used rightly is the illustration of God’s people, the church. The woman used wrongly is an illustration of the kingdom of darkness. They that choose their own way of religion, whatever it may be. These Jews were believers, isn’t that right? Here’s Jesus talking to the Jews. They were believers. They read the scriptures. They went to the synagogue, and they talked to Jesus and say, “We’re not born of fornication.” What’s the word? Fornication. And they weren’t. They had legitimate parents. They weren’t adulterous parents. They could say that. But spiritual fornication is different. See, they created their own way of serving God. Even though they used the scriptures, even though they used God, they had their own way of doing it. And they said, “We’re not born of fornication,” but they were. “We have one father” — who is the father? God. See, they thought they were okay. And Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would what? Love me.” See, love in the Bible would do no harm. You’d do nothing to harm me. You do nothing to harm others. You are harming others, because you’re leading them astray from me. And then he says these powerful words: “You are of your father the devil.” Because why? “The works of your father you do.”
What is spiritual fornication, and what did Jesus say to the Jews who said they were not born of fornication?

John 8:41: You do the deeds of your father.” Then they said to Him, “We were not born of fornication; we have one Father—God.” John 8:42: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I proceeded forth and came from God; nor have I come of Myself, but He sent Me. John 8:44: You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it.

Is it possible to believe in Jesus and still go to hell?

If you start using his name to worship your own way and live your own way, that is spiritual fornication. And that’s what this on the beast is all about. And it’s that simple. It’s not the Catholic Church. It’s not the Baptist church. It’s not the Presbyterian church or any of these people that come to Christ. It is anyone in them that decides to take his name and not live his way and serve him his way. Amen. Moms. Amen.
Should you read the Bible before you reject it?

He says that, talking with people with their own dreamed-up religion who never read the Bible, he asked how many know you cannot condemn a book until you read it and cannot say it does not work until you apply it. He says many Christians have not read the book either and just believe everything on radio and TV, which he says tells a lot of lies, and he asks, in the natural, what kind of mother or parent are you.
Should you read the Bible before you reject it?

You say, “What’s that got to do with Mother’s Day?” Well, what kind of mother are you? See, in the natural, are we leading our kids right, or we got our own way? I mean, I just talked to people Friday night that had their own dreamed-up religion. They never read the Bible. They just come up with ideas from hearing TV and talk show people and all the rest. And we had a great discussion there. At least I did. How many of you know you can’t condemn a book until you read it? And you can’t say a book doesn’t work until you read it and you applied it. Yeah. And they were failing on all parts. And how many you know, many Christians haven’t even read the book yet. They just believe everything on radio and TV, which are telling you a lot of lies. I guarantee you, you won’t hear this on the book of Revelation on radio and TV.

He says Babylon, the city that rules over the kings of the earth, has fallen and is inhabited by evil spirits, with the kingdom of darkness the main force of influence in it, and the call is to come out from this false Christianity. He says the call goes to God’s people, who are still on earth, not raptured out, and Jesus is inviting everyone to come out of their own opinions and ideas and come to him, not religion.
What does “Come out of her, my people” mean in Revelation 18?

So the [unclear] is judged. She is Babylon that rules over the kings of the earth. The mother of abominations, and martyrs and the saints. She sits on seven mountains, sits on the nations. Ten kings hate and destroy her. And Revelation 18:2, it goes on to say that Babylon, this city, this is fallen, and it’s inhabited by evil spirits. So the word fallen doesn’t mean it’s totally destroyed. It’s fallen. It’s deteriorated, and the kingdom of darkness is the main force of influence in it. Are you with me? All right. All nations, kings, merchants commit fornication with her. They’re rich through her delicacies. Here it is: “Come out from what? Her— who? The—“ Come out from this false Christianity. Who is he saying to come out? “My people.” So where are they still? Where is the people? On earth. See, they got us in this dream world of rapturing out of here and all this bad stuff happening. But Revelation has us here handling it, because Jesus is the King of Kings and the Lord of Lords, and he is all powerful, and he keeps his people. Amen. And he’s saying, “My people, don’t have anything to do with that kind of religion.” They’re still here. And he’s inviting everyone today to come out from your own opinions, to come out from your own ideas, to come out from your friends’ ideas and their opinions, and come to him. He’s still saying, “Come unto me, all ye that labor and heavy laden, and I will give you rest. As many as come to me, I will in no wise cast out.” Jesus is still calling out to the world through the word and through the Spirit: “Come to me,” not religion. Catholic can’t get you to heaven. Baptists can’t get you to heaven. Pentecostals can’t get you to heaven. They can’t give you wisdom and knowledge and understanding and peace and love. “I can give it all to you. Come out, my people.” And that’s what every church should be preaching: come to him. Hallelujah.

Revelation 18:2: And he cried mightily with a loud voice, saying, “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and has become a dwelling place of demons, a prison for every foul spirit, and a cage for every unclean and hated bird! Revelation 18:4: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, “Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues. If I have made spiritual mistakes, can I correct them?

He says yes: if we have made the mistake we can correct it, in the natural or in the spiritual. He says he made a lot of mistakes as a young Christian, thinking it was spiritual when it was not, and that Jesus is still the forgiver, the deliverer and the one who can save you, but you have to recognize the differences so you are not a partaker of her sins and plagues.
If I have made spiritual mistakes, can I correct them?

So, see, if we’ve made the mistake, can we correct it? Absolutely. In the natural, if we’re sexual immoral people or thieves and liars and so forth, can we come out and correct the natural? If in the spiritual we’re wrong, can we correct the spiritual? Yes. Thank God, I’d have been killed a long time ago, [unclear] I’ve been cast out a long time ago. I made a lot of mistakes as a young Christian, thinking it was spiritual and it wasn’t. And you can raise your hand and say, “Yeah, I can relate.” See, both in the natural and in the spiritual, he is crying, “Come to me. I’m still the forgiver. I’m still the deliverer. I’m still the one that can save you. I’m still the one that can get you to the goal.” But you got to recognize the differences to be able to make that decision, so you don’t be a partaker of her sins and of her plagues.

Why does the Bible use a mother to picture the church?

He says it is the mother who carries, nourishes and finally gives birth to the child, while the man conceives it and gives it life. He says what the mother eats and does in the natural affects the child being born, and how she teaches it and lives before it affects it afterward, so mothers must keep the responsibility until the child is a responsible adult with good character and discipline.
Why does the Bible use a mother to picture the church?

The Bible uses the mother because it’s the mother that carries and nourishes and finally gives birth to that child. The man conceives it. He gives it life. It takes on his nature. But the mother nourishes it. And this is why the church is illustrated as a woman. See, what you eat, what you do with your body in the natural is going to affect that child being born. And after it’s born, how you teach it, the life you live before it is going to affect that child. And so, mothers, you’re very important not to just birth the child, but to keep that mother responsibility to see that that child gets to twenty years old, an adult that’s responsible, has good character, discipline in their life.
How should parents raise their children, according to this message?

He says the woman driven into the wilderness reproduced children with great character who had the testimony of Jesus and obeyed the word of God, and that dads are included because these are spiritual decisions. He says parents should stay, support the child and the home, live as an example, and bring children to church so they see them worshiping God, and he remembers his own mother’s voice keeping him from wrong.
How should parents raise their children, according to this message?

And that’s what the woman that was driven into the wilderness had. She reproduced children with great character. They had the testimony of Jesus, and they obeyed the word of God. Wow. So, moms, have we been doing that? And can we improve on that? And dads, if you think you can escape this message, I’m going to connect you, because it says spiritually. We’re talking about spiritual decisions. And so it’s not just the woman now, but the men need to make the same decisions. Can that be an amen? You don’t just give life to a child because you like to have sex and then just run off on it and leave it. That’s horrible. But you hang in there and you support that child. You support that home. You live an example to that home. Amen. Like Mike said, you bring them to church so they get the word of God in them from another source, not your own. Your own’s confirmed. They see you worshiping God. They don’t see you dropping them off at church and then going back home to watch the Lakers on TV or whatever. They see you right there with them. They see you are concerned about the things of God. And see, that’s the way my mom was. And I wound up just like her. Hallelujah. And sometimes when I was a teenager and I was doing bad things, it wasn’t God bringing me under conviction; it was my mom’s voice. David, now don’t get me wrong, God used my mom’s voice to bring me in conviction. But it was my mom [unclear] that said, “Don’t you do that.” I noticed one of my older brothers was saying, “Man, mom told me three things.” And one of the things is, you know, you don’t have sex outside of marriages and have kids that you don’t raise and all that. And though he’s in his seventies, he said, “Man, if I did anything wrong, I would remember that voice.” And I said, “I’m with you. I remember that voice.” Hallelujah. So it pays for moms to follow through on being a mom, and dads to follow through. Does he say there are good and bad people in every church?

He says he has met good Catholics, good Baptists and good Pentecostals, and lousy ones too, in the many denominations where he has ministered. He says their lifestyle and their own way of serving God comes up short in those cases.
What does it mean to be chosen and faithful?

He says Jesus called us to himself, and when we accepted his sacrifice, admitted we were sinners and accepted forgiveness and deliverance, he chose us. He says that when we pursue him, learn of him and keep growing in a lifestyle pleasing him, that is being faithful.
What does he say about the theory that Christians leave the earth first?

He says the theory has us going out of the earth before all this happens, but in every chapter he has shown that we are still here. He says Revelation has Jesus keeping his people here, handling it, because he is the King of Kings and Lord of Lords and is all powerful.
Does God love every nation equally?

He says God loves Uganda and Paraguay and all the nations everywhere on the earth, and has no prejudice and no preference. He says every nation, people and language is important to him, even though the smaller ones do not make the news.
How many languages does he say there are?

He says there are over 6,000, about 6,500 languages in the earth, and that wherever there is a language this beast is right there. He ties the word tongues to languages, and says the beast is a spiritual condition.
Is the kingdom of God a culture?

He says there are as many cultures as languages, and not everything in a culture should be kept. He says the kingdom of God is a culture and a tradition, and we are to learn that and keep that tradition and culture.
Can God lie or turn away someone who comes to him?

He says God cannot lie and cannot reject you if you come to him, because God is good and cannot do evil. He says that when we come to Christ, however big a sinner we think we are, Jesus cannot reject us, because it is not in his nature.
Does he say there are only two spiritual roads?

He says there are only two spiritual kingdoms, dark and light, right and wrong, and only two roads: the wide road to hell and the narrow road to heaven. He says Satan tries to lead you away from right and Jesus tries to lead you away from wrong, and the darkness and the light are at war.
How do we commit spiritual fornication, according to this message?

He says it happens when we listen to people who follow the kingdom of darkness and follow them in their way, and we become like them. He says it means choosing your own way of religion while using the scriptures and God’s name, as the Jews did when Jesus spoke with them.
What does he say love looks like in this passage?

He says love in the Bible would do no harm: you would do nothing to harm him and nothing to harm others. He says the Jews were harming others by leading them astray from Jesus, and he points to Jesus’s words that the works of your father you do.
Are dads included in this message to mothers?

He says that if dads think they can escape this message he is going to connect them, because it says spiritually and these are spiritual decisions. He says it is not just the woman but the men who need to make the same decisions, and that you do not give life to a child and then run off and leave it.
What does he say about his mother’s influence on him?

He says that when he was a teenager doing bad things, it was his mother’s voice he heard, and God used her voice to bring him under conviction. He says one of his older brothers, now in his seventies, said he would remember that voice if he did anything wrong, and he says he remembers it too.

They think God is only good for an immediate necessity. God will be there at the snap of their finger. We need him every day of our life. When I was dying in that hospital ... I don't need a healer to come in here. I need the Healer. Jesus. I'm not panicked ... I'm in his hands. He makes the decisions.
📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 6:11 — Give us this day our daily bread.

items.d: No. God has no grandchildren and no stepchildren — only children.
p: No. God has no grandchildren and no stepchildren — only children.
Pastor Kincer says you have to be born again yourself and have your own first contact with Him. You can’t use your parents, your church or your minister as an excuse on judgment day.

🎙 From the sermon “The problem in America is if my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I’m a Baptist, don’t bug me.” ▶ 13:19 “God does not have grandchildren. He does not have stepchildren. He has children. In other words, you got to get born again by him. You got to have that initial first contact with him.” ▶ 15:02 “I can’t use my parents for an excuse on judgment day. I can’t use my church or the minister on judgment day because I’m accountable to find him and serve him and follow him.” ▶ 15:27 if my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I'm a Baptist, don't bug me If my granddad was a Catholic ... and I'm a Catholic, don't bug me God does not have grandchildren. He does not have stepchildren. He has children. you got to get born again by him You got to have that initial first contact with him. I can't use my parents for an excuse on judgment day. I can't use my church or the minister I'm accountable to find him and serve him and follow him.
📖 Scripture (NKJV) John 3:3 — Jesus answered and said to him, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

items.t: Can the Word still turn a nation?
items.d: Yes. Pastor Kincer says that if the church gets the message out, the Word does the work — it convicts and convinces people.
p: Yes. Pastor Kincer says that if the church gets the message out, the Word does the work — it convicts and convinces people.
Pastor Kincer points to God’s promise that His word will not return void. He says it is the Word — not a denomination — that must get out, and the turning of a nation starts with the church.
Can the Word still turn a nation?

🎙 From the sermon “But if we can get the message out, and the word will work. Remember the Bible says the word will not return what? Void — but it will be profitable into the purpose that I have purposed it.” ▶ 31:16 “But it’s the word. It’s not the Catholics. It’s not the Protestants. It’s not the Jews. It’s the word that’s got to get out.” ▶ 31:32 “You speak the word and the word convicts and convinces people. The word does it. You don’t have to force them.” ▶ 32:12 Can the Word still turn a nation? Isaiah says God’s Word will not return unto Him void, but it will accomplish what He pleases. Pastor Kincer says it is the Word that must get out: it convicts and convinces people, and the turning of a nation starts with the church getting beyond its four walls.
Can the Word still turn a nation?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Isaiah 55:11 — So shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; It shall not return to Me void, But it shall accomplish what I please, And it shall prosper in the thing for which I sent it.

items.t: Do we only want to hear smooth things?
items.d: Many people do. They want to be told they’re okay, so they hire ministers to say what they want to hear instead of what is right.
p: Many people do. They want to be told they’re okay, so they hire ministers to say what they want to hear instead of what is right.
Pastor Kincer cites Isaiah 30:10, “Speak to us smooth things.” He says Scripture is given for righteousness and good works, but people don’t want to hear what is right.
Do we only want to hear smooth things?

🎙 From the sermon “There’s many groups doing what’s right in their own eyes, hiring and appointing ministers to flatter them, to please them, not God, as it says in Isaiah 30:10, speak to us smooth things, speak to us deceit, don’t speak to us right things.” ▶ 19:34 “We don’t want to hear about good works, we don’t want to hear about what’s right, we want to hear that we’re okay.” ▶ 20:08 “And so they get the money, they get the big fancy houses, they get the cars, they get the fame, they pay ministers to preach what they want to hear.” ▶ 20:12 Do we only want to hear smooth things? Isaiah says, “Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits.” Pastor Kincer says they pay ministers to preach what they want to hear. They want to be told they are okay, but Scripture is given for righteousness.
Do we only want to hear smooth things?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Isaiah 30:10 — Who say to the seers, “Do not see,” And to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us right things; Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits.” 2 Timothy 3:16 — All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.

items.t: Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?
items.d: In what is preached, yes. Pastor Kincer says the Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same in every church.
p: In what is preached, yes. Pastor Kincer says the Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same in every church.

Paul urged believers to speak the same thing, with no divisions. A Big Mac is identical in Brazil, Korea, China and every state, Pastor Kincer says — but in America church teaching isn’t, and that confuses everybody.
Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?

🎙 From the sermon “He says, I want you to all speak the same thing.” ▶ 9:19 “I can go to McDonald’s, order a Big Mac and it’s identical. They didn’t change the Big Mac.” ▶ 9:38 “See, the Holy Ghost shouldn’t be preached different in one church and in another way in another church. It should be the what? Same. Salvation should be what? The same. Righteousness and holy living should be what? The same.” ▶ 10:38 “Everything should be the same like McDonald’s is, but in America, do we have that? No! And so we confuse everybody.” ▶ 10:53 Paul says, “I want you all to speak the same thing” (1 Corinthians 1:10). Pastor Kincer says that in Brazil, Korea, China or any state in America, a Big Mac is identical, the fries are the same, and the Coke is the real Coke. The Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same way in every church, but in America they aren’t, and it confuses everybody.
Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 1:10 — Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

items.d: It can feel that way. Pastor Kincer says church was boring to him as a teenager because he wasn’t involved and had lost his desire for Jesus.
p: It can feel that way. Pastor Kincer says church was boring to him as a teenager because he wasn’t involved and had lost his desire for Jesus.

Pastor Kincer contrasts that with David, who was glad when they said, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.” Pastor Kincer says the church is made up of people, and the people determine what a church is.

🎙 From the sermon “When I was 17, 16, 18, church is boring because I didn’t get involved. I wanted to do my thing.” ▶ 3:50 “Or we just lost our desire for Jesus.” ▶ 4:33 “David said, I was glad when they said unto me, let us what? Go to the house of the Lord. Man, he was excited. It’s assembly time. Oh, glory, let’s go.” ▶ 4:40 “But the church is made up of who? People. And it’s the people that are the determination of a church.” ▶ 5:00 Young people say church is boring. Pastor Kincer says he said the same thing at 16, 17 and 18, because he didn’t get involved and was a clock watcher. David said, “I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.” Many Christians have lost that gladness and blame the church, but the church is made up of people.
📖 Scripture (NKJV) Psalm 122:1 — I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.”

items.t: Who was really crucified for you?
items.d: Christ was — not Paul, and not any church name, group or minister.
p: Christ was — not Paul, and not any church name, group or minister.

Corinth had four groups — “I am of Paul,” “of Apollos,” “of Cephas,” “of Christ.” Pastor Kincer says only the group focused on Christ is right, because only Christ can save — not a church name, group or minister.
Who was really crucified for you?

🎙 From the sermon “You’ve got four groups here and only one is right. Can you rationally, reasonably, logically tell me which group is right? Yeah, the Christ group.” ▶ 15:48 “He says, was Paul baptized or crucified for you? See, was the Pope crucified for Catholics? Can the Pope save Catholics? No.” ▶ 16:51 “They’re focused on Christ who can do something. Not their church name, not their church group, not some minister.” ▶ 17:29 “It is Christ and the Scriptures.” ▶ 17:41 “I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.” Pastor Kincer says there were four groups in Corinth, and only one was right: the Christ group. Is Christ divided? No; He is one with the Father and the Scriptures. Was Paul crucified for you? No church name, church group or minister can save anyone. It is Christ and the Scriptures.
Who was really crucified for you?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 1:12–13 — Now I say this, that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” or “I am of Apollos,” or “I am of Cephas,” or “I am of Christ.” Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

items.t: What if a nation turns back to God?
items.d: God says He will relent from the judgment He planned. Pastor Kincer adds that Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.
p: God says He will relent from the judgment He planned. Pastor Kincer adds that Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.
Jeremiah shows both sides: a nation that won’t obey is plucked up, but one that turns from its evil is spared. That is why, Pastor Kincer says, we need to get the Word out.
What if a nation turns back to God?

🎙 From the sermon “If they will not obey, I will utterly pluck them up and destroy that nation.” ▶ 21:54 “But, Jeremiah 18:8, if that nation I have pronounced destruction, turn from their evil ways, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” ▶ 22:19 “You see, if we get them to embrace Bible morality, it is also an umbrella of protection when God judges.” ▶ 22:54 Jeremiah 18:8 says, “If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” Pastor Kincer says God warns before He judges. If a nation turns from its evil ways and back to Bible morality, God can relent from the judgment He planned.
What if a nation turns back to God?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Jeremiah 18:8 — if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. Jeremiah 12:17 — But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation,” says the LORD.

items.t: Can a divided home still stand?
items.d: No. Jesus said a house divided against itself will not stand.
p: No. Jesus said a house divided against itself will not stand.

Pastor Kincer says husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go different ways, conflict follows and the kids can’t wait to get out.
Can a divided home still stand?

🎙 From the sermon “Jesus said these words. If they’re divided against themselves, they will not stand.” ▶ 12:16 “In the home, is it imperative that the husband and wife stand together with the same truth, the same moral standards? Is it important? And being an example to their children, not just telling their children about Jesus, but showing them in their life. Yes, it is. Why? Or the home isn’t going to stand.” ▶ 12:44 “Because the husband and wife go two different ways.” ▶ 13:13 Jesus said every kingdom, city and house divided against itself shall not stand (Matthew 12:25). Pastor Kincer says “stand” is a military word: an army that isn’t united loses the war. In the home, husband and wife must stand together with the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go two different ways, conflict comes, and the kids can’t wait to get out.
Can a divided home still stand?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 12:25 — But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.”

items.t: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?
items.d: God wants to rule our lives, not just bless them. Too many want heaven and His blessings without doing what He says.
p: God wants to rule our lives, not just bless them. Too many want heaven and His blessings without doing what He says.

Pastor Kincer says Israel rejected God and did what was right in their own eyes, and Jesus’ parable shows citizens refusing the king’s rule. People want God’s blessings and approval, he says, but God wants His Scriptures to rule their lives.
Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?

🎙 From the sermon “God said to Samuel, they have rejected me that I should not rule over them. They haven’t rejected you, Samuel. They rejected me.” ▶ 10:36 “See, the people didn’t want God telling them what to do. Is that America? Yeah, we want to go to heaven. You see, we want his blessings. We want him to prosper us, but we don’t want to do what he tells us to do.” ▶ 10:45 “People want God’s blessings and God’s approval. But God wants to rule in their life. He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life, and they don’t want it.” ▶ 11:23 They rejected God, rejected the Scriptures, and did what they wanted in their own eyes. People want to go to heaven and want His blessings, but do not want to do what He tells them to do. Luke 19:14 says, “We will not have this man to reign over us.” People want God’s blessings and approval, but God wants to rule in their life — and He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life.
Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Samuel 8:7 — And the LORD said to Samuel, “Heed the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them.” Luke 19:14 — But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We will not have this man to reign over us.’

items.d: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
p: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
Pastor Kincer says people hear “be perfect” and think it means never sinning. He points to Hebrews 5:14 and James 1:4 to show it is about growing up and being complete, lacking nothing.

🎙 From the sermon ““Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is Jesus talking.” ▶ 16:08 “And they thought perfect was just living a life that had no flaws in it. No, it’s coming to what? Spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness.” ▶ 16:24 “Let patience have her perfect work, that you may be what? Perfect and entire, lacking what? Nothing.” ▶ 16:50

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 5:48 — Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. James 1:4 — But let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing. Hebrews 5:14 — But solid food belongs to those who are of full age, that is, those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

items.t: What if my gifts are just noise?
items.d: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
p: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
Pastor Kincer explains Paul’s picture: a cymbal clanging by itself would drive you nuts in about 30 seconds. He says love is more important than both kinds of languages — men’s and angels’.
What if my gifts are just noise?

🎙 From the sermon “Though or if I speak with tongues of men and angels, but have not love, I am become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.” ▶ 0:23 “And if I had someone over there just clang the cymbals together, you know, in about 30 seconds, you would go, “You’re driving me nuts. What’s the point?”” ▶ 0:37 “There’s languages of men, like they spoke on the day of Pentecost. And there are languages of angels. But the key is love is more important than both of those.” ▶ 1:01
What if my gifts are just noise?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 13:1 — Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. 1 Corinthians 12:31 — But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.

items.t: Does real love insist on its own way?
items.d: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
tg: love does not demand its own way
p: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
Pastor Kincer walks through Paul’s description of love: patient, kind, not proud or rude. Love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, the church or the community, and it keeps no record of wrongs.
Does real love insist on its own way?

🎙 From the sermon “Love does not seek its own way. Well, it’s going to be my way. I’m going to hit the highway. You know, love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, in the church, or in the community. It demands the right way, the truth.” ▶ 6:47 “Love is not easily provoked. It, you know, they’re not touchy. You know, if you don’t say the right thing or do the right thing, they’re all ticked off. And love doesn’t do that.” ▶ 7:03
Does real love insist on its own way?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 13:4–5 — Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil.

items.t: Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?
items.d: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.
p: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.

Pastor Kincer points to Jesus’ warning about people who prophesied and cast out demons in His name, yet hear “I never knew you.” He says they were used by God but missed love, which he describes as obeying God.
Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?

🎙 From the sermon “See, love is to obey God. And he had the message, but he didn’t have the love.” ▶ 2:18 “See, they had faith to do all these things and these gifts and these spiritual manifestations were working in them. And Jesus said, “I will say to them, I never knew you.” Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.” ▶ 3:02 “You see, you didn’t have love. You might have been used of God to do things, but you missed the important thing, and that is love.” ▶ 3:14
Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 7:22–23 — Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’ 1 Corinthians 13:2 — And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

items.t: What is the real goal of God’s Word?
items.d: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
p: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
Pastor Kincer says “end” in this verse means goal. We tend to think the goal is eternal life or the gifts of the Spirit, he says, but it is love.
What is the real goal of God’s Word?

🎙 From the sermon “Now the end of the commandment is love out of a pure heart. The word end means the goal. You see the goal of the word of God is love out of a pure heart.” ▶ 23:10 “See, we think it’s eternal life. No, you’re going to live eternally no matter what.” ▶ 23:41 “We think that it’s the gifts of the spirit in our circles.” ▶ 24:04 “And it’s not. It’s love. And that’s why we have such phoniness in the spirit-filled world as we try to push something that God isn’t doing.” ▶ 24:14
What is the real goal of God’s Word?
📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Timothy 1:5 — Now the purpose of the commandment is love from a pure heart, from a good conscience, and from sincere faith.

items.t: Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?
items.d: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.
p: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.

Pastor Kincer notes that love is listed first among the fruit of the Spirit, that God is love, and that love sits at the top of sharing in the divine nature. His point: the fruit and character of God come before the manifestations.
Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?

🎙 From the sermon “Love, joy, peace. It’s the first fruit. 1 John 4:8 says, “God is love.” See, that is exactly what God is. He just gave us the description of God.” ▶ 8:29 “So the love is at the peak of divine character and it’s at the beginning of the fruits of the spirit. And believe me, Paul is telling us, you can’t have the manifestations of the spirit without the fruit and the divine character of God. That’s what he’s telling us. This is the way to get it.” ▶ 9:01
Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Galatians 5:22–23 — But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law. 1 John 4:8 — He who does not love does not know God, for God is love.
